ko-news-notices-1692-8372c75064.title: Understanding Ocean Dynamics through Q&A published and shared as a file
ko-news-notices-1692-8372c75064.text:
Understanding Ocean Dynamics through Q&A published and shared as a file
2023-10-12
[For the PDF version of this book (not for sale), please download the “attached file” at the bottom of the introduction. ]
GeoSR Co., Ltd. has published “Easy-to-understand Ocean Mechanics through Q&A” by Professor Seung Young-ho, Professor Emeritus of Oceanography at Inha University. According to the author's passion and writing intention to help younger students in the maritime field. It was published in a not-for-sale PDF version, and anyone interested in marine mechanics can download and study it. Through this book, I hope that the author's 30 years of lectures and experience in marine mechanics will serve as a good guide for everyone who wants to understand marine mechanics, and I am deeply grateful for the author's dedication.
I have been thinking for a long time about the proposition, “How can I easily explain the concept of complex marine phenomena?” and decided to include the results in this book. -From the author's preface-

ko-news-press-1440-c14319c1ac.title: Feeding and fish farm management using ICT... “The sea is the future” 6,000 people visited
ko-news-press-1440-c14319c1ac.text:
Feeding and fish farm management using ICT... “The sea is the future” 6,000 people visited
2022-03-25
[2017 Sea Farm Show―Marine Fisheries, Aquaculture, and Food Expo]
Marine environment observation-feeding system, etc... Visitors are amazed by the cutting-edge aquaculture technology
Popular for sampling seafood such as fish cake and steamed abalone
Sturgeon and soft-shelled turtles… Unique fish species also attract attention
“I usually enjoy seaweed snacks as a side dish for beer. I think it is a promising export product as well.” (Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Strategy and Finance Kim Dong-yeon)
“Seaweed is a ‘semiconductor of the fishing industry’ whose exports are expected to reach $500 million this year. There are many types of seaweed, such as stone seaweed and seaweed for sushi, and they taste good, so they are well-received in the global market.” (Seaweed Industry Association official)
Deputy Prime Minister Kim and Minister of Oceans and Fisheries Kim Young-chun, who visited the ‘2017 Sea Farm Show - Oceans, Fisheries, Aquaculture and Food Expo’ which opened at KINTEX in Goyang-si, Gyeonggi-do on the 17th, showed special interest in various farmed marine products and cutting-edge aquaculture technology. The eyes and ears of domestic and foreign guests and visitors were focused on Korea's smart fish farming industry, which is equipped with cutting-edge technology. This expo, held under the theme ‘The Ocean is the Future,’ was an opportunity to present a vision for the next generation of future food and examine the path forward for the Korean aquaculture industry.
○ Aquaculture technology and marine observation technology showcased
Government agencies such as the National Institute of Fisheries Science, which has led the development of domestic aquaculture technology, local governments, and aquaculture-related companies all participated in this expo.
GeoSR, which builds and operates a marine environment system, introduced technology that not only measures fishing grounds environments such as water temperature and salinity, but also observes marine environments such as green algae and weather. A GeoSR official explained, "Due to the recent high temperature phenomenon, damage to fish farms has increased more than tenfold over the past five years. Water temperature information is sent to a smartphone application once every 30 minutes, and devices installed in fish farms adjust the net height to prepare for damage."
The Future Aquaculture Investment Forum, which was formed last year with the goal of converging the aquaculture industry and cutting-edge technology, introduced various smart aquaculture technologies, such as an automatic feed supply system and an automated laver cultivation system, at the expo. The Future Aquaculture Investment Forum announced, “We will introduce a cutting-edge system and find optimal data using artificial intelligence (AI) from 2020.” Koo Bon-gon (49), a visitor to the exhibition hall, said, “Recently, I heard that there is a lot of interest in Korea’s smart aquaculture technology in Japan,” and added, “I think it will be a good opportunity to introduce cutting-edge aquaculture technology to Japan and other countries by linking up with companies with technology.”

ko-news-press-1436-c14319c1ac.title: Damage in Geoje from Nakdong River marine debris estimated at KRW 15 billion
ko-news-press-1436-c14319c1ac.text:
Damage in Geoje from Nakdong River marine debris estimated at KRW 15 billion
2022-03-25
It is attracting attention as the damage to the Geoje region due to marine debris flowing in due to the opening of the Nakdong River estuary dam floodgates is expected to exceed 15 billion won.
According to Geoje City on the 24th, at the mid-term service briefing session on the 'Nakdong River marine debris inflow route survey and countermeasures' held recently in a small conference room at City Hall, it was reported that damage to the local tourism and fisheries industries due to marine debris flowing in due to the opening of the Nakdong River estuary dam floodgates exceeds KRW 15 billion.
Our Sea of East Asia Network (OSEAN) and GeoSR Co., Ltd., which were in charge of the service on this day, announced that due to the opening of the flood gates of the Nakdong River estuary dam twice in July last year, about 8,000 tons of marine debris washed up on the northeastern coast of Geoje, resulting in enormous collection costs, and that not only damage to the fishing industry but also the number of tourists decreased significantly.
In 2011, when the floodgates were actually opened, only about 400,000 people visited Geoje Island's famous beaches such as Gujora and Wahyeon, a 60% decrease from the 960,000 people in 2010.
Therefore, when Geoje City is included in the Nakdong River watershed area, it can receive benefits such as purification projects by signing a cost-sharing agreement. However, as there are concerns about disadvantages such as development restrictions due to the application of the Water Quality Management Act, it was pointed out that it is necessary to review ways to receive support and other benefits without being included in the watershed area.
-Gyeongnam Domin Ilbo 2012.07.25
Geoje City Council member Park Jang-seop (independent, La constituency) said, “At this service report, the estimated amount of damage to the fisheries industry was announced at around 800 million won, but if we estimate the damage caused by sedimentation on the seabed, the damage to the fisheries sector alone is expected to be in the billions to tens of billions of won,” and urged an accurate damage investigation.
Meanwhile, Geoje City paid a service fee of 62 million won in May to provide a service for 'Nakdong River marine debris inflow route survey and response plan'. The city plans to receive a report on the results by the end of December and based on this, contact the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs and the Ministry of Environment to discuss damage response measures in various ways.

ko-news-press-1430-c14319c1ac.title: The East Coast's shrinking beaches — Solutions remain out of reach
ko-news-press-1430-c14319c1ac.text:
The East Coast's shrinking beaches — Solutions remain out of reach
2022-03-25
Coastal erosion is ‘severe’ in 6 out of 25 places… The biggest cause of artificial facility construction
Limitations in deriving solutions at the local government level… Government level support must be actively provided20110619002108
Coastal erosion on the east coast of Gyeongbuk has become increasingly serious, making it urgent to prepare countermeasures.
According to cities and counties such as Gyeongbuk Province, Pohang, and Gyeongju on the 19th, the province commissioned GeoSR and Ara Technology Co., Ltd. to monitor the coastal white sandy beaches in the east coast region for comprehensive erosion control. As a result, out of 25 surveyed areas, six places were grade D with severe erosion, and the erosion severity rate reached 24%. This is a significant increase compared to 22.7% in 2009 and 18.2% in 2008.
In the service survey, out of 25 regions, none were grade A (good), 8 were grade B (average), 11 were grade C (concern), and 6 were grade D (severe). There were 17 areas where erosion was at a concern or serious level, accounting for 68%.
The area of ​​Oryu Beach in Gampo-eup, Gyeongju-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do, where coastal erosion is serious and measures are needed.
Gyeongju = Reporter Jang Young-tae
Grade C and D areas where erosion is severe, with white sand beaches disappearing and sand soil being lost to the bottom of the road, include Jeonchon, Najeong, and Oryu in Gyeongju, Songdo in Pohang, Daetan in Yeongdeok, and Bongpyeong, Wolsongjeong, Deoksin, Geumeum, and Hujeong in Uljin.
White sand beaches are not only an important element of the coastal environment but also have an important function, such as serving as a natural septic tank. However, the preparation of countermeasures is sluggish compared to the seriousness of the issue.
In particular, Songdo Beach in Nam-gu, Pohang City had an average width of 70 to 80 meters of white sand, but now only a portion of it remains and has completely lost its function as a beach.
Samjeong Beach in Guryongpo, Nam-gu, Pohang, and the coast around Hajeong-ri also lost sand, turning the white sand into a gravel field. Concrete trivets were installed in the nearby sea to prevent the sand from being washed away by the sea, but it is not enough.
Experts say that the biggest causes of coastal erosion are changes in the direction of waves due to breakwater construction and the construction of artificial coastal structures such as hinterland development.
Therefore, it is pointed out that an integrated management strategy should be pursued, including proactive measures to prevent coastal erosion and crackdown on indiscriminate development activities.
This year, Gyeongbuk Province plans to spend 430 million won to carry out a coastal erosion monitoring project targeting 23 locations on the east coast of Gyeongbuk from last March to the end of this year to identify the erosion status and promote a scientific and eco-friendly coastal maintenance project.
In particular, precise monitoring will be conducted on two locations: the coast of Sadong 1-ri, Ulleung-gun, and the coast of Gusan-Wolsong-ri, Uljin-gun.
Rep. Jang Doo-wook of the Gyeongbuk Provincial Council said, “Coastal erosion should be viewed as a national problem as there are limits to perfect response at the local government level,” and added, “The province should actively appeal to the relevant ministries about the seriousness of east coast erosion and urge comprehensive support.”
Pohang = Reporter Jang Young-tae 3678jyt@segye.com

ko-news-press-1428-c14319c1ac.title: Eco-Friendly Green Growth Technology Cooperation Symposium
ko-news-press-1428-c14319c1ac.text:
Eco-Friendly Green Growth Technology Cooperation Symposium
2022-03-25
Eco-friendly green growth technology cooperation symposium held
Green growth technology experts from industry, academia (research), and government are gathered in one place...
Korea Coast Guard (Chief Lee Gil-beom) will hold a joint research symposium of "industry, academia (research), government" on September 25th at 3:00 PM in the conference room on the 2nd floor of Korea Coast Guard in order to actively respond to rapidly changing domestic and foreign marine environment changes and strengthen technological cooperation for eco-friendly green growth.
In this symposium, experts will gather together to present and discuss eight marine environment-related tasks, including ‘Analysis of alkylphenol distribution in sediments from marine dumping areas’ by Professor Kyeong-Hoon Shin of Hanyang University and ‘Study on the fate of oil and its impact on floating ecosystems using medium-sized closed ecosystems’ by Dr. Won-Jun Shim of the Korea Ocean Research Institute.
In particular, this symposium will focus on ways to minimize environmental damage in the event of a large-scale pollution accident by supporting scientific control technology that emerged after the Taean Hebei Sprit accident, such as the change process of oil spilled at sea and the cause of tar formation.
The "Industry-Academia-Research-Public" Joint Research Council was established in June 2004 by appointing maritime experts from Korea Ocean Research Institute, Inha University, and SK Energy, centered around the Korea Coast Guard, to enhance the expertise of coast guard work through establishing and activating an organic cooperation system between the public and private sectors, and to improve problems and discuss future development directions through mutual complementation.
This council additionally appointed the Korea Environmental Research Institute and GeoSR this year to expand and organize the participation of marine specialized organizations. A total of 10 institutions and organizations in 4 fields, including marine pollution control technology and biotoxicity, are participating and conducting joint research.
Korea Coast Guard promotes academic advice and information exchange through regular meetings of the Joint Research Council, and strengthens the organic technology exchange and cooperation system by mutually supplementing insufficient research areas such as joint use of research facilities. Meanwhile, it is pursuing certification as an internationally recognized testing research organization (ISO 17025) to receive international recognition for test research results, and is expected to greatly contribute to enhancing the expertise of “industry, academia (research), and government.”

ko-news-press-1427-c14319c1ac.title: [New growth engine company] GeoSR
ko-news-press-1427-c14319c1ac.text:
[New growth engine company] GeoSR
2022-03-25
GeoSR (CEO Kim Hong-seon, www.geosr.com), a company specializing in marine and water environment engineering services, is evaluated as having secured the highest level of technology in Korea through bold investments in cutting-edge equipment and continuous research and development.
GeoSR performs work areas such as marine physical survey, water quality and sediment analysis, surveying and exploration, coastal erosion monitoring system construction, and GIS and S/W development. In addition, we are expanding our business scope to include marine remote monitoring systems and remote management of route indications by training experts in the field. GeoSR, which has been carrying out various national research projects since its establishment in 2000, has recently been focusing on △direct and remote monitoring, △surveying and exploration, and △numerical model experiment projects.
The numerical model experiment project is a field that reproduces observation results and simulates future changes or past phenomena using computer programs that numerically analyze differential equations that express the movement, diffusion, and interaction of materials, including water flow in oceans, rivers, and lakes. GeoSR has hundreds of domestic and international applications, including a variety of cutting-edge programs that can simulate tides, flows, waves, material movement and diffusion, topography, and ecosystem changes in marine and water environments. In addition, we have a unique technology that can reduce coastal disasters by building surge data for each typhoon invasion scenario and quickly forecasting coastal flooding.
A GeoSR official explained, “Not only have green growth and natural disaster reduction become hot topics recently, but as the new and renewable energy industry that can replace fossil fuels has emerged, the technology to accurately simulate various phenomena occurring in the marine and water environment is becoming more important.” GeoSR is expected to maintain its unrivaled status in the field of numerical model experiments based on its differentiated competitiveness in identifying phenomena and establishing alternatives through a multidisciplinary approach to numerous research and field tasks. CEO Kim Hong-seon said, “As a leading company in the field of marine research and technology services, we will strive to contribute to the development of Korea’s marine science and technology and to have our technology recognized globally.”

ko-news-press-1424-c14319c1ac.title: The white sand beach will disappear like this.
ko-news-press-1424-c14319c1ac.text:
The white sand beach will disappear like this.
2022-03-25
[Hankyoreh] It was found that erosion is progressing at a worrying level on nearly half of the white sand beaches and dunes across the country. This is a phenomenon that is particularly serious on the east coast due to the combination of typhoon damage and reckless development of the seaside, such as the construction of coastal roads and embankments and aggregate extraction.
According to a research report commissioned by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries to GeoSR on the 16th, which surveyed and graded the erosion history of 62 beaches and sand dunes across the country last year, 21 places were at the ‘concern’ level and 6 were ‘severe’, with 44% of the total showing above-average erosion.
Among the beaches rated ‘Concern’ include Gwangalli and Haeundae in Busan, Gyeongpodae and Jeongdongjinri in Gangwon-do, and Kkotji Beach in Anmyeon-eup, Chungcheongnam-do.
On the Jeongdongjin coast, the slope of the white sand beach is becoming steeper after the coastal road was expanded and the river was maintained, and at Kkotji Beach, after the white sand beach hinterland, which used to be a sand dune, was developed and a concrete retaining wall was built, 3.4km of the coast was eroded and the sand beach became gravel.
The coast of Namhangjin-ri, Seongdeok-dong, Gangneung-si, Gangwon-do, which was judged to be 'severe' and required urgent measures, is experiencing erosion along the 1.85 km long coast, including the collapse of the coastal iron fence of the military base after the construction of a breakwater. At Hosan Beach in Wondeok-eup, Samcheok-si, 1.3 km of the coast is being shaved off as the balance of soil supply is broken due to aggregate extraction and construction of Hosan Port.
In addition, Unyeo Beach in Gonam-myeon, Taean-gun, South Chungcheong Province, is at risk of collapsing the newly built revetment due to serious erosion after large-scale silica sand extraction and revetment construction.
Coastal erosion on the east coast is particularly severe, and out of 16 survey points in Gangwon-do, 8 were judged to be ‘concern’ and 4 were judged ‘severe’. In Gyeongbuk, among the six coastal areas, four, including Songdo Beach in Pohang, were considered ‘concern’, and the coast in Bongpyeong-ri, Jukbyeon-myeon, showed a ‘serious’ level of erosion.
Kim Moo-hong, an official in the coastal planning division of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, said, “Coastal erosion is mainly caused by artificial factors such as coastal reclamation or the construction of roads or seawalls without examining the comprehensive impact,” and added, “We are establishing a long-term monitoring system to identify the exact cause of erosion.”
Hongseop Cho, environmental reporter ecothink@hani.co.kr

ko-news-press-1419-c14319c1ac.title: Beach water quality inspection varies depending on the survey method.
ko-news-press-1419-c14319c1ac.text:
Beach water quality inspection varies depending on the survey method.
2022-03-25
Beach water quality inspection survey points vary depending on the method Reporter Park Jeong-hwan
hi21@
Beach water quality results vary depending on the survey location and sampling method, reducing reliability.
Accordingly, it is pointed out that clear guidelines should be established regarding the points and investigation methods of beach water quality testing.
Representative Kim Young-joo of the National Assembly's Environment and Labor Committee announced on the 3rd the results of a water quality test at Eulwang-ri Beach, Yongyu Island, Jung-gu, Incheon, conducted on the 5th and 6th of last month at the request of the National Institute of Marine and Fisheries Science.
As a result of the test, a total of 9,200 to 2,400 E. coli bacteria were detected per 100 ml of seawater collected from three Eurwangri beaches, which exceeded the standard for sewage treatment plant effluent (3,000 bacteria per 100 ml) by more than three times.
Fecal Escherichia coli, which occurs in feces and sewage, was also found at 2,400 to 1,100 per 100 ml of seawater.
Rep. Kim said, “Eulwangri Beach is so polluted with E. coli that swimming at the beach should be banned.”
At about the same time, the water quality test results of Eulwang-ri Beach, investigated by the Incheon City Health and Environment Research Institute, were completely different.
The water quality at Eurwangri Beach, where samples were collected on the 13th of last month, had a total E. coli count of 20 per 100 ml.
This was a ‘suitable’ beach water quality, and was completely different from the water quality results that Rep. Kim had commissioned from the National Institute of Marine and Fisheries Research.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries determines that a beach is ‘suitable’ for swimming if the total number of E. coli in the water quality is less than 1,000 per 100 ml of seawater.
Even though it is the same beach, the water quality results are completely different because the sample collection methods are different.
An employee of the Jung-gu Tourism Promotion Department, who collected samples from Rep. Kim's National Institute of Marine Fisheries Science and the city's Institute of Health and Environment's water quality tests, said the two organizations' sample collection methods were different.
The survey by the National Institute of Marine and Fisheries Science, commissioned by Rep. Kim, is the result of collecting samples from a point about 30 meters away from the beach when the sea water was low due to low tide, even during the same rainy season. This is a sample collected when household sewage washed by rainwater on land flows into the sea and causes E. coli bacteria to flourish.
When the city's Public Health and Environment Research Institute collected samples through Jung-gu, it was about 100 meters away from the beach during high tide. As domestic sewage such as excrement and sewage was diluted with seawater, the quality of the water, including malignant bacteria such as E. coli, was inevitably reduced.
The problem is that the sample collection method for beach water quality testing is not clear.
In the case of beach water quality investigation points, the water depth is defined as 0.5 to 1.5 m (within 15 cm of the surface), and no specific method has been established.
Accordingly, in the East and South Seas, where the difference between high and low tides is not severe, and the West Sea, where there is a large difference in tides, the range of variation in water quality is bound to be quite large even if samples are collected under the same conditions.
Mr. K (45), a merchant at Eulwang-ri Beach, said, “The city’s beach water quality survey showed that there were ‘no problems,’ so people flocked to the beach for vacation, but with the announcement of the survey results by the National Institute of Marine and Fisheries Research, the number of vacationers has suddenly decreased. As someone who runs a business near the beach, I am embarrassed.” /Reporter Park Jeong-hwan blog.itimes.co.kr /hi21

ko-news-press-1417-c14319c1ac.title: GeoSR — Global environmental conservation and marine survey expertise
ko-news-press-1417-c14319c1ac.text:
GeoSR — Global environmental conservation and marine survey expertise
2022-03-25
[Growth companies in the spotlight] GeoSR — Global environmental conservation and marine survey expertise (2004-05-27)
As global warming pollution water contamination and declining fisheries resources threaten the environment in various ways an engineering services company working in fisheries and aquaculture is attracting attention for its contribution to environmental conservation and development.
GeoSR Co Ltd (CEO Hong-seon Kim www.GeoSR.com) conducts engineering research services related to the global environment and fisheries and aquaculture. Its staff include many specialists with doctoral and master's degrees. Around 40 employees graduated in related fields and divide their work through in-depth research and analysis in their respective specialties.
The company also undertakes marine and aquatic environment surveys numerical modeling water quality analysis marine structure design domestic and overseas marine projects coastal development environmental software development and the construction of monitoring systems.
GeoSR is recognized for world-class expertise in three-dimensional numerical modeling of marine water quality.
Last year the company worked with the Marine Environment Research Center on a survey and research project for Saemangeum marine environmental conservation measures and successfully led the prediction of marine water quality inside and outside the seawall.
Since last year it has also been working with Daeyoung Engineering to establish a coastal erosion monitoring system. It successfully installed economical video camera systems capable of continuous observation at Haeundae and Daecheon beaches.
The video-based wave observation method developed in this project with Professor Tae-rim Kim of Kunsan National University is attracting attention as a world first.
The company has also invested actively in expensive advanced observation equipment. It is the only domestic company to own an acoustic Doppler current profiler (ADCP) as well as ADCP bottom moorings acoustic underwater releases and related equipment.
A company representative said that GeoSR recorded sales of approximately KRW 2.5 billion last year expects sales growth of more than 100% this year and spends approximately 12% of annual sales on research and development.

ko-news-press-1415-c14319c1ac.title: Acceleration of coastal erosion at 178 white sand beaches nationwide
ko-news-press-1415-c14319c1ac.text:
Acceleration of coastal erosion at 178 white sand beaches nationwide
2022-03-25
Acceleration of coastal erosion at 178 white sand beaches nationwide
Impact of ports, road construction, etc. Loss of sand and gravelization in progress
GeoSR Dr. Suyong Nam’s team
It was found that the coasts of more than 178 white sand beaches across the country are being eroded.
At the ‘Symposium for Efficient Use and Conservation of the Coast’ held in Gangneung on the 7th, Dr. Nam Su-yong’s team from GeoSR made this statement and emphasized the urgent need to prepare effective measures.
According to Dr. Nam, the 178 locations where coastal erosion is currently occurring include 92 locations with soil envelopment, 36 locations with revetment collapse, 35 locations with white sand beach erosion, and 15 locations with sand dune envelopment.
The reasons for coastal erosion were the installation of coastal structures such as ports on the east coast, the decrease in soil supply and invasion from typhoons on the south coast, and the installation of coastal roads and storms on the west coast.
By region, Samcheok's Hosan Beach has been graveling due to sand loss since 2001 due to large-scale sand extraction, and Busan's Haeundae is experiencing continuous coastal erosion due to the revetment road and hinterland development built in the late 1960s.
In addition, Songdo in Busan, Songdo in Pohang, and Gyeongsangnam-do have either completely lost their function as beaches or are in danger, and many gravels have been exposed after the installation of breakwaters in Mallipo, Chungcheongnam-do.
Reporter Kim Won-hak (environment@bosa.co.kr)

ko-news-notices-469-8372c75064.title: GeoSR provides an example and hope for corporate international coastal cleanup.
ko-news-notices-469-8372c75064.text:
GeoSR provides an example and hope for corporate international coastal cleanup.
2022-03-02
GeoSR and the Marine Fisheries Corporation's International Coastal Cleanup, which provided an example and hope for corporate International Coastal Cleanup (ICC)
September 17, 2018
Jongsoo Lee, Researcher at East Asia Marine Community Ocean Co., Ltd.
leesavannah@hanmail.net
An international coastal cleanup with GeoSR and Marine Fisheries Enterprise Association employees was conducted on Oido Beach in Siheung on September 7. GeoSR is a marine research and research company established in 2000 and has specialized personnel and equipment in fields such as marine physical survey, numerical modeling, water quality and sediment analysis, surveying and exploration, geographic information system and software development. Since 2014, we have joined Ocean of East Asia as a sponsoring company and have been helping Ocean's activities. Last year, we participated in the International Coastal Cleanup of the Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries, but this year, for the first time, we conducted activities independently as a company, and Ocean provided support for the specific details of the activities. The Marine Fisheries Enterprise Association also attended this event, and a total of 25 people carried out cleanup activities for about an hour on a 500m beach.
Oido Beach in Siheung is a place where trash is regularly collected through public works, and even on the day of the activity, a significant amount of trash was placed in bags and loaded on the beach embankment. The meaning of simple international coastal cleanup and the results of the 10 years of activities carried out in Korea were explained, and the cleanup activity was immediately carried out. When I first arrived at the beach, I was a little concerned because there seemed to be no trash, but to put my concerns to naught, a lot of large trash, such as discarded refrigerators, plywood, and processed wood, was collected, as well as a lot of relatively small trash less than 30cm. People who participated in the activity worked together to collect heavy trash such as discarded refrigerators, plywood, and nets from every corner, and collected them with great enthusiasm from one end of the 500m long beach to the other.
While picking up trash together, people asked a lot of questions about the marine trash problem, and Kim Hong-seon, CEO of GeoSR, asked how international coastal cleanup can be applied as a daily activity. In response to this question, I explained that coastal cleanup can also be carried out in city parks, and I was surprised that many people showed such specific interest. Throughout the activity, I had the deep impression that I was witnessing an exemplary international coastal cleanup by a private company, albeit on a relatively small scale.
According to Kim Moon-jin, Secretary General of the Siheung Environmental Movement Federation, who participated and supported the goods and activities, large waste is collected through public works and a lot of small waste is left behind. Perhaps that is why many pieces of glass, tiles, and rope were found, as well as many pieces of Styrofoam. Judging by the fact that there is no permit in the immediate vicinity of the beach embankment, it appears that trash from nearby commercial and residential areas washed up on the beach. The total amount of trash collected in about an hour was 149.4 kg. In this international coastal cleanup activity, a large amount of trash was collected in a short period of time, and thanks to the hard work of those who participated, I believe it was an activity that could be considered an exemplary case both quantitatively and qualitatively. I hope that these activities will take place not only in private companies but also in schools and public institutions, so that Korea's international coastal cleanup will grow significantly in terms of content and scale.
[Source]International Coastal Cleanup by GeoSR and the Marine Fisheries Corporation Association, which provided an example and hope for the corporate International Coastal Cleanup (ICC) (East Asia Marine Community Ocean)|Author leesavannah

2018-11-13 11:17
Announcement of 565 ‘small and medium-sized companies that are great places to work’… Selected as 8 themes including CEO vision and work-life balance
(Seoul = Yonhap News) Reporter Bae Young-kyung = The Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry announced on the 13th that it had selected 565 ‘small and medium-sized companies that are good places to work’.
On this day, the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry selected small and medium-sized businesses that are good to work for under eight themes, including ▲ CEO (CEO) vision and philosophy, ▲ growth potential, ▲ employee recommendation rate, ▲ executive capabilities, ▲ work-life balance, ▲ company culture, ▲ promotion opportunities and possibilities, and ▲ welfare and salary.
In particular, the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry explained that this year, qualitative evaluation was conducted in parallel by introducing new criteria such as CEO vision and philosophy, employee recommendation rate, and executive competency.
In terms of work-life balance, Gabia Co., Ltd. was selected as a small and medium-sized business with a good place to work.
This company received positive reviews for creating a flexible working environment by applying a staggered work schedule and nickname system, providing breakfast, dinner, and snacks, and operating an in-house library (g-hye's forest).
In addition, Sunin Co., Ltd. was selected as a good small business to work for in the growth potential theme category in recognition of attracting 34 billion won in investment from Goldman Sachs last year.
By region, 314 companies in Seoul, 137 in Gyeonggi-do, 18 in Daejeon, 15 in Chungcheongbuk-do, and 13 in Incheon were selected.
By industry, there are 181 manufacturing/chemical companies, 182 IT/web/communication companies, 67 distribution/trade/transportation companies, and 47 media/design companies.
The Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry announced that it plans to designate 'Company Visit Day', a small business visit program, at the end of the year together with 73 chambers of commerce nationwide to provide young job seekers with the opportunity to visit excellent small and medium-sized businesses of their choice and experience the actual working environment.
A full list of good companies to work for can be found on the ‘Good Small Business Site to Work for’ (http://goodcompany.korcham.net).

ko-news-notices-458-8372c75064.title: The flow of the four major rivers slows, sediment builds up and oxygen depletes.
ko-news-notices-458-8372c75064.text:
The flow of the four major rivers slows, sediment builds up and oxygen depletes.
2022-03-02
【Sejong = Newsis】Reporter Lee In-jun = A research report has been published showing that due to the influence of weirs built on the four major rivers, including the Han River and Nakdong River, the flow of river water slows down and sediment accumulates on the river bed, creating a lack of oxygen in the water.
This assessment was made according to the research project report 'Investigation and Evaluation of Sediment Dissolution from Four Major River Weirs - Focusing on 14 Weirs' conducted last year with the participation of Hanyang University, Sejong University, Ewha Womans University, and GeoSR at the request of the National Institute of Environmental Research.
If phytoplankton proliferates in the water and the dead phytoplankton later accumulate on the river bottom, the oxygen consumption rate may increase. This phenomenon is more severe in Korea's freshwater environment because the water depth is shallow.
The research team analyzed the 'Sediment Oxygen Demand (SOD)', which indicates how much oxygen is consumed in the process of decay of organic matter in sediment, in 14 of the 16 weirs in the Four Major Rivers from May of last year to March of this year, excluding the Sangju Weir and the Changnyeong Haman Weir, and found that the Four Major Rivers are actually experiencing oxygen depletion.
As of August, the daily oxygen demand of sediment in an area of 1 m² at the Yeoju Weir of the Han River was 0.47 g, while the Gongju Weir of the Geum River required 2.7 times more oxygen at 1.74 g.
The sediment oxygen consumption rate, measured from September to October at a point where the flow rate is expected to slow due to topography, was the lowest at 0.76 g at the Ipo Weir of the Han River and 1.8 times higher at 2.13 g at the Yeoju Weir of the Han River.
If the oxygen consumption rate is high, it becomes difficult for aquatic life such as fish to survive, and the water quality deteriorates due to the lack of oxygen required for purification through decomposition of organic matter.
Deteriorating water quality causes phytoplankton to multiply, repeating the vicious cycle.
The report said, “Residence time and flow rate affect the organic matter content of the sediment, which can cause an increase or decrease in the oxygen consumption rate,” and “It is believed that if the discharge amount is low, the amount of organic matter flowing into the sediment increases, increasing the amount of oxygen consumed by the sediment.”
This year, the National Institute of Environmental Research plans to expand its investigation into the sediments of the four major rivers by conducting an investigation into the period when dissolved oxygen in bottom water decreases before the spring and summer rainy seasons and accumulating data from summer to fall, spring, and summer.

ko-news-notices-436-8372c75064.title: (Project carried out by our company) Completed installation of equipment to build a ‘sea water flow observation system’ at Ulsan Port
ko-news-notices-436-8372c75064.text:
(Project carried out by our company) Completed installation of equipment to build a ‘sea water flow observation system’ at Ulsan Port
2022-03-02
Reporter Go Eun-hee = Ulsan Port Authority (UPA, CEO Lee Chae-ik) announced on the 9th that it completed the installation of equipment to build the 'Seawater Flow Observation System' at Ulsan Port over a three-day period from August 4th to 6th.
For the 'Sea Flow Observation System', UPA invested a budget of approximately 300 million won, and in collaboration with the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency, one type of meteorological observation, two types of real-time ocean observation, and one type of seafloor moored ocean observation equipment were installed at two points in the front sea area of ​​Ulsan New Port in Yongyeon-dong, Nam-gu and one point in the front sea area of ​​the southern breakwater in Onsan-eup, Ulju-gun.
After testing this week's observation data, UPA will provide port users with real-time information on sea water flow and weather conditions in Ulsan Port, along with sea level information from the currently operating Ulsan Tide Observatory, through the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency website starting next week.
In particular, we plan to accumulate data through long-term seawater flow observations in sea areas where abnormal currents occur, analyze the causes of abnormal currents through spatiotemporal analysis and numerical modeling, and use them as data for safe operation of ships.
UPA President Lee Chae-ik said, “With the establishment of this system, we expect to secure the safety of ships entering and leaving Ulsan Port,” and added, “We will continue to do our best to create a safe Ulsan Port.”

ko-news-notices-431-8372c75064.title: Renewable marine tidal energy information at a glance
ko-news-notices-431-8372c75064.text:
Renewable marine tidal energy information at a glance
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency has created a renewable tidal energy resource map that provides information on tidal energy in the West and South Seas at a glance.
Tidal energy is an eco-friendly energy source obtained by installing water wheels in areas with strong currents, and has been confirmed to have high development potential in the West and South Sea coasts where tidal phenomena are dominant.
This tidal energy resource map was completed by analyzing long-term seawater flow data observed at 337 locations from Baengnyeong Island to Ulsan over the past 25 years.
The sea area with the highest energy density on the coast of Korea is near Uldolmok, Jeollanam-do, where the tidal power plant was completed on May 14 (27.8 MWh/㎡), followed by the Gyodong Waterway at the Han River Estuary in Gyeonggi Bay (16.1 MWh/㎡).
In addition, Maenggol Waterway (15.1 MWh/㎡), Geocha Waterway (9.3 MWh/㎡) and Jangjuk Waterway (8.8 MWh/㎡) in Jeollanam-do and Daebang Waterway (7.2 MWh/㎡) in Gyeongsangnam-do were analyzed to have high energy amounts.
This study, which was attempted for the first time in Korea based on observational data, is expected to be used in the development of green energy, and at the same time, it is expected to help in field testing and installation of power generation facilities required by marine renewable energy-related companies and research institutes and in selecting suitable sites for installation.
Meanwhile, we plan to continuously provide updated information using ocean observation data conducted every year through the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency website (www.nori.go.kr).

ko-news-notices-429-8372c75064.title: Establishment of national river master plan in addition to the four major rivers
ko-news-notices-429-8372c75064.text:
Establishment of national river master plan in addition to the four major rivers
2022-03-02
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs (Minister Jeong Jong-hwan) announced that it will begin work on “Establishing a master plan for national rivers other than the four major rivers” from July 23 to recreate them as spaces safe from floods and rich in water, culture, and ecology.
In addition to the four major rivers, this service is intended to prepare a comprehensive action plan to revive the major functions of rivers, such as water management, water flow, environment, and culture, as in the "Four Major Rivers Restoration" program, rather than the fragmentary river maintenance of the seven major river systems, including Anseongcheon, Sapgyocheon, Mangyeong River, Dongjin River, Tamjin River, Taehwa River, and Hyeongsan River, which are closely related to the lives of local residents and regional development.
* There are a total of 61 national rivers (3,002km), of which 18 (1,973km) are included in the "Four Major Rivers Restoration Project". In this service, plans are being established for the remaining 43 national rivers (1,029km). Upon commencing the service, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport will consult with related ministries such as the Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, and Forestry, and the Ministry of Culture, and relevant local governments to improve water quality in connection with river maintenance. We plan to jointly establish various regional development plans such as culture, tourism, and leisure. In particular, the Mangyeong River and Dongjin River are planned to be directly linked to the Saemangeum Master Plan currently being established by the government to lay the foundation for the successful implementation of the Saemangeum project, such as improving water quality in Saemangeum and creating an ecological belt.
In addition, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport is preparing a maintenance plan for small local rivers flowing into it in connection with the establishment of a plan for national rivers, and announced that a comprehensive maintenance plan for all rivers across the country will be prepared in December '10, when the establishment of this master plan is completed.

This observation was conducted for 30 days (April 14-May 13) by installing cutting-edge marine observation equipment (RCM-9) on a buoy to determine the movement of seawater. As a result, it was analyzed that the seawater flow was in the north-south direction with a maximum speed of 2.6 knots.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, "The data collected this time can be used as basic data to analyze the before and after changes in the surrounding environment due to the construction of the Gyeongin Haeway Waterway and the passage of ships," and added, "We plan to conduct periodic observations to provide accurate data in the future."
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency plans to disclose the results of this project through its website (www.nori.go.kr).

ko-news-notices-427-8372c75064.title: Work to the end with a happy heart
ko-news-notices-427-8372c75064.text:
Work to the end with a happy heart
2022-03-02
We all face personal challenges. Some people are physically sick and many things are mentally tiring. Also, when the social and economic situation is bad, the stress gradually increases. If we do not respond resolutely to this stress, we will react more harshly than necessary and waste our precious mental energy. Yuji Ikegaya said in the book “The Illusory Brain” that “It is important to know how to relieve stress, but you also need to have the mindset to accept stress confidently and believe that you can relieve it at any time.” We have something to do and a purpose, even in the face of personal difficulties and stress. This is truly difficult. However, in times like these, we need the persistence to push forward until we gain a foothold. Anselm Green said in his book “Flow, Don’t Stay”:
Stick with whatever you do until you take root in a place of your own choosing. I really want to see your growth. When faced with a difficult task, it may be difficult and difficult, but it is important to do your best until you establish the foundation for the work. Once things get established, things will go smoothly. After that, the results from your work will be very significant. It is important to have confidence that you can confidently accept and relieve the stress you face in the process of carrying out difficult and difficult tasks until you have established a foundation. They say we only have one life, and we need to do our best at every moment. In addition, it is an obvious but precious truth that we can survive by helping and helping each other with our family and friends. From now on, it is necessary to give joy, receive joy, and live happily during difficult times for myself and those who love me.
Source: Hyundai Economic Research Institute 09.07.24
