ko-news-notices-419-8372c75064.title: “If you build a dam, water quality will worsen” Four major rivers project faces ‘backflow’
ko-news-notices-419-8372c75064.text:
“If you build a dam, water quality will worsen” Four major rivers project faces ‘backflow’
2022-03-02
An unexpected obstacle emerged in the Four Major Rivers Maintenance Project: water quality problems. The government's official position is that if the four major rivers are dug deeper and dams are built, the water volume will increase and this will lead to improved water quality, but analysis has been raised within the government that "this may not be the case."
According to the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs and the Ministry of Environment on the 21st, the government is known to be pursuing a plan to build a total of 10 weirs under 15m in height in the four major rivers, including 2 to 3 dams in the Han River and 5 to 6 dams in the Nakdong River, in order to secure the water volume of the four major rivers.
The question is what effect the dam will have on water quality. Regarding this, there has been a strong conflict between those who say it will "improve" (the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport) and those who say it will "get worse" (environmental groups, etc.), but the Ministry of Environment, which is in charge of water quality management, has not expressed its position so far.
However, at an internal meeting of the Ministry of Environment ('meeting on measures to restore health of the four major rivers') held on the 15th under the chairmanship of Minister Lee Man, the National Institute of Environmental Research under the Ministry of Environment reported the results of an analysis that "If 10 weirs are built in the four major rivers, water quality will worsen."
This simulation analysis by the Korea Institute of Environmental Research was conducted after receiving some data, including a water quality prediction model, from the Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology, which is conducting research on establishing a master plan (basic plan) for the Four Major Rivers Maintenance Project at the request of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
As a result of the analysis, government sources reported that the installation of a weir had the positive effect of lowering the level of pollution by diluting the pollutants through the abundant water, but the negative effect of increasing the level of pollution by blocking the flow of water was greater.
Specifically, among the water quality items, the concentration of total phosphorus (TP) drops to some extent due to phenomena such as blocking weirs and sinking to the river bottom, but chlorophyll-a and biological oxygen demand (BOD), which cause green algae due to algae growth, "showed an overall tendency to increase," multiple government sources reported.
For example, in the case of Paldang Lake on the Han River, the annual biological oxygen demand (BOD) in 2007 and 2008 was 1.2PPM and 1.3PPM, respectively, but even if the maintenance project is completed by installing dams in the four major rivers, the water quality will remain stagnant or worsen.
A government official said, "This means that even if we spend 14 trillion won to complete the maintenance of the four major rivers by 2012 and then invest trillions of won again to implement water quality improvement measures, the water quality will not improve."
In this case, the government's long-term plan for water quality management will be shaken to its core. For this reason, some in the government are even concerned that “the Four Major Rivers Project is following in the footsteps of Sihwa Lake and Saemangeum.”
In Sihwa Lake, water pollution rapidly rose to an unexpected level during the process of desalinating the water after the completion of the seawall, causing the water to rot, leading to the decision to open the seawall sluice gate to distribute seawater. Saemangeum Island also became embroiled in a strong controversy for and against the pros and cons after an analysis by the Ministry of Environment found that the water quality of the freshwater lake was difficult to use as agricultural water (grade 4). There is concern that the Four Major Rivers Maintenance Project may also be affected by 'water quality reefs'.
Of course, this analysis is still a preliminary conclusion and may change in the future. Yoon Seung-jun, director of the Ministry of Environment's Water Environment Policy Bureau, said, "This is a prediction made while the master plan has not yet been finalized, so we cannot conclude that building a dam will worsen water quality."
Jae Hae-chi, head of the public relations team at the Four Major Rivers Planning Headquarters of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, also said, "There has been no confirmation at all about how much and at what height weirs will be built on the four major rivers." In relation to this, there is a possibility that water quality issues due to the construction of the Four Major Rivers weirs will be raised at the 'Four Major Rivers Restoration Report Conference' to be held on the 27th, presided over by President Lee Myung-bak, and some are pointing out that how this is resolved could be a 'watershed' for the Four Major Rivers Project.

ko-news-notices-418-8372c75064.title: Jeju naval base construction 'difficult'...conflict still exists
ko-news-notices-418-8372c75064.text:
Jeju naval base construction 'difficult'...conflict still exists
2022-03-02
(Jeju = Yonhap News) Reporter Kim Seung-beom = Next month marks two years since Jeju Island decided to accept the government's Jeju Naval Base construction plan, which has caused sharp controversy among residents, but the conflict surrounding it shows no signs of abating.
Residents of Gangjeong Village in Seogwipo-si and civil society groups who oppose the naval base filed a cancellation lawsuit with the Seoul Administrative Court on the 20th, saying, "The Minister of National Defense's approval of the naval base project implementation plan last January violated the Environmental Impact Assessment Act." Then, on the 21st, they held a rally in front of the Jeju Provincial Office and announced their will to fight to the death.
On the other hand, the Navy Headquarters, the project implementer, plans to proceed according to the original schedule, which aims to start construction in December of this year, including proceeding with the land compensation plan and publicizing the draft environmental impact assessment report.
The Jeju naval base construction project, which is contested by those in favor of saying that it is a national project and helpful in revitalizing the local economy, and those opposing it saying it will tarnish Jeju's image as an island of peace and harm its clean ecosystem, has been discussed several times since 2001 and became official in April 2007 when the Minister of National Defense visited Jeju Island and conveyed the government's position.
Jeju Provincial Government Kim Tae-hwan, who had pondered over a solution to the 'Naval Base', which emerged as an issue during the 2006 local elections, decided to make a policy decision by comprehensively judging 'provincial consensus', 'conformity to the image of an island of peace', and 'contribution to the local economy' as prerequisites for the construction of the naval base as soon as his term began in July of the same year.
In May of the following year, Governor Kim agreed with the government's policy to build a naval base, saying, "As a result of the analysis of the Naval Base Task Force (TF) composed of civil and private officials, it was found that the naval base and the Island of Peace are compatible, and that the construction of the naval base has a large ripple effect on the local economy."
He also said, "When the Jeju Local Government Association commissioned Gallup Korea to ask 1,500 residents of the province whether to host a naval base, 54.3% were in favor, 16.1 percentage points more than against (38.2%). In a survey of 1,000 residents each from the three towns and villages mentioned as candidates, Daecheon-dong, where Gangjeong Village is located, was in favor with 56%, and Andeok-myeon's “It was selected as the top priority destination ahead of 42.2%,” he announced.
However, those who oppose the naval base, including some residents of Gangjeong Village, civil society groups, and religious circles, raised the issue of the representativeness of the residents in the sample of 1,500 people and objectivity in the public opinion poll process, saying, "Is there no way to confirm the opinions of the residents of the province other than a telephone poll while the provincial authorities are deciding on a policy for the naval base, which has been controversial for as long as 15 years?"
The Jeju Provincial Council's Military Base Special Committee also conducted an administrative investigation regarding the public opinion poll, pointing out the lack of survey items, ambiguity in weight assignment, and damage to neutrality due to the Navy's holding briefing sessions for each village in Daecheon-dong, Seogwipo-si.
Around this time, local Democratic Labor Party lawmaker Hyun Ae-ja staged a 27-day hunger strike and complained about the unfairness of the policy decision, while the Catholic Diocese of Jeju Priests formed the 'Peace Island Special Committee' to publicize the unfairness of hosting a military base, leading to opposition movements from all walks of life.
As the opposition to the construction of the naval base grew stronger, the government and political circles turned to considering the construction of a complex port with the functions of a ‘tourist port’ and a ‘cruise port’ at the naval base.
The Korea Development Institute (KDI), which was in charge of the service, said, "In the case of installing a very large cruise ship berthing facility on the previously planned naval base breakwater, building a new access road, and additionally installing a tourist ship park with a cruise terminal and an outdoor park in the Gangjeong Port area, the benefit-to-cost ratio was found to be 1.4, exceeding the standard (1.0)," and judged that it was "economically feasible."
Based on this, the Prime Minister's Office announced a plan to develop a 'world-class civil-military complex tourist port on the coast of Gangjeong Village, Seogwipo-si, Jeju Island' through a national policy coordination meeting in September last year and revised the nature of the naval base to 'civilian-military complex'.
The currently confirmed development plan is for the Navy to invest KRW 953.7 billion by 2014 to build a 1,950-meter pier in the Gangjeong Village area of ​​480,000 m2 (200,000 m2 of public water reclamation) that can accommodate 20 ships and two 150,000-ton cruise ships at the same time, and to provide auxiliary facilities where 7,500 military personnel and their families can reside.
In addition, the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs plans to spend 53.4 billion won to build cruise ship mooring facilities and terminals, as well as Hamsang Park, and provide separate support in consultation with Jeju Island in accordance with the 'Regional Comprehensive Development Plan' that will be finalized in May.
Since then, the Ministry of National Defense has carried out preliminary environmental consultations with the Ministry of Environment for the construction of a civil-military complex tourist port, secured the 2009 budget (KRW 37.5 billion), and promoted port construction bidding. In January of last year, it approved the implementation plan for the national defense and military facility project (Jeju Naval Base) with the Chief of Naval Staff as the business operator.
The government asserts the necessity of constructing the Jeju Naval Base, saying, "In order to protect the national defense and southern maritime routes, and for Jeju Island to prosper as a base for international exchange and cooperation and as a free international city, securing self-defense means to protect peace from external threats must be prerequisite."
However, the opposing side is fighting back, saying, "If a naval base is built, it could become a base or target for military conflict in case of emergency, and there is a risk that the image of the 'island of peace' and an international resort and tourist destination will be damaged."
In particular, they are strongly opposed to the naval base construction project, saying that while the construction of the naval base is expected to cause damage to the marine environment as well as fishing rights such as village fishing grounds due to reclamation of public waters, there will be little ripple effect on the local economy.
Regarding the joint ecological survey of the Gangjeong waters last February, they raised concerns about the poor survey, saying, "The survey period was limited, and the survey scope only covered '3.5km forward from the Gangjeong-dong coastline' suggested by the Navy, making it difficult to properly determine the ecological status of the soft coral colony."
However, the Navy Headquarters is not slowing down the pace of the project, including announcing a compensation plan for 284,000 m2 of 201 parcels of expropriated land last month, announcing a draft environmental impact statement on the 6th of this month, and planning a resident briefing session on the 24th of this month. As such, conflict between the two sides seems inevitable unless special measures are taken.

ko-news-notices-417-8372c75064.title: Incheon, joint development of tidal power generation facilities with private companies
ko-news-notices-417-8372c75064.text:
Incheon, joint development of tidal power generation facilities with private companies
2022-03-02
Incheon City announced on the 20th that it is considering a plan to jointly develop a tidal power generation facility using the flow of seawater in the sea near Deokjeok Island with a private company.
For the Deokjeok Island tidal current power generation facility, which is being promoted through a public-private joint third sector development method, POSCO E&C will manufacture the facility and build the complex, and Korea South-East Power Co., Ltd. will take charge of system construction and operation, and Inha University will provide technical advisory support.
The city plans to sign a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with these organizations on the 29th and then confirm a specific project schedule with the goal of operation in 2016.
Currently, a plan is being reviewed to invest 800 billion won and install 200 tidal current generators in four locations around Deokjeok Island, Daeijak Island, and Soijak Island off the coast of Incheon. The power capacity of one generator is 1 MW, which can produce a total of 613,200 MW of power per year. This amounts to 3.2% of the current annual power requirement of 18.165 million MW in Incheon City.
The city expects that if tidal power generation is established here, it will have the effect of replacing 212,642 tons of bituminous coal, 126,511 tons of heavy oil, and 101,414 tons of liquefied natural gas (LNG) as power generation fuels annually.

ko-news-notices-416-8372c75064.title: Gangwon Deep Water ‘For a Thousand Years’ launched in May
ko-news-notices-416-8372c75064.text:
Gangwon Deep Water ‘For a Thousand Years’ launched in May
2022-03-02
The deep ocean water production plant promoted by Gangwon Deep Water Co., Ltd. (CEO Go Myeong-seon) was completed, and a completion ceremony was held at the Goseong-gun headquarters on April 17 with the attendance of about 200 domestic and foreign guests, including Gangwon-do Governor Kim Jin-seon, Goseong-gun Mayor Hwang Jong-guk, Daekyo Group Chairman Kang Young-jung, and Japanese KIBI System Chairman Matsuo Masaki.
Gangwon Deep Water Production Plant Co., Ltd. installed an offshore plant capable of taking in 3,000 tons of deep sea water per day at a depth of 605m at a location 6km off the East Sea in November last year. A stable supply of raw water was made possible by installing the only seamless deep sea water intake pipe in Korea. With the completion of a facility capable of processing 90 tons of desalination water per day and an onshore plant including bottle filling and packaging facilities, a state-of-the-art production plant that can process everything from water intake to product production in one place has been completed.
With the completion of the production plant, we will be equipped with a system that can utilize deep sea water from deep water raw water to desalinated water and mineral water. We plan to begin production of products in May and sell ‘Millennium Dangan’ drinkable deep sea water from June.
‘For a Thousand Years’, which is being released this time, will be released in two types: 1.2 liter for home supply and 350 ml for store supply. For home use, the system recruits members targeting households purchasing water purifiers and plastic bottles and distributes them directly to homes. The price per bottle is 1,000 won. In-store use can be purchased through department stores, hotels, fitness clubs, and convenience stores, and the price per bottle is 800 won.
What is deep ocean water?
It is a seawater resource that originates in Greenland and circulates through the Atlantic, Indo, and Pacific Oceans every 2,000 years. When the circulating seawater reaches the glacier area of ​​Greenland, it becomes very cold, its specific gravity increases, and it goes down to the deep sea (sea below 200m in depth). Water whose temperature has cooled to about 2℃ maintains a boundary with water near the surface and exists without mixing like water and oil. This is called ‘deep ocean water.’
The deep water located on the bottom of the East Sea in front of Goseong-gun, Gangwon-do is water that was created near Greenland about 4,000 years ago. It has excellent self-cleaning ability, is clean, and contains abundant minerals. It is a future new resource that has resource characteristics and can be used in various industrial fields.
In particular, Goseong deep ocean water was taken from a depth of 605m and was found to contain a large amount of minerals beneficial to the human body, such as magnesium, calcium, potassium, and sodium.

ko-news-notices-415-8372c75064.title: Saving the Four Major Rivers, a new starting point for creating ecological rivers
ko-news-notices-415-8372c75064.text:
Saving the Four Major Rivers, a new starting point for creating ecological rivers
2022-03-02
Saving the Four Major Rivers, a new starting point for creating ecological rivers
Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport is promoting guidelines for creating ecological rivers
With the promotion of the ‘Four Major Rivers Restoration Project’, the direction of river creation in Korea is expected to preserve the functions of natural rivers and be reborn as true ecological rivers where life breathes.
While carrying out the ‘Four Major Rivers Restoration’ project, the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs is promoting the establishment of the ‘Ecological River Creation Plan Guidelines’ to preserve the unique functions of rivers, create ecological rivers suited to the characteristics of natural rivers, and preserve the river environment.
The main contents of the newly prepared ecological river creation plan guideline are to collect and reflect the opinions of local residents and experts and to collect and reflect the opinions of local residents and experts from the planning stage in order to preserve the natural river functions when developing the river's water-friendly space. Based on sufficient research, such as analyzing and evaluating the characteristics of the target river, the basic direction of river creation will be applied differently by dividing it into conservation districts, restoration districts, and water-friendly districts so that the continuity and diversity of the entire river can be preserved. plan.
The conservation district is an area that requires conservation without artificial maintenance due to its excellent ecological history, culture, and scenery. In order to preserve the unique characteristics of the river, artificial creation of the environment or structural change is, in principle, prohibited.
In the case of a restoration district, it is an area that has been damaged or destroyed due to human interference or natural disasters and needs restoration to preserve nature, history, and cultural values. The past and present conditions are comprehensively reviewed and the size, water flow, and landscape aspects are comprehensively evaluated, and restoration is planned to the extent that it does not affect the preservation of the river's unique characteristics.
In addition, as a water-friendly district adjacent to a densely populated area and the city center, where water-friendly activities are possible within the scope of not damaging the inherent value of the river for the public interest, we plan to develop it to preserve and restore the environmental function of the river and to achieve a desirable harmony between the river and human life.
Facilities installed within the waterfront district minimize ecological disturbance, avoid the use of concrete structures, and use natural or eco-friendly packaging materials.
In addition, in order to not affect flood traffic and water flow, the installation of other fixed facilities, excluding benches, lighting, and small-scale sports facilities, will be restricted. Excessive restrictions on sports facilities through facility placement plans in water-friendly districts, prohibition of installation of river parking lots, and installation of bicycle paths will also be included.
The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport is currently in the process of supplementing the "Ecological River Creation Plan Guidelines" (draft) by collecting opinions and advice from experts in various fields. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport plans to enact the guidelines by the end of this month and apply them to the 'Four Major Rivers Restoration Project' by disseminating them to local governments, regional land management offices, etc., and if there is success, it plans to further expand the application of the guidelines that consider ecological river conservation more than water-friendly spaces when creating other rivers.

ko-news-notices-414-8372c75064.title: Blue House establishes regional secretary for ‘Saving the Four Major Rivers’
ko-news-notices-414-8372c75064.text:
Blue House establishes regional secretary for ‘Saving the Four Major Rivers’
2022-03-02
Blue House establishes regional secretary for ‘Saving the Four Major Rivers’
On the 21st, the Blue House carried out organizational reorganization and follow-up appointments at the secretary level, including the establishment of a regional development secretary in charge of comprehensive regional development measures and ‘saving the four major rivers’.
Oh Jeong-gyu, planning director of the National Balanced Development Committee, was appointed as the regional development secretary newly established under the Office of Senior Secretary to the President for Government Policy. After being appointed as the second secretary for national policy under the Office of Senior Secretary to the President for Government Policy Planning in May, candidate Oh moved to the position due to the reorganization of the Blue House. Accordingly, the Senior Secretary to the President for Government Affairs and Planning will have four secretaries for government affairs, future vision, broadcasting and communications, and regional development.
In addition, the position of Secretary for National Policy under the Office of Senior Secretary to the President for Government Policy, which became vacant due to the appointment of Secretary Heo Gyeong-wook as Vice Minister of Strategy and Finance, was renamed to Secretary for State Affairs, and Secretary for Economy and Finance Kim Dong-yeon moved to the position.
In addition, the Secretary for Economic Affairs and Finance was changed to Secretary for Economic Affairs, and Lim Jong-ryong, Director of the Planning and Coordination Office of the Ministry of Finance, was appointed. In relation to this, the Blue House has reportedly decided to establish a separate financial team in the form of a task force (TF) under the Office of Senior Secretary to the President for Economic Affairs, and will appoint a secretary-level team leader at a later date. The financial secretary position, which was eliminated in the reorganization in June last year, was virtually reinstated after 7 months. It is observed that the establishment of the financial team is in response to the judgment that financial market stability is essential to overcome economic difficulties and corporate restructuring, which are the top government tasks this year.
In addition, the Blue House changed the names of the Secretary for Science to Secretary for Science and Technology, the First Deputy Spokesperson to Deputy Spokesperson, and the Second Deputy Spokesperson to Director Chunchu.
An official from the Blue House explained, “We have carried out some organizational reorganization to actively respond to changes in circumstances such as the economic crisis and to assist in smooth administration of state affairs, including the promotion of a new government agenda. We have increased efficiency by creating only essential parts or strengthening functions.”
Reporter Choi Jae-wang jwchoi@msnet.co.kr

ko-news-notices-413-8372c75064.title: Deep-sea hydrothermal vent microorganisms are responsible for the world's energy
ko-news-notices-413-8372c75064.text:
Deep-sea hydrothermal vent microorganisms are responsible for the world's energy
2022-03-02
- Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport opens a path to highly efficient hydrogen production from hyperthermophilic archaea -
<Deep sea hydrothermal vent>
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs (Minister Jeong Jong-hwan) announced that it has succeeded in developing, for the first time in Korea, a core technology to produce highly efficient biohydrogen using ultra-thermophilic archaea NA1 (Thermococcus onnurineus NA1) isolated from deep-sea hydrothermal vents in the South Pacific.
This study is evaluated as a remarkable research achievement of the marine biotechnology development project that the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs has been promoting as its own R&D project.
* Research institution: Marine and Extreme Biomolecular Genome Research Center (Korea Ocean Research Institute, Director: Jeong-Geuk Kang)
NA1 is a type of archaea that grows at a high temperature of 80°C. It was collected in 2002 from the hydrothermal vent area off the coast of Papua New Guinea by Korea's ocean research vessel Onnuri.
As a result of the genome analysis of NA1, it was found that it possesses eight hydrogenase clusters, which is at least twice as many as other microorganisms known to date, so not only is the hydrogen extraction per unit much larger, but it is also very useful as it can produce biohydrogen using various substrates (food) such as carbon monoxide (CO), starch, and formic acid.
In addition, since environmental pollutants such as carbon monoxide can be cultivated as a food source, it is expected to present an innovative method of reducing carbon monoxide to companies that emit carbon monoxide during the manufacturing process.
Dr. Sangjin Kim's team at the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute published their research results in the latest issue (November 2008) of the Journal of Bacteriology (Impact 4.0, within the top 10% in the field of microorganisms), an internationally authoritative journal. The domestic application has been completed and overseas applications are being prepared.
According to a recent economic analysis*, the production cost of 1 kg of hydrogen from carbon monoxide using NA1 is estimated to be $0.8, which shows that it is more economical than other methods (water decomposition, etc.) that cost more than $3 per kg.
In addition, it is expected that commercialization will be possible within the next five years if additional and follow-up research** on gene regulation mechanisms and production optimization conditions continues.
* Jointly conducted by Ensoltech Co., Ltd., Korea Institute of Energy Research, Korea Institute of Basic Science, Kyung Hee University, and Sogang University
** Research to maximize hydrogen production efficiency through conditions in which hydrogenase groups are expressed or stopped or through genetic manipulation. Hydrogen can produce heat and electricity through a simple electrochemical reaction with oxygen in the air, and its only by-product is water (H2O), so it is attracting attention as an environmentally friendly future alternative energy source that does not emit CO2.
In addition, it has a high calorific value per unit weight and can be used in almost all fields used in current energy systems, including basic industrial materials, general fuel, automobiles, airplanes, and fuel cells. However, the currently used hydrogen production technology relies on the supply of fossil fuels in the water decomposition process and has low hydrogen production volume compared to the input energy, making it less economical, so the development of hydrogen production technology using solar power, wind power, and microorganisms is required.
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs announced that it plans to begin pilot production in 2009 by further identifying the hydrogen production mechanism and establishing a high-efficiency strain production system.
Source: Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs Policy News 2008-12-11 11:00 AM

ko-news-notices-412-8372c75064.title: Gageocho Marine Science Base completed in early October
ko-news-notices-412-8372c75064.text:
Gageocho Marine Science Base completed in early October
2022-03-02
- Birth of the second marine science base following the Ieodo base -
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs (Minister Jeong Jong-hwan) announced that it will invest 5.9 billion won (total construction cost 10 billion won) next year to complete the Gageocho Marine Science Base in October. As a result, Gageocho Base becomes the second comprehensive marine science base to be built in Korea, following the Ieodo Marine Science Base, which was completed in 2003.
The science base will be installed in Gageocho (15m depth of water), 47km west of Gageodo, and construction of the base structure is currently in progress on land. The progress rate in December 2008 was around 40%.
The total height of the Gageocho base is approximately 51m, and 26m, the height of a 10th floor apartment building, is revealed above the water. It weighs 523 tons and has an area of ​​330 m2 (100 pyeong), which is about 1/4 the size of the base. Although it is smaller than the Ieo Island base, there is no significant difference in terms of function.
At the Gageocho base, 27 types of meteorological and ocean-related observation equipment will be installed to carry out missions, and the observation data will be transmitted in real time to relevant researchers through the Rose of Sharon satellite.
The transmitted observation data is used to increase the accuracy of weather and marine forecasts and is expected to be used in many fields, including minimizing damage from natural disasters at sea.
Source: Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs 2008-12-29 11:00 AM

ko-news-notices-411-8372c75064.title: Korea Maritime Industry Association inaugural general meeting
ko-news-notices-411-8372c75064.text:
Korea Maritime Industry Association inaugural general meeting
2022-03-02
- Creation of blue ocean through strengthening cooperation between maritime small and medium-sized enterprises -
In order to strengthen corporate competitiveness by promoting exchange and cooperation among small and medium-sized maritime enterprises, the inaugural general meeting of the ‘Korea Maritime Enterprise Association’, in which 79 maritime-related companies participated, will be held at the Ritz-Carlton Hotel in Seoul at 3 p.m. on Wednesday, December 17.
At the inaugural general meeting on this day, about 100 people, including Vice Minister of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs Lee Jae-gyun, National Assembly member Park Sang-eun, and representatives of member companies, will attend the promoters' meeting and begin official activities.
The ‘Korea Maritime Industry Association’, which is being launched this time, is a private-led consultative body that plans to lay the foundation for the continued growth of the maritime industry in the future, including sharing maritime-related information and presenting policy proposals to strengthen corporate competitiveness.
An official from the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs said, ‘With the launch of the Korea Maritime Enterprises Association, it is expected that we will be able to overcome the limitations of small-scale maritime small and medium-sized enterprises and promote the development of the maritime industry through cooperation between companies. In addition, it is significant that in the recent difficult economic conditions, small and medium-sized maritime businessmen voluntarily formed an association to wisely overcome the crisis in the spirit of coexistence and strengthen their resolve to take a new leap forward.’
Source: Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs Policy News 2008-12-17 06:00 AM

ko-news-notices-410-8372c75064.title: Invasion of red and green tides into the sea of ​​Jeju Island
ko-news-notices-410-8372c75064.text:
Invasion of red and green tides into the sea of ​​Jeju Island
2022-03-02
Invasion of red and green tides into the sea of Jeju Island
Part 2 Impact of Three Gorges Dam (Chief Researcher Dong-rim Choi, South Sea Characteristics Research Department)
The Yangtze River basin is a catchment area where water from all tributaries gathers into the main stream of the Yangtze River. The basin area is approximately 1,940,000 km 2, which is one-fifth of China's area, and approximately 400 million people, approximately one-third of China's total population, reside here. Comparing their size with South Korea's area (100,000 km 2 ) and population (48 million people), they are 19 times larger and more than 8 times larger, respectively. Materials discharged from the Yangtze River basin, that is, not only the red clay from the mountains and fields washed by rainwater, but also all materials dissolved in surface water or groundwater, gather and flow into the main stream of the Yangtze River. The color of the water in the Yangtze River is a yellowish ocher color, which is much more turbid than the color we think of river water. You can immediately see that it contains a lot of floating sand. In addition, domestic sewage, agricultural and livestock wastewater, and industrial wastewater discharged by residents living in cities and villages also seep into the Yangtze River.
Approximately 50,000 large and small dams have been built on the tributaries and main stream of the Yangtze River. Among these, the construction of the Three Gorges Dam, which is by far the largest not only in China but also in the world in terms of dam size, freshwater storage volume, and power generation capacity, is scheduled for completion in 2009. The size of the Three Gorges Dam is approximately 2.3 km wide and 185 m high. The dam's freshwater storage area extends to Chongqing with an average width of about 1.1 km and a length of about 660 km, with a maximum freshwater storage capacity of about 39.3 billion tons. The biggest problem with storing water in a dam is that the high concentration of suspended sediments contained in the Yangtze River water settle to the bottom. Before the dam was built, this floating sediment formed a natural embankment as it passed downstream, and when it reached the coast of the Shanghai estuary, it contributed to the creation of new land.
Points where red tide and green algae (spiny sea lettuce) were discovered on the west and east sides, respectively, along with the Yangtze River low-salinity water mass identified during oceanographic observations between August 1 and 5, 2008 in the southwestern waters of Jeju Island. The picture in the upper right corner shows the Yangtze River basin.
The average amount of sediment discharged from the Yangtze River to the East China Sea every year is approximately 480 million tons. However, as dam construction became more active in the 1980s, the concentration of floating sand showed a noticeable decrease. According to recent Chinese data, the water level of the dam rose from 136m to 156m over the three years from the completion of the first dam construction of the Three Gorges Dam in 2003 to the completion of the second construction in 2006, and during this period, annual discharge sharply decreased to an average of about 170 million tons. In particular, in 2006, it recorded a surprising decrease of about 0.9 billion tons, which is less than 100 million tons.
It can be easily expected that when the dam construction is finally completed in 2009 and the dam water level rises to 175 m, it will decrease further. With plans to build more dams in the future, emissions reductions are expected to accelerate further. In addition, it will decrease further once the South Water North Flow Project (a large-scale waterway construction project to bring water from the Yangtze River in the south to the northern water shortage area by creating an artificial waterway), which is currently under construction, is completed. For reference, the amount of floating sediment discharged from the Yellow River was usually about 1 billion tons, but it has decreased sharply since the 2000s, and is known to be discharged into Bohai Bay at only about 12% compared to the past.
From the Yangtze River, not only suspended sediments but also nutrients flow out to the estuary coast and the East China Sea. In particular, major nutrients such as nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and silicon (Si) are dissolved in fresh water and supplied to seawater. According to Chinese reports, the distribution of nitrate and phosphate concentrations in the Yangtze River Estuary has been showing a steep increase since the mid-1980s. The causes of this are analyzed to be the abuse of chemical fertilizers to improve agricultural productivity, which are common in modern industrial society, the increase in domestic sewage such as synthetic detergents, and the indiscriminate discharge of industrial wastewater. In contrast, the concentration of silicates shows a clear tendency to decrease. The construction of dams will lead to a decrease in the concentration of silicates of land origin supplied to the sea, and in particular, the sharp decrease in suspended sediment emissions due to the construction of the Three Gorges Dam will further fuel the decline of silicates in the East China Sea.
The amount and balance of nutrients in marine ecosystems have a significant impact on the community and species composition of phytoplankton. Excessive nitrates and phosphates supplied from land cause eutrophication in coastal waters, resulting in the proliferation of harmful red tide organisms. In fact, it is known that the number and area of ​​red tide occurrences in the Yangtze River estuary and coastal waters have been rapidly increasing since the 1990s due to the abundant supply of nitrate and phosphate. It is reported that, unlike nitrate and phosphate, the supply of silicate is decreasing, and as a result, the distribution ratio of diatoms that depend on silicate to survive is gradually decreasing in the entire phytoplankton community. Such changes in the ecosystem are thought to be natural abnormalities that occur when the balance established by organisms adapting themselves over millions of years is broken in an extremely short period of time by the selfish activities of people.
The green algae and red algae discovered this year are distributed in the east and west of the Yangtze River low-salt water mass, respectively, with the green algae taking the lead and the red algae following. In other words, the low-salinity water mass pushed out of the Yangtze River Estuary served as a carrier to transport those distributed in the estuary and coastal areas. Last year, DDT, a type of persistent organic pollutant, was detected in slightly low-salinity water of about 30% observed in the western waters of Jeju at a much higher concentration than the surrounding seawater. China is the country that used the third largest amount of DDT in the world, following the United States and the former Soviet Union. Although its use is currently banned in both Korea and China, it appears that the non-degradable DDT used in the past is still mixed in the Yangtze River water. This shows that harmful organisms and hazardous chemical pollutants are not limited to the Yangtze River estuary and coastal areas, but are flowing into Korean waters in low-salinity water.
The amount of freshwater from the Yangtze River supplied to the East China Sea is about 920 billion tons on average every year, and more than half, about 480 billion tons, is discharged during the rainy season from June to September (about 25 times the outflow of the Nakdong River), and a significant amount of this reaches Jeju Island, about 450 km away from the mouth of the Yangtze River, in about a month. In addition, water quality and environmental changes are rapidly occurring due to large-scale water repair work taking place around the Yangtze River, such as the construction of the Three Gorges Dam. The above-mentioned environmental problems are too close to our waters, too large in scale, and too obvious to be limited to internal problems in neighboring countries. I think what we need to do now is to systematically approach the rapidly changing surrounding environment, look closely at it, diagnose it accurately, and come up with appropriate alternatives.
I close this article with the hope that the red and green tides that have appeared in Jeju waters are not a sign of environmental change that can occur at any time, but rather a temporary phenomenon that occurred only this year.
Source: Ocean Research Institute 2008.09.22

ko-news-notices-409-8372c75064.title: Gyeongin Canal Project Plan
ko-news-notices-409-8372c75064.text:
Gyeongin Canal Project Plan
2022-03-02
The Gyeongin Canal Project Plan is;
Using spillways as canals to prevent floods, reduce logistics costs, resolve transportation difficulties, revitalize culture, tourism, and leisure, and promote local economic development.
□ The Gyeongin Canal is used as a spillway to prevent flood damage in the Gulpocheon basin, a frequently flooded area (100-year frequency).
※ The spillway is only used for 15 days during the flood season → Canal construction is used for 350 days, improving water quality.
□ Reduces logistics costs, alleviates transportation difficulties, and contributes to low-carbon green growth
* Direct transportation from Busan or China to Seoul (Gimpo Terminal) without transshipment
□ Connecting rivers and sea routes to create various synergy effects in culture, tourism, and leisure
* Role as the aorta of the western metropolitan area, including Songdo, Cheongna, Geomdan, and Gimpo districts
* Developed into an international tourism and logistics attraction in connection with Seoul’s Hangang Renaissance
* Marina vessels such as yachts can sail from the Han River to the Gyeongin Canal to the West Sea.
- Water-friendly spaces such as bicycle paths, walking trails, and parks are provided in the surrounding area.
□ Revitalization of the local economy, including employment effects of approximately 25,000 people and production inducement of approximately 3 trillion won.

ko-news-notices-408-8372c75064.title: 7 habits of successful people
ko-news-notices-408-8372c75064.text:
7 habits of successful people
2022-03-02
(Overview of the 7 habits of successful people)
1) Habit 1: Be proactive
The actions we take are determined by the decisions we make, and are in no way influenced by the circumstances surrounding us.
- There is no way I can do it  Let’s find an alternative
- He makes me so angry  I can control my emotions
- They won't allow it  I can persuade them effectively.
2) Habit 2: Set goals and take action (personal leadership)
Starting today, using the image, appearance, and paradigm you want to have in your final moments as the frame of reference and standard by which you review everything.
3) Habit 3: Do important things first (principle of personal management)
Successful people have a habit of being willing to do things that other people don't want to do.
“The most important things should not be influenced by the most insignificant things” (Goethe)
- Ability to prepare and plan according to priorities
- Ability to implement priorities
4) Habit 4: Pursue mutual benefit (interpersonal leadership)
A mindset that pursues mutual benefit in all interpersonal relationships
5) Habit 5: Listen and then understand (principle of empathetic communication)
6) Habit 6: Use synergy (principle of productive cooperation)
The most difficult part to put into practice.
Many people have not experienced even the slightest synergy at home or at work. People are trained to communicate defensively and protectively, and are imbued with a script that tells them not to trust others or their lives. As a result, people are not open to productive cooperation. However, this represents the greatest tragedy and waste in life. Because enormous potentials are completely buried and undeveloped.
* Example of synergy: generating one new idea in a classroom or organization
- An atmosphere of openness to each other, learning and listening to each other's ideas, and feeling safe emerges.  Brainstorming, where creative spirit, imagination, and intellectual exchange appear rather than evaluation and criticism.  Discussions that weave and shape, new developments, ideas, and exciting transformations taking place that are clearly visible to all involved.
7) Habit 7: Train your mind and body (balanced self-renewal)

ko-news-notices-407-8372c75064.title: Estuary conservation, the mother of life, is the way to save the country.
ko-news-notices-407-8372c75064.text:
Estuary conservation, the mother of life, is the way to save the country.
2022-03-02
Estuary conservation, the mother of life, is the way to save the country.
- Held a symposium to prepare efficient management measures for the Yeongsan River Estuary -
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs will hold a symposium on September 5th in the conference room of Jeonnam Provincial Office to prepare effective management measures for the Yeongsan River Estuary.
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs has been conducting a systematic survey of estuaries across the country since 2007 to establish an efficient estuary management system, and is currently conducting a survey targeting the Yeongsan River estuary this year.
In this symposium, in addition to the results of the Yeongsan River Estuary survey conducted by the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs, the status of environmental changes, problems, and policy proposals, including water quality, sediment, marine life, and hydrology, surveyed by various research institutions such as Korea Rural Development Corporation, Jeonnam Development Institute, and Mokpo National University will be discussed. Based on this, civic groups, experts, local governments, and government agencies will work together to explore various alternatives to overcome the problems.
In most estuaries in Korea, the construction of estuary dams is causing destruction of ecosystems, such as blocking the exchange of seawater and fresh water, destroying habitats, and disrupting food webs. In the case of the Yeongsan River estuary, environmental problems such as continuous deterioration of water quality and damage to the estuary ecosystem have been caused since the construction of estuary dams in 1981.
The water quality of the inner Yeongsan Lake, which was recently cut off by the estuary bank of the Yeongsan River, is unsuitable even as agricultural water, and the adverse effects on the ecosystem due to eutrophication, such as green algae phenomenon occurring in Mokpo Port located around the estuary bank, are worsening, so an effective management policy to improve water quality is urgently needed.
Hyunsoo Yoon, head of the Marine Ecology Department at the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs, said, “The existing estuary policy was assessed to have achieved significant effectiveness in terms of stable water security, food production, and construction of transportation infrastructure, but as social issues and values change, various problems such as ecosystem destruction are being exposed,” adding, “This symposium will present the status and problems of the Yeongsan River Estuary from an expert perspective, and various stakeholders such as local residents, local governments, and NGOs will discuss pending issues.” “It will be held as a venue for open discussion to come up with solutions, and various measures, such as estuary restoration and water quality improvement through seawater distribution, will be discussed,” he said.
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs plans to develop and promote a more effective estuary management policy through cooperation between the central and local governments based on the contents presented at this symposium.
Posting date 2008-09-05 06:00:00.0 (Source: Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs)

ko-news-notices-406-8372c75064.title: Realizing green growth through mudflat restoration
ko-news-notices-406-8372c75064.text:
Realizing green growth through mudflat restoration
2022-03-02
Realizing green growth through mudflat restoration
‘International Symposium on Tidal Flat Restoration’ held to commemorate the Ramsar Conference of the Parties
Korea's mudflats are considered one of the world's five largest mudflats, but they are also always under development pressure such as reclamation and reclamation.
Tidal flats are not only a major food source that provides a variety of food, but also a resting place for citizens that provide beautiful scenery and relaxation. Additionally, tidal flats are spawning grounds and habitats for numerous marine organisms, and are also an important space for maintaining ocean biodiversity. Tidal flats are known to have excellent pollution purification and disaster prevention functions as well as climate change control functions.
Recently, as the importance of these mudflats has become known, the need for restoration of damaged mudflats has been raised, and large-scale restoration projects are already underway in advanced countries for the purposes of promoting biodiversity, recovering fisheries resources, revitalizing ecotourism, and preventing coastal disasters due to climate change.
Accordingly, the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs is also pursuing an ambitious plan to restore the function of the marine ecosystem by restoring Korea's mudflats in an eco-friendly manner, taking advantage of the 10th Ramsar Conference of the Parties held in Korea.
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs announced that it will hold an international symposium on tidal flat restoration under the theme of “Recent Progress on Coastal Wetland Restoration” at the Hoam Faculty Center of Seoul National University starting September 8 with the participation of local governments, experts, environmental groups and local residents related to tidal flats.
At this international symposium, attended by about 200 domestic and foreign experts, experts from the United States, Japan, and the Netherlands, who have extensive experience and know-how in tidal flat restoration, will focus on presenting cases of actual tidal flat restoration projects in their countries. On the following day, Gochang-gun, which purchased an abandoned fish farm for the tidal flat restoration project, will be visited on-site to review and advise on the tidal flat restoration plan. plan.
In particular, Dr. Henk J. de Vries, a Dutch Wadden Sea mudflat expert, will introduce the case of restoring a Dutch polder back to a mudflat, and Dr. Jun Kakino from Japan will introduce the regeneration of clam resources through the restoration of the Tokyo Bay mudflat.
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs plans to use this international symposium as an opportunity to continuously identify global trends in tidal flat restoration and implement active tidal flat restoration policies.
Yoon Hyeon-soo, head of the Marine Ecology Department at the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs, said, “We will establish a comprehensive plan for tidal flat restoration at the end of the year when the actual survey on damaged tidal flats and sites for restoration across the country is completed, and we will promote a pilot project starting in 2009. As a pilot project, we are considering not only a project to convert abandoned fish farms or abandoned salt farms into mudflats, but also a project to reverse reclaim farmland created through past reclamation.” He also said, “We will lead green growth by securing marine biological resources and preventing coastal disasters through tidal flat restoration, which is a green technology, as well as pursuing the revitalization of eco-tourism.”
This event, which is being held amid growing interest in tidal flats at home and abroad, including the holding of the Ramsar Conference of the Parties, is expected to involve not only related experts but also the general public interested in tidal flats.

ko-news-notices-405-8372c75064.title: Asan Bay sand sediments are moving
ko-news-notices-405-8372c75064.text:
Asan Bay sand sediments are moving
2022-03-02
Comparison of two points in time: 1976 and 2006... Research is needed to predict changes in seafloor topography.
Local seafloor topography changes are actively taking place in Asan Bay.
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency compared and analyzed chart data from 1976 and 2006 and revealed that the form of sand sediments accumulated in Asan Bay has been changing over the past 30 years. Jungangcheontoe, a sandy deposit, is distributed in a northwest-southeast direction from the entrance to Asan Bay, about 15 km long and 2 to 5 km wide, and the northeast is steeper than the southwest, forming an asymmetry. According to the analysis results, compared to 30 years ago, the area of ​​the summit exposed above sea level during low tide has expanded by about 10,000 m2, and a small trough has been formed at the southeastern end. In addition, the sand deposits were moved 400 to 500 m to the northeast, clearly showing changes in the seafloor topography.
Existing research results suggest that these topographical changes are due to the installation of seawalls, port construction, and industrial complexes that have been going on since the early 1970s, resulting in a monotony of the coastline, resulting in changes in seawater flow characteristics and changes in the form of sediments. In particular, changes in tidal currents in Asan Bay, which has a large average elevation (573 cm) and is deeply indented inland, are known to have influenced the shape and direction of movement of sand deposits. And if coastal development continues, the form of sediments is expected to continue to change to maintain balance with the changed marine environment.
□ The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency plans to continuously monitor water depth changes in the future to identify changes in the shape and movement patterns of sand sediments and conduct research to predict future changes in seafloor topography. In addition, we plan to produce data necessary for coastal use development, including providing information necessary for navigational safety by comparing and analyzing trends in water depth fluctuations in sea areas where environmental changes are expected.

ko-news-notices-404-8372c75064.title: The possibility of seawater flooding on the Korean Peninsula gradually increases.
ko-news-notices-404-8372c75064.text:
The possibility of seawater flooding on the Korean Peninsula gradually increases.
2022-03-02
Due to global warming, the possibility of seawater flooding on the Korean Peninsula is gradually increasing.
Analysis results showed that typhoons are becoming stronger on the Korean Peninsula due to the effects of global warming, and the annual maximum tsunami height is increasing.
※ Tsunami height: The difference between the actual observed sea level height and the predicted sea level height.
Since 1970, Korea's average temperature has increased by 1.16℃, and coastal surface water temperature has also increased by about 0.7℃ over the past 35 years. In addition, over the past 40 years, the average sea level in the waters surrounding Korea has risen by about 2 to 5 mm every year, and this appears to be closely related to the rise in air and water temperature.
Currently, the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency, which is conducting research on changes in sea level along the coast of the Korean Peninsula, selected four locations, including Yeosu, Tongyeong, Mukho, and Sokcho, among sea level data observed off the coast of Korea over the past 20 years and compared them with meteorological data, revealing that the maximum tsunami height increased by approximately 10 to 30 cm. In particular, it is understood that about 78% of the annual maximum tsunami heights were affected by typhoons.
Meanwhile, the recently released 4th report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) (2007) predicts that temperatures will rise by 1.8 to 4.0°C, sea levels will rise by 18 to 59 cm, and typhoons will become stronger within this century, raising awareness of abnormal weather events and local sea level rise due to future temperature rises on the Korean Peninsula.
Moreover, if a high tsunami due to a typhoon occurs during high tide, serious coastal flooding can result in enormous human casualties and environmental and economic losses, so it is urgent to prepare countermeasures.
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency has installed and operates an ocean observation buoy to predict typhoon paths, and plans to continue to conduct monitoring and forecasting research to reduce coastal disasters along with analysis of long-term variability in tsunami heights using sea level observation data and comparative research using meteorological data.

ko-news-notices-403-8372c75064.title: The core of team leader leadership
ko-news-notices-403-8372c75064.text:
The core of team leader leadership
2022-03-02
(Team leader leadership)
Only those who are ready to get their hands dirty can succeed as true leaders. In other words, these are the behavioral guidelines that a ‘field-oriented leader’ who is strong in practical situations must have.
1) Establish the basics of leadership through communication
Communication is an important fundamental element in building leadership skills. This is because excellent leadership cannot be demonstrated without communication. There are countless cases of business failure due to poor communication. Therefore, leaders must be able to communicate smoothly with all employees as well as people related to the business and customers. The core of communication strategy is to always provide support and encouragement to the organization and its members, and to share and further strengthen the company's vision.
2) Move your mind and achieve results
A leader must have the ability to motivate members to achieve good results. If you provide employees with opportunities for continuous training and growth and motivate them to feel fully recognized and empowered by their superiors, your team's work performance will improve significantly. Rather than strongly controlling members by creating an atmosphere of fear, you should be able to truly move their hearts by using motivational methods such as continuous communication and ‘positive reinforcement.’ And more importantly, leaders must be able to motivate themselves.
3) Strengthen teamwork through coaching
Leaders also need to act as coaches. The coaching process can help employees solve problems on their own while providing an environment that encourages more creative thinking. Coaching activities are not aimed at managing and guiding employees, but rather focus on leading and influencing them, so above all, leaders should not be obsessed with authority and authority. Coaching produces good results through questions and discussions rather than instructions, and listening and support rather than control.
4) Distribute the leader’s authority
Empowerment is widely used in the business world to mean ‘delegation of authority.’ The purpose of empowerment is to ensure that employees recognize that they are making invaluable contributions to the company's development and success. If a leader realizes empowerment and delegates tasks and authority to employees, employees can develop the ability to handle work wisely with a proactive attitude. Unfortunately, many leaders have difficulty accepting the idea of ​​delegating authority to their employees. It is important to remember that the best leaders successfully achieve empowerment by utilizing the potential of each employee to the fullest.
5) Achieve your goals through unified teamwork
In an economic situation that changes rapidly every day, companies are strengthening ‘team management’, which involves forming teams with a small number of people to perform core tasks. In addition, we are building teamwork in a more powerful and efficient way to achieve corporate goals and pursuing a shift in a new direction. Therefore, the team leader must create a dynamic team by accurately identifying the strengths and weaknesses of each team member, while acknowledging their strengths and utilizing them to the fullest to strengthen teamwork.
6) Manage your time efficiently
Time management has emerged as an important leadership issue. This is because many leaders are overwhelmed by excessive workload. Therefore, a leader who cannot properly coordinate and manage time cannot demonstrate leadership properly. It is a good idea to use time efficiently by accurately understanding the severity and progress schedule of the work, while reducing the amount of work the leader is responsible for as much as possible through methods such as delegation of authority. Organizing your work space to create a convenient work environment is also a way to utilize time efficiently.
7) Jump directly into the cause of the conflict
No matter how talented the leader is, there will always be conflict in any organization. However, since a team's performance is determined by how effectively it can resolve conflicts, leaders must quickly identify the cause of the conflict and proactively resolve it together with employees. The best way to resolve conflict is through open communication. This is a method of seeking the opinions of everyone involved in a conflict and talking openly with them. What is most important is the leader's courage to face the problem head-on and come up with a solution.
8) Lead change with a proactive attitude
‘Change management’ is a very important quality directly related to a leader’s survival. The idea of ​​staying where you are and not accepting change can be said to be almost an illusion in the world of fierce business competition. Therefore, leaders must accurately grasp the reality of change and carefully consider how to deal with the emotions and psychological states that come from letting go of familiar things. In change management, nothing is more important than how you handle change. Open communication, the attitude of being in an opposing position, building trust, a positive attitude, and the attitude of accepting employees' opinions and delegating authority to them are ways to lead leaders to flexibly respond to and manage change.
9) Secure the best talent
The representative task of a leader is ‘recruiting talent.’ There is no better strategy to develop an organization or company than hiring talented people. This is because a company cannot achieve business success if its human resources are not combined appropriately and in a balanced manner. Therefore, the criteria for talent recruitment should be, above all, conditions that can contribute to the success of the company, and careful judgment should be made by establishing detailed recruitment plans and strategies. Only leaders who recognize the critical importance of the hiring process can attract the best talent and ultimately create a strong work environment by attracting great human resources.
10) Establish your own evaluation strategy
Excellent leaders continuously evaluate employees’ work abilities to increase the organization’s productivity and performance. To evaluate employees fairly and make it worthwhile, leaders must begin the evaluation by accurately identifying the employee's strengths and weaknesses and recommending improvements. The purpose of evaluation is not to criticize employees' shortcomings, but rather, it is important to enable employees to recognize their own shortcomings. Employee performance evaluations should not be a one-time, year-round event, but should be conducted continuously on a regular basis. Additionally, it is important to conduct both positive and negative evaluations at the same time, and to evaluate each employee in a different way.
11) Excellent leadership is revealed in the ability to deal with problem employees
There are various types of problem employees, including employees with poor work ability, employees who handle work sloppily, employees who are lazy, employees who are always late, and employees who blatantly rebel against company policies. To become an excellent leader, you must be able to accurately identify the type of problem employee and respond appropriately. If an employee causes a problem, you should not blame them right away. They first show tolerance by saying that it is entirely possible, and do not spare encouragement and support to help solve the problem. If the problem persists, hold a meeting with the employee and ask him or her to correct the inappropriate behavior. If this does not work, seriously consider dismissal.
12) Recognize and reward employees’ abilities
The skill of managing subordinates is also an important quality a leader must have so that employees can work happily and continue to want to do their best for the leader and the company. There are surprisingly many cases where employee management is overlooked, and in this case, companies may suffer irreparable losses. Therefore, leaders must make active efforts to manage employees to avoid losing talented employees, while also paying attention to managing employees' information and skills accumulated over a long period of time.
13) Proactively assert yourself, but respect others.
The most important factor in becoming a leader is personality. A person who does not express himself well and has a passive personality will never be able to lead many people.
Source: Team Leader Leadership (Bob Adams)

ko-news-notices-402-8372c75064.title: How to lead an organization of 10 or fewer people well
ko-news-notices-402-8372c75064.text:
How to lead an organization of 10 or fewer people well
2022-03-02
(How to lead an organization of 10 or less people well)
The team leader is just as important as the CEO!
All companies, from small companies with about ten employees to large corporations with thousands of employees, are made up of small organizations led by managers, managers, team leaders, etc. Leaders of these small organizations are managers who give employees goals and help them achieve results, but they are also practitioners who must achieve results in their work. Additionally, in small companies, they play the role of professional managers, establishing business strategies and making decisions together with the managers. Therefore, it is no exaggeration to say that their role determines the fate of the company.
A leader who is good at leading an organization of 10 or fewer people
* Leaders do not step forward
Thanks to the steady success of selling cars so far, he has risen to the position of leader. If the department is instructed to sell 50 units per month, how many units should the leader sell? As the leader, can I work harder and sell about 15 units? The author clearly states that a leader does not need to sell a single unit. When leaders dive directly into practical work, they have less time to manage employees. As a result, employees are unable to complete the remaining goals. A leader who tries his best alone will become angry, and employees will become less motivated, further reducing productivity. Leaders can allocate roles to employees according to their personalities and abilities, and focus on providing guidance and management to motivate and improve sales ability. Leaders are no longer top employees but department managers.
* Provide clear instructions and check each step.
When giving work instructions, you must express them clearly and check each step as you proceed. What you need to keep in mind for clear work instructions is not ‘what to do’ but ‘produce a certain result.’ Leaders themselves must clearly set their expectations and clearly communicate the desired results to their employees. In addition, during the work process, you must check each step and quickly correct if expectations are not met to achieve the desired expectations.
* Consideration is given according to ability and motivation (customized consideration)
It is urgent to give new employees gentle instructions on their work rather than personal consideration. Employees with high ability and motivation do not need instructions or consideration. This is because unnecessary instructions or consideration can be annoying or create feelings of distrust, which reduces motivation.
* Don't be obsessed with popularity
A person who tries to impress his employees cannot be a good leader. This is because not wanting to be hated clouds your judgment. If you remain silent when you need to speak, you will not be able to provide necessary guidance, and of course, management will not be done properly. (In fact, more employees change jobs under leaders who do not point out mistakes. If you point out mistakes accurately and do not spare praise and encouragement, you will become a leader who flexibly uses carrots and sticks.)
* Treat employees with sincerity
To truly care about your employees is to help them grow so that they can accomplish any task on their own. If employees are viewed as tools to achieve the leader's goals or as a means for one's own advancement, this is implicitly conveyed to them. Looking back, everyone will have that feeling, and at the same time, their trust in the leader and love for their work would all disappear. Let’s maximize the capabilities of our employees with the goal of enabling them to become independent after three years of working under me. With their growth, the department's productivity will be maximized. And maybe it will become something big enough to change that employee's life.
Source: How to lead an organization of 10 or fewer people well (Katsuhiko Horinouchi)

ko-news-notices-401-8372c75064.title: ‘Sihwa District Sustainable Development Council’ launched as an official organization
ko-news-notices-401-8372c75064.text:
‘Sihwa District Sustainable Development Council’ launched as an official organization
2022-03-02
‘Sihwa District Sustainable Development Council’ launched as an official organization
Exemplary success stories of governance systems
The “Sihwa District Sustainable Development Council” (hereinafter referred to as the “Sihwa Sustainability Council”), which has been discussing environmental improvement and eco-friendly development plans in Sihwa District, was reborn as an official organization. The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs believes that it is necessary to make it an official organization in order to strengthen the function of the ‘Sihwa Sustainability Council’, which has been discussing and coordinating social conflicts due to environmental improvement of Sihwa Lake and eco-friendly development of Sihwa District. It was announced that Directive No. 2008-43 (April 8, 2008) was enacted and that, based on this, it was newly launched as an official organization on April 30, 2008 after going through the committee appointment process.
The ‘Sihwa Sustainability Council’ is a public-private consultative body formed in January 2004 by citizens, environmental groups, experts, related ministries, and local governments to resolve environmental issues in the Sihwa District and conflicts surrounding Sihwa Lake tidal flat development, etc. It started based on the principle that citizens, environmental groups, and the government review all matters related to the development and environment of the Sihwa District from the beginning, and has held about 160 meetings over the past 4 years to continuously discuss the matter. As a result, many achievements have been made. Specifically, in the environmental aspect, water quality was greatly improved by the Korea Water Resources Corporation, the project operator, investing about 68 billion won in environmental improvement resources, and air quality was also able to be improved by jointly conducting a thorough survey of about 2,000 companies moving into the complex by residents, citizens, environmental groups, and local governments. In terms of urban planning, the foundation for eco-friendly development was laid by ensuring that the Sihwa MTV and Songsan Green City projects, which had been discontinued since the late 1990s due to environmental controversies, were developed normally through consultation and coordination.
* Sihwa Industrial Complex river water quality improvement: COD 1,970ppm in '04 → 17ppm in '06
* Contribution to the Air Quality Improvement Fund (KRW 20 billion): Facility improvement for major odor emitting companies
* Construction of Sihwa MTV, a high-tech industrial complex, began on the northern tidal flat (9.26㎢) (August 2007)
* Agreement to develop Songsan Green City, a tourism and ecological complex city, on the southern tidal flat (54.69㎢) (August 2007)
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs plans to ensure that the newly launched Sihwa Sustainability Council will maintain and develop the existing principles of decision-making based on social consensus and further expand the scope of stakeholder participation as well as active communication with the local community. The chair of the Sihwa Sustainability Council was decided to be jointly held by the private sector and the government. Civil and environmental groups active in the Sihwa district and related experts recommended by civil and environmental groups will participate as private members. Government members will include central ministries such as the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, the Ministry of Knowledge Economy, the Ministry of Environment and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, local governments such as Gyeonggi Province, Siheung City, Ansan City and Hwaseong City, and the Korea Water Resources Corporation, the Sihwa District project operator. The organization was composed of a general meeting, a coordination committee, and specialized subcommittees (urban planning, environmental improvement) to increase the systematicity and expertise of discussions, and when necessary, it was decided to expand the scope of community participation by forming a special committee to collect residents' opinions for active communication with the community.
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs expects that with the launch of the ‘Sihwa Sustainability Council’ as an official organization, the responsibility of discussion will increase and greater trust from local residents and civil society will be secured, and based on this, the Sihwa District will be developed in a more eco-friendly manner.
