ko-news-notices-400-8372c75064.title: The era of integrated management of marine environmental surveys begins!!
ko-news-notices-400-8372c75064.text:
The era of integrated management of marine environmental surveys begins!!
2022-03-02
The era of integrated management of marine environmental surveys begins!!
- Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs Conducted comprehensive marine ecosystem survey targeting Jeonnam region-
In the future, an integrated environmental management system is expected to be established in the sea.
The Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs announced that it will hold a briefing session on the launch of the 2008 comprehensive marine ecosystem survey project at Mokpo City Hall in Jeollanam-do on April 30.
This comprehensive marine ecosystem survey, in which national organizations such as the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs, the National Institute of Fisheries Science, and the Tidal Flat Research Center, and about 20 professional organizations such as the Korea Ocean Research Institute, universities, environmental businesses, organizations, and NGOs participate, unifies the survey areas of various projects carried out as part of the marine survey project by the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs. and estuary management system establishment research was conducted to maximize policy effectiveness by focusing on the Jeonnam region.
The launch briefing session for this project, attended by approximately 200 people, including local government officials, residents, and related experts, will be conducted in the order of introduction of each project and general discussion, following the introduction of Korea's marine ecosystem conservation policy by the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs.
The Marine Ecosystem Basic Survey Project ('06~'15) is a survey project on the overall marine ecosystem of Korea, including seawater, sediments, and marine life. It is a project to create a marine ecosystem map that can classify the health of the marine ecosystem and provide basic data for designating marine protected areas. The 2nd Marine Ecosystem Basic Survey Project ('08~'12) is a 5-year project conducted by the Minister of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs in charge of coastal wetlands (tidal flats). As a project to periodically investigate the sedimentation environment, pollution, and status of animals and plants in Korea's mudflats, we plan to conduct an overall survey of the mudflats in the Jeonnam region, focusing on the bottom and condition of the Shinan-gun area.
In addition, the estuary investigation project targeted the Yeongsan River estuary and included the estuary's functions, including investigation of water quality and sedimentation environment of the estuary, basic production, and benthic food web. These survey results are planned to be used as basis for evaluating the economic value of the estuary and suggesting policy utilization measures in the future, and will also be implemented as a review of restoration technology and prior research for the restoration of small rivers.
Meanwhile, this survey area includes many islands and mudflats, such as Uido and Hauido, with beautiful unpolluted natural scenery and excellent biodiversity. For areas with high protection value or in need of environmental conservation, designation of protected areas will be reviewed through local public hearings.
Starting with this comprehensive marine ecosystem survey, the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs expects a synergy effect on environmental conservation by unifying the survey area for future marine survey projects, and aims to implement a reliable administrative system that directly touches local governments and local residents by presenting comprehensive, interconnected and fruitful research results on the local environment.
In addition, the data from this comprehensive survey are planned to be provided as an information service to the public through a website, and the results of the project, such as the status of tidal flats in the Jeonnam region, will be introduced at the Ramsar general meeting held in October.

ko-news-notices-399-8372c75064.title: May, maritime fog peaks... Crash Accident Alert
ko-news-notices-399-8372c75064.text:
May, maritime fog peaks... Crash Accident Alert
2022-03-02
May, maritime fog peaks... Crash Accident Alert
-We ask shipping companies to operate safely, including by adjusting sailing schedules-
According to the May 2008 marine safety forecast released by the Central Maritime Safety Tribunal (President Lee In-su), maritime fog was identified as the biggest accident vulnerability factor in May and requested worker training to prevent accidents during the fog season.
Over the past five years, marine accidents in May include: 63 collisions (28.5%), 53 organ damage (24.0%), 21 strandings (9.5%), 20 fires and explosions (9.0%), 14 casualties (6.3%), and 14 casualties (6.3%). 8 cases (3.7%) ▲Other 34 cases (15.3%).
Collisions during foggy weather have the characteristic of causing significant damage to ships and casualties because they occur after the approaching vessel is discovered late and is in the process of escape action.
The Golden Rose incident, which caused social controversy last year due to a suspected hit-and-run at sea and the loss of 16 lives, also occurred in May.
Vessels passing through foggy areas must slow down to a safe speed, be on thorough alert through radar, and sound a whistle signal. If there is a risk of collision, they must slow down to the minimum speed that can maintain the course.
An official from the umpire said, “During the fog season, retraining of workers on zero-ship navigation is absolutely necessary,” and added, “It would also be helpful to prevent accidents by scheduling sailing companies to ensure that the captain does not overdo it,” and urged shipping companies to operate safely.
In addition, it was found that safety management needs to be strengthened in water leisure boats, guided boats, and fishing boats, which have a high risk of accidents due to the concentration of vacationers in May.

ko-news-notices-398-8372c75064.title: Ye-jong Woo inaugurated as Director General of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency
ko-news-notices-398-8372c75064.text:
Ye-jong Woo inaugurated as Director General of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency
2022-03-02
Ye-jong Woo inaugurated as Director General of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency
On March 21 Ye-jong Woo aged 48 took office as the 32nd Director General of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency.
Woo graduated from Dankook University and passed the 28th Higher Civil Service Examination. He began his public service career in 1985 as an administrative officer in the Port Affairs Bureau of the Korea Maritime and Port Administration. He subsequently served as Head of the Resources Management Division in the Fisheries Resources Bureau of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Head of the International Cooperation Division Planning and Budget Officer and Deputy Head of the Northeast Asian Logistics Hub Planning Task Force. He was also assigned to the Korea National Defense University for national security studies before being appointed Director General of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency under the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs.
In his inaugural address Woo said he would improve the efficiency of the agency's work and strengthen its international competitiveness by actively participating in international activities that produce information meeting global standards.
He also said that growing international concern over global warming and the increasing importance of hydrographic surveying and ocean observation in responding to abnormal weather typhoons earthquakes and other natural disasters made it essential for the agency to do its utmost to support the country's development through the ocean.

ko-news-notices-396-8372c75064.title: The era of marine ubiquitous mobile phones opens
ko-news-notices-396-8372c75064.text:
The era of marine ubiquitous mobile phones opens
2022-03-02
The era of marine ubiquitous mobile phones opens
Establishment of a safety information network for sea users by installing a mobile phone repeater at the lighthouse facility
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced on the 6th that it plans to establish a ubiquitous safety information network by installing mobile phone repeaters at lighthouse facilities to ensure safe sea life anytime and anywhere as the number of marine leisure activities such as small fishing boats, fishing boats, and leisure boats increases.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Safety Management Office (Director Jeon Byeong-jo) announced that it plans to install mobile phone repeaters at lighthouse facilities installed along the coast of the country to improve the safety and convenience of sea users without spending a large budget, so that mobile phone calls can be made even in the sea around the lighthouse. Accordingly, in consultation with mobile carriers such as KTF, LG Telecom, and SKT, we plan to install repeaters in lighthouses and develop waterproof mobile phones.
System configuration diagram
An official from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries said that especially on the west and south coasts, where there are many islands, the tidal range is large and the current is fast, when the sea weather is bad and the mobile phone explodes easily, it is recognized that there is a lighthouse (mobile phone repeater) nearby, which is effective in preventing accidents by encouraging safe navigation of small fishing boats, fishing boats, leisure boats, etc.
In addition, only those who wish can freely receive real-time sea weather information and route information from the manned lighthouse, and if an emergency patient or emergency situation occurs at sea, the manned lighthouse can be used to quickly request emergency patient evacuation or rescue from the Coast Guard.
Plan to expand to callable areas
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries plans to review the installation of repeaters at lighthouse facilities together with mobile communication companies such as KTF, LG Telecom, and SKT and actively promote the project starting this year. By establishing a rapid response system in case of accidents and distress at sea, we plan to contribute to marine traffic safety and marine environment conservation and promote marine safety for sea users.
An official from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries said that the reason for this measure is that in order for sea users to live safely, they need a means to quickly communicate from ship to ship and from ship to land.
In May 2005, when a leisure boat was in distress for 14 hours at sea near Ipado Island on the west coast, killing seven members of a family, lives could have been saved if only they had been able to contact each other via cell phone.
If a dangerous situation such as a safety accident or emergency patient occurs at sea, an easy-to-use and fast communication method must be available.
For now, the only means of communication is mobile phones, which are easily used by all citizens. However, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries explains that currently, calls can only be made within about 20km around land or islands, and cell phones do not work well in the sea far from land, so this measure was prepared to ensure safety at sea.
■Inquiries: Safety Management Office Maritime Transportation Facilities Team Leader Kim Gyu-jin Secretary Seok Young-guk 02-3674-6343 / F 3674-6346

ko-news-notices-395-8372c75064.title: Revised hydrographic surveying service regulations
ko-news-notices-395-8372c75064.text:
Revised hydrographic surveying service regulations
2022-03-02
Revised hydrographic surveying service regulations
Helping local governments resolve maritime boundary disputes
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (President Dong-Hyeon Shim) announced on the 17th that it has revised the Hydrographic Survey Service Regulations, which stipulate marine boundary delimitation surveys to resolve maritime boundary disputes and aerial laser survey methods, the latest survey technology.
Recently, interest in maritime boundaries has increased and disputes are constantly progressing among local governments due to jurisdictional operating rights and permission to collect sea sand due to port development, and surveys of exposed rocks exposed to islands and the sea are difficult to access and take a lot of time, so surveys using aerial laser surveys have been required.
In the revised regulations, the coastline is used as the reference point and the midline as the boundary line in case of disputes over marine boundary demarcation, and accurate location information is provided through GPS surveying. The introduction of aerial laser surveying maximizes work efficiency by stipulating that seawater flooding areas as well as navigation obstacles can be investigated in a short period of time.
In addition, in order to ensure the reliability of marine information and to obtain accurate data, the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency stipulated that the data be acquired by experts using the latest equipment and reviewed by the Korea Oceanographic Survey Association, which has extensive field experience.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “The revised hydrographic survey service regulations establish the basis for providing consumer-centered services by identifying the exact location and facts of the maritime boundary dispute area and stipulating the new technology, aerial laser surveying method.”

ko-news-notices-394-8372c75064.title: Marine Environment Management Corporation established
ko-news-notices-394-8372c75064.text:
Marine Environment Management Corporation established
2022-03-02
Marine Environment Management Corporation established to comprehensively manage the marine environment
The Korea Marine Pollution Control Association expanded its functions and launched on the 21st.
The ‘Korea Marine Pollution Control Association (November 1997)’, which was established as part of the prevention measures following the Sea Prince accident in July 1995, is newly launched as the ‘Marine Environment Management Corporation’ after 11 years.
Based on Article 96 of the Marine Environment Management Act (enacted on January 20, 2008), the Korea Marine Environment Management Corporation has been preparing for its establishment by forming the Corporation Establishment Promotion Committee with the Vice Minister of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries as the chairperson since April 2007 with the vision of ‘leaping forward as an agency specializing in the comprehensive management of the national marine environment’.
The expanded corporation's main tasks include ▲ marine environment conservation, management and improvement projects ▲ marine pollution control projects ▲ marine environment and marine pollution-related technology development and education and training projects. Through the management rationalization of the Marine Pollution Control Association, only 5 people were added, making the total number of employees 485 (3 headquarters, 2 departments, 1 center, 17 teams, 12 national branches).
In relation to the Hebei Spirit oil spill accident, the Corporation decided to skip the grand launch ceremony and hold a simple signboard unveiling ceremony at its office building in Samseong-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul on the 21st, as most of the employees were deployed to the accident site and efforts had to be put into coastal clean-up.
An official from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries said, “As the only organization specializing in marine environment conservation in Korea, the Corporation will create an organization trusted by the public by more faithfully performing professional and efficient pest control tasks that are difficult to perform in the government, local governments, and the private sector.”

ko-news-notices-393-8372c75064.title: Establishment of a long-term plan to restore the Taean oil accident ecosystem
ko-news-notices-393-8372c75064.text:
Establishment of a long-term plan to restore the Taean oil accident ecosystem
2022-03-02
Establishment of a long-term plan to restore the Taean oil accident ecosystem
Domestic and foreign oil pollution experts, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), launch an on-site impact survey
In order to scientifically investigate the damage to the marine and coastal environment caused by the oil accident that occurred off Mallipo, Taean-gun on the 7th and prepare proactive measures, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries urgently formed an expert group to investigate and evaluate the impact of oil pollution accidents, including domestic and foreign experts, to conduct environmental impact studies and prepare a long-term plan for ecosystem restoration.
The domestic expert group assembled around the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute planned to begin fieldwork as soon as possible to assess the environmental impact of the Taean oil spill and prepare a long-term ecosystem restoration plan. It would work closely with three pollution-response specialists from the United States Coast Guard (USCG) and one marine ecosystem specialist from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) who arrived on the 13th. Eight additional specialists in pollution crisis management pollution assessment emergency response and medium- to long-term environmental impact assessment from the European Union (EU) the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) were scheduled to arrive on the 15th.
According to the Marine Environment Management Act, if pollutants exceeding a certain level (100 kℓ or more) are discharged into the sea from a ship, the owner of the ship or marine facility must conduct a marine pollution impact survey through a marine pollution impact survey agency within 3 months from the date of occurrence. However, in this case, a large amount of pollutants were discharged beyond the scale, and the spread of pollutants was causing massive damage to aquaculture facilities, etc., so an investigation into the impact of pollution on the marine environment was urgently conducted by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries in accordance with the relevant exception regulations.
In the case of the Sea Prince oil pollution that occurred in 1995, it was difficult to prove economic loss to the International Oil Pollution Compensation Funds (IOPC Fund) because scientific evidence collection and observations to assess the initial oil pollution impact were not immediately implemented. Based on past experience and the severity of current oil pollution, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries convened domestic experts and held a response meeting as part of emergency measures in the current Hebei Spirit incident.
The results of the on-site impact investigation of the oil pollution accident, which will soon be conducted under the support of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, will be used to scientifically evaluate the actual environmental impact and economic loss in the Taean waters caused by this oil pollution accident, and will be actively used in future IOPC fund compensation claims. It will also be used as basic data to establish and implement a long-term ecosystem restoration plan. In particular, this immediate action by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries can be of great significance in that it has expressed its will to pursue not only scientific pollution impact investigation but also long-term restoration of the marine and coastal ecosystem caused by this incident.

ko-news-notices-392-8372c75064.title: Deep sea water bottled water expected to be released within this year
ko-news-notices-392-8372c75064.text:
Deep sea water bottled water expected to be released within this year
2022-03-02
Deep sea water bottled water expected to be released within this year
2. Promulgation of enforcement ordinance and enforcement rules on the 4th, completion of foundation for full-scale business promotion
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced that the enactment and promulgation of the enforcement ordinance and enforcement rules for the implementation of the ‘Act on Development and Management of Deep Marine Water’ enacted on August 3 last year has been completed and full implementation will begin on the 4th.
The main contents established in the sub-regulations include ▲ rates for deep sea water usage fees and charges ▲ deep sea water intake depth ▲ deep sea water quality standards ▲ detailed standards for license review ▲ deep sea water development business facility standards, etc.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries has completed all institutional foundations in four years since enacting this law in February 2004 to create a new marine industry and contribute to the healthy lives of the people by developing and utilizing deep ocean water, which is called a future resource.
As this law comes into full force, deep ocean water is expected to be used in a variety of fields, from the production of beverages, alcohol, cosmetics, and medicines made from deep ocean water to the development of cold-water fish stocks using deep ocean water and health leisure industries such as spas. Related industries predict that the size of the deep ocean water market will reach 1 trillion won per year within the next five years.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries plans to quickly take the necessary administrative procedures to first receive an application for designation of a water intake area from the relevant mayor or county head by the end of this month, designate a water intake area after review by the Deep Ocean Water Committee, and then issue a deep ocean water development business license within June.

ko-news-notices-391-8372c75064.title: Production and free distribution of portable charts and marine traffic information
ko-news-notices-391-8372c75064.text:
Production and free distribution of portable charts and marine traffic information
2022-03-02
Production and free distribution of portable charts and marine traffic information
Create a portable marine theme map, expected to be used by the general public and marine and fisheries workers
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Shim Dong-hyeon) announced that it will produce portable charts and maritime traffic information maps for new ports and Mokpo Ports, where many ships enter and depart, and distribute them free of charge starting from mid-January.
The portable chart was designed to be foldable and convenient to carry in A3 size, targeting New Port, Sokcho, Daesan, Jeju, and Mokpo Port. Various important information such as tidal data forecasts, port operation regulations, emergency call numbers, and coastal distance tables are displayed on the front, and the corresponding chart is displayed on the back.
In addition, the maritime traffic information map contains information on things to keep in mind when entering and leaving ports, information on the maritime traffic control system, and the domestic marine pollution prevention law for Masan, Yeosu, Gunsan, and Mokpo ports.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “With the distribution of portable charts and maritime traffic information charts, we expect that navigators and marine fisheries workers will be able to easily and conveniently use major port information,” and added, “We plan to produce and distribute various maritime navigation charts to promote user convenience in the future.”
Portable charts and maritime traffic information maps are planned to be distributed free of charge to mariners and maritime and fisheries-related organizations, such as pilot associations and shipping companies. Please contact the Charts Division (032-885-3825).

ko-news-notices-390-8372c75064.title: ‘Encouragement’ and ‘praise’ develop talent.
ko-news-notices-390-8372c75064.text:
‘Encouragement’ and ‘praise’ develop talent.
2022-03-02
‘Encouragement’ and ‘praise’ develop talent.
There is a Korean proverb that says, ‘A word can repay a thousand debts.’ There is also a saying that ‘praise makes even whales dance.’ This means that a simple word can encourage courage and further have the effect of moving a person's heart. In business management, of course, material rewards are important to motivate employees, but warm encouragement and a word of praise often have a great effect in boosting morale.
3M, well known as a representative example of an innovative company, is famous for its management philosophy that emphasizes praise and encouragement as a way to motivate employees to demonstrate spontaneity and creativity. William L. Mcknight, the legendary CEO of 3M in the early days, applauded innovation-oriented employees with the belief, "Management that severely criticizes mistakes when they are made is killing employees' autonomy. Voluntary people are essential for us to continue to grow," and he was generous and generous with encouragement when it came to failures. The unique management philosophies of these past executives made it possible for 3M to grow into the world-class company it is today.
Mental rewards make the other person happy, regardless of the degree. If used well, encouragement and praise can be more effective than material rewards in some cases. Corporate managers and managers should not cover up the mistakes of their subordinates and then reprimand them. Of course, rewards and punishments must be clear, but if you appropriately censure according to the severity of the case and at the same time understand the strengths of subordinates and praise and encourage them appropriately, you will be able to develop employees' potential creativity and promote voluntary innovation efforts. There is a need to re-recognize that the source of a company's competitiveness is ultimately people, and to think about effective motivation measures that will move people's hearts.
Source: Hyundai Economic Research Institute Chairperson Note No. 173

ko-news-notices-389-8372c75064.title: Our future in the 21st century will be created by marine science and technology.
ko-news-notices-389-8372c75064.text:
Our future in the 21st century will be created by marine science and technology.
2022-03-02
Our future in the 21st century is created by marine science and technology.
Contributed by Seoul Economic Rotary ((November 8)
「2013, approximately 2000 km southeast of Hawaii, Onnuri Lake on the Clarion-Clipperton Sea at the deep bottom of the Pacific Ocean. Researchers are working diligently to test a mining system that mines manganese nodules from Korea's single mine located 5,000 meters below the seafloor. A few minutes later, the mining system continues to spit out potato-shaped black nodules. The researchers' faces, covered in sweat, naturally smile brightly.
If the technology is transferred to a private company a few years later and manganese nodules are developed in earnest, it will be possible to develop 3 million tons of manganese nodules per year, containing key strategic metals such as copper, nickel, and cobalt, for about 100 years. Researchers envision this future and are thrilled that their research efforts are bearing fruit.”
This is a scene that always comes to mind and makes me smile when I think about marine science and technology.
View of Onnuri Lake
The ocean is emerging as a treasure trove of future resources that can replace depleting land resources and as a means of survival for humanity that can solve the problem of climate change caused by global warming. Ocean science and technology is a future science and technology that solves the common challenges of humanity in the 21st century and secures sustainable national growth engines through the development of the ocean. Advanced countries around the world are making every effort to secure leadership in the ocean through the development of ocean science and technology.
Korea has expanded investment in marine science and technology since the launch of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries in 1996. As a result, Korea has created visible achievements, such as the construction of the Ieodo Science Base and the development of the world's fourth deep-sea unmanned underwater vehicle with a depth of 6,000 meters. We have laid the foundation for the creation of new marine industries, such as deep ocean water, construction of the world's largest Sihwa Lake tidal power plant, and development of marine biotechnology technology, and secured a 40,000㎢ manganese mine in the open seas of the Pacific Ocean, which is expected to produce strategic metal resources worth 2 trillion won annually. In addition, the development of an icebreaker for polar exploration and a second Antarctic base are also in progress.
Panoramic view of Ieodo Island
“The reason we want to know the sea is not simply out of curiosity, but because our survival depends on the sea.”
This is the message that U.S. President Kennedy sent to Congress in 1961, emphasizing the need for ocean development. It is time to strengthen efforts to develop marine science and technology as a clear blue ocean strategy to prepare for our future and survival.
Kang Moo-hyun, Minister of Oceans and Fisheries

ko-news-notices-388-8372c75064.title: First exploration of the Ulleung Basin in the East Sea by the unmanned submarine ‘Haemirae’
ko-news-notices-388-8372c75064.text:
First exploration of the Ulleung Basin in the East Sea by the unmanned submarine ‘Haemirae’
2022-03-02
First exploration of the Ulleung Basin in the East Sea by the unmanned submarine ‘Haemirae’
Designation of 3 marine animal rescue and treatment institutions... Full treatment of injured animals
‘Haemirae’, the world’s fourth unmanned 6,000m-class underwater vehicle developed after the United States, Japan, and France, will conduct its first exploration activities in the Ulleung Basin in the East Sea.
Shin Pyeong-sik, head of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries' maritime policy division, said in a regular briefing on the morning of the 8th, "The unmanned submarine 'Haemirae' has completed several performance tests and is carrying out full-scale seabed exploration in the 1,500m deep sea in the Ulleung Basin in the East Sea from the 1st to the 12th of this month."
Unmanned submarine ‘Haemirae’ exploration concept diagram
‘Haemirae’ will be aboard the ocean exploration ship ‘Onnuri’ and will be led by a 26-member exploration team, including Dr. Pan-muk Lee of the Korea Ocean Research Institute, to conduct exploration activities such as observing the ecological environment of the Ulleung Basin, collecting seafloor samples, and conducting precise observations of the seafloor topography.
The unmanned underwater vehicle ‘Haemirae’ with a total weight of 3,700 kg is equipped with a robotic arm, various measuring equipment, underwater cameras, and lighting devices.
In particular, ‘Haemirae’ is capable of moving back and forth, left and right, and up and down at a speed of 1.0 to 1.5 knots through six electric propulsors, and is equipped with a location tracking device (USBL) that can track a target within a range of ±5m.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute invested 12 billion won from 2001 to last year to develop the submersible ‘Haemirae’ and the launching device ‘Haenubi’, and have completed performance tests and operational software tests in the East Sea and Pacific Ocean.
‘Haemirae’ will be used in the future to explore cold water and hydrothermal vents in the East Sea and Pacific Ocean, explore underwater resources such as methane hydrate, and research marine ecosystems and new materials.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries also designated three places, including Seoul Grand Park, Haeundae Aquarium in Busan, and Pacific Land in Jeju, as specialized rescue and treatment facilities for marine animals in order to treat injured and stranded marine animals and return them to nature.
Although the number of marine animals injured or stranded is increasing every year due to human activities, there has been no national marine animal rescue or treatment facility, making treatment difficult even when live animals are found.
Major marine animals are expected to include minke whales, common dolphins, finless whales, sickle dolphins, common dolphins, bottlenose dolphins, black killer whales, bottlenose dolphins, harbor seals, fur seals, sea lions, otters, loggerhead turtles, and green sea turtles.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries estimates that 24 cetaceans and 1 to 6 sea turtles are bycaught or stranded on the coast of Korea each year.
In addition, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries is expected to be passive in reporting marine animals due to their economic use value, and in order to create an atmosphere for active reporting and ensure the effectiveness of rescue, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries has decided to consider a plan to pay rewards for reporting live marine animals and helping with rescue treatment.

ko-news-notices-387-8372c75064.title: Dong-Hyeon Shim inaugurated as head of Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency
ko-news-notices-387-8372c75064.text:
Dong-Hyeon Shim inaugurated as head of Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency
2022-03-02
Dong-Hyeon Shim inaugurated as head of Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency
On the 5th, Director Sim Dong-hyeon (50) was inaugurated as the 31st head of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency.
In his inauguration speech, the new director, Shim Dong-hyeon, expressed his inauguration aspiration, saying, “We will promote the direction of increasing international competitiveness by actively participating in international activities that can increase the efficiency of work carried out at our institute and produce information at an international level.”
Since starting his public service as an administrative officer in 1983, Director Shim has served as the head of the General Affairs Department of the Yeosu Regional Maritime and Port Office, the U.S. Seattle Port Authority, the head of the Port Operation Improvement Division of the Bureau of Shipping and Logistics, and the head of the Marine Environment Division of the Marine Policy Bureau. He is an orthodox maritime and fisheries bureaucrat who has held major positions, including recently being dispatched to the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
The new director, Shim, graduated from Jeonju High School and Seoul National University and received a master's degree in law from the same graduate school.
As a family, he has one son and one daughter with his wife Joo Hyeon-hee.

ko-news-notices-386-8372c75064.title: If you want to be good at internal politics...
ko-news-notices-386-8372c75064.text:
If you want to be good at internal politics...
2022-03-02
If you want to be good at internal politics...
Even if you feel disgusted by the behavior of established politicians, you cannot get rid of politics. Whether you like office politics or not, you cannot deny its existence. The mainstream view is that office politics is also a part of competitiveness. The secrets to success in corporate politics revealed in management books and the writings of successful CEOs are very diverse. However, if you group them into large categories, they can be divided into 5 categories.
1. Develop your skills first and then speak
If you are a new employee who has been with the company for less than 5 years, it is better to completely forget about office politics. If you try to reach the line here and there for no reason, you will only end up being talked about. Even if you think you're smart, everyone's lives are similar. In particular, there are many cases where a junior's 'prank' is clearly visible to seniors or department superiors. Mr. Lee (32), an employee at a local company, does not miss out on drinking parties with his seniors. I reported all personnel and new policy information I had heard about to my immediate supervisor. However, the boss, who was so cute, called Mr. Lee and said this before transferring him to another department. “There were a lot of criticisms about when I drink and work all the time. It’s good to hang out with seniors and juniors and build relationships, but first take care of your own business. And from now on, I won’t be able to talk carelessly when I drink with you.”
2. Don’t try to beat your boss.
You can never succeed by turning your back on your boss. To be good at company politics, you need to develop followership, a concept that corresponds to leadership. A follower is different from a yes man or sycophant. It literally means ‘right-hand man’ who assists and keeps the boss in check. Conflict may arise. If the direction of work is different, try to understand your boss's position before criticizing him or her for being ignorant or just selfish. 'Words' can easily lead to misunderstanding depending on the nuance. It is also a good idea to write down work progress, opinions, complaints, etc. by e-mail.
3. Learn conversation skills
It's easy to criticize anyone, but it's difficult to praise someone to the core. Look at the project plan presented by your competitor and do not hesitate to praise the parts that you can truly learn from. After listening sufficiently, give your opinion in a progressive direction. Anyone can criticize something by saying something cannot be done, and it can make oneself look like a complainer. Even when reporting to your superiors, you must clearly understand your tendencies. Report only the key points directly to a boss who is impatient, and report in detail any areas that may be lacking to a boss who only provides general direction.
4. Have a future-oriented mindset.
How do you present alternatives to your boss? There are types who list several alternatives, explain the pros and cons, and then leave the decision to their superiors, and there are types who come up with what they think is the best policy and convince them of the reasons. Usually, bosses like the latter. This is because it gives the impression that the junior is working on this policy with insight and responsibility. In other words, in order to succeed within the company, you must approach each task as if you were the one doing it yourself, that is, with a ‘manager’s mindset’ rather than an ‘office worker’s mindset’. At the same time, you need to reveal the dreams you want to achieve within the company whenever you have the opportunity. When there is a personnel change, superiors naturally think, 'That person would be good for that job.'
5. Raise your juniors
Gil-seon Cho, a business consultant and author of '10 Survival Skills', said, "I have lived with the thought that 15% of my salary is not mine." He gave it to his juniors who needed financial help without hesitation. These people are bound to become their own people who are ‘loyal’. Even in the era of self-PR, it is shameful to talk about one's own achievements. At times like this, juniors call themselves ‘praise trumpeters.’ Even though they are new juniors now, they are the ones who can provide much-needed help when they want to solidify their position as a team leader or manager.
Reporter Kim Soo-yong ksy@msnet.co.kr

ko-news-notices-385-8372c75064.title: Saemangeum reclaimed land produces Dubai oil effect
ko-news-notices-385-8372c75064.text:
Saemangeum reclaimed land produces Dubai oil effect
2022-03-02
“Grunt, growl, rattle”
This is the sound made while building a seawall with rocks using an excavator at the Saemangeum construction site, which is changing the map of Korea.
The water dam construction was completed on April 21 last year, and the seawall construction work is currently in full swing. This seawall connects Daehang-ri, Byeonsan-myeon, Buan-gun, Jeollabuk-do and Bieungdo Island, Gunsan-si.
Exhibition director Park Deok-yeol, who was met by a reporter at the Saemangeum exhibition hall located in Daehang-ri, said, "The seawall is divided into four sections: Unit 1 Daehang-ri ~ Garyok Drain Lock (4.7km), Unit 2 Garyok Drain Lock ~ Shinsi Drain Lock (9.9km), Unit 3 Shinsi Drain Lock ~ Yami Island (2.7km), and Unit 4 Yami Island ~ Bieungdo (11.4km). “It came true,” he explained.
The Saemangeum seawall is 1km longer than the previously longest seawall in the world, the Dutch Juwitherge seawall (32km).
It is 28.7km from section 1 to section 4 seawall, which is shorter than Jwiwideoji, but including the two drain locks of 660m and the 3km section of Bieungdo Island that Gunsan City is constructing itself, it is longer than Jwiwideoji.
Currently, only the Unit 1 seawall (4.7km) and the power drainage lock completed by Daewoo Engineering & Construction are receiving visitors. The new city drain lock, which has already been completed, and the seawalls for Units 2, 3, and 4, which are under construction, are expected to be opened to the public only at the end of 2009.
Director Park accompanied the group from the control area, Unit 2's seawall section, to the Bieungdo section.
Currently, construction of the outer and inner seawalls is underway simultaneously in all sections of the Saemangeum seawall, excluding the Unit 1 seawall. Black muddy water was gushing out through large iron pipes in various places where the inner seawall construction was in progress.
Director Park explained, "Saemangeum is reclaimed with sand dredged from the sea. When a dredger flows dredged soil from the sea outside the seawall through a large pipe, water mixed with sandy soil comes out from the pipe extending to the inside. The water is drained, and only the sand and soil are used to build a seawall and reclaim reclaimed land."
14.3 million 15-ton dump trucks worth of earth and sand were used to build the seawall alone. These soils are enough to build the Gyeongbu Expressway (416km from Seoul to Busan) at a height of 7m.
The project team is distributing seawater to the reclaimed land and regularly draining water through 18 Garyok and Sinsi drainage locks (36 floodgates). One lock gate, which is 30m wide, 15m high, and weighs 484 tons, discharges 8,812 tons of water per second, or 7,050 tons of water per second.
Once the water drainage work is completed, Saemangeum reclaimed land (40,100 ha = 28,300 ha of land + 11,800 ha of freshwater lake), equivalent to 66% of the area of ​​Seoul in 2011, will be created and will be developed sequentially until 2030.
According to Director Park, the corporation plans to complete development in the Dongjin River area, which has relatively good water quality, by 2020 after land development work, and in the Mangyeong River area by 2030 after securing water quality standards while maintaining seawater distribution.
The reclaimed land is based on the principle of eco-friendly development. Accordingly, reclaimed farmland, which is more environmentally friendly than other industries, accounts for 56.9% of the total land area. Director Park explained that although only 6.6% was allocated to industrial complexes, the remainder satisfies domestic industrial demand.
Director Park said, "This is a reclaimed land that prioritizes eco-friendliness. Unlike Sihwa Lake, which is known to be a failed reclamation project, we have thoroughly established environmental measures. We will continue to supplement any shortcomings and devise countermeasures in the future."
In particular, in the case of the Saemangeum reclaimed land, water quality is managed by dividing it into three sections: the Dongjin and Mangyeong River basins, freshwater lakes within the reclaimed land, and seawater outside the seawall.
Just as Director Park said that land and water resources can have as much economic effect as Dubai's oil resources, it appears that it will not be long before the Saemangeum reclaimed land will be transformed into fertile soil that will create the 'new Mangeum' of the 21st century.
Gogunsan Islands seen from the Sinsi Baeryeok Gate.

When a dredger flows dredged soil into a large pipe from the sea outside the seawall, water mixed with sandy soil comes out from the pipe extending to the inside. The water is drained, and only the sand and soil are used to build seawalls and reclaim reclaimed land. The photo shows the construction site of the Unit 2 seawall being built by Hyundai Engineering & Construction.

ko-news-notices-384-8372c75064.title: Han River Estuary, starting with joint investigation between South and North Korea
ko-news-notices-384-8372c75064.text:
Han River Estuary, starting with joint investigation between South and North Korea
2022-03-02
As a result of the inter-Korean summit, the possibility of developing the Han River basin has increased. The Grand National Party and the Unified New Democratic Party also announced the development of the Han River Estuary and the Grand Canal Project as pledges. Candidate Lee Myung-bak proposed the construction of an artificial island measuring 29.75 million square meters (9 million pyeong) northeast of Gyodong Island, Ganghwa-gun, at the mouth of the Han River as a pledge project. Candidate Lee Hae-chan made a pledge that if the sand deposited at the mouth of the Han River, where the Han River and Imjin River meet, is scooped up and used as construction material, repeated flooding can be prevented and logistics costs can be reduced through the canal between Kaesong and Paldang.
However, the two people do not know much about the Han River. There is a tidal difference of about 10m at the mouth of the Han River. One person only sees the flooding of the Han River estuary during high tide, and the other only sees the tidal flats during low tide.
The Han River Estuary has a basin area of ​​38,665㎢. Rainwater collects in 17.4% of the area of ​​the Korean Peninsula and forms the Namhan River, Bukhangang River, Imjin River, and Yeseong River and joins at the estuary, and 70% of it is discharged concentrated during the flood season. Water is a resource comparable to oil. By creating a freshwater lake by blocking the seawall, a large amount of water can be secured for industrial use, wide tidal flats and high-quality soil, as well as estuary flooding can be prevented. However, artificial islands cause flooding.
The potential of the Han River Estuary lies in its potential to grow into a new base for the Northeast Asian economy. Following Japan's Tokyo in the 1960s, Seoul in the 1970s, China's Pearl River Estuary Special Economic Zone in the 1980s, Shanghai Pudong at the Yangtze River Estuary in the 1990s, and the Yellow River Estuary and Bohai Bay in the 2000s, the Korean Peninsula should become a growth base for Northeast Asia in the 2010s. The key to developing the Han River estuary is not local flood prevention, river aggregates, or artificial islands. The key is how to maximize its potential and become a growth base in Northeast Asia.
By blocking the seawall at the mouth of the Han River, abundant water resources and vast tidal flats can be used to develop peace industrial complexes, free trade zones, new cities, and hub ports necessary for the industrialization of a unified Korean Peninsula. Inter-Korean economic cooperation is important by developing the potential of the Han River estuary to achieve competitiveness that surpasses Japan and China. For the Han River Estuary, it is most important for South and North Korea to cooperate to verify economic feasibility and reach an agreement to establish a new economic system. Rather than hasty development projects, we must first conduct a joint research study on the potential and development needs of the Han River Estuary.
Source: JoongAng Ilbo, October 10, 2007
Gwangnam Kim, CEO of Construction Business Management Research Institute

ko-news-notices-383-8372c75064.title: Completed hydrographic survey of major ports on the East Coast
ko-news-notices-383-8372c75064.text:
Completed hydrographic survey of major ports on the East Coast
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency's Donghae Oceanographic Survey Office (Director Kim Jeong-gi) announced that it has completed the hydrographic survey of Donghae Port, Samcheok Port, and Ulsan (Mipo) Port, which began last April.
This survey area is a major port on the east coast where large ships frequently pass, and is a sea area where up-to-date seafloor topography data is required.
As a result of the hydrographic survey, the water depth distribution of Donghae Port was not significantly different from the existing one, and the water depth near Chuam was distributed between 24 and 27 m, but due to the dropping of artificial reefs, a shallow water depth of 18 m was found. In addition, it was revealed that the water depth of 4.6m that existed near the southern port entrance and exit of Ulsan (Mipo) Port was changed to 9.1m through dredging.
An official from the Korea Maritime Research Institute said, “It is expected that the results of this hydrographic survey will be quickly reflected on charts and used as basic data needed for port management and operation and marine development as well as securing maritime traffic safety by providing the latest information.”

ko-news-notices-382-8372c75064.title: KHOA supports marine disaster prevention in developing countries
ko-news-notices-382-8372c75064.text:
KHOA supports marine disaster prevention in developing countries
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced on the 28th of last month that it had dispatched a marine observation expert to Indonesia to transfer advanced technologies for preventing marine disasters.
This dispatch was promoted through cooperation with the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) as part of Korea's free foreign aid program (ODA) to support recovery from the tsunami that hit the Indonesian island of Sumatra in December 2004, and the dispatched experts plan to develop their capabilities to minimize marine-related disasters in Indonesia through technology transfer on marine observation technology and the establishment of a tsunami forecast system for three months.
Through this support, Korea will be a good opportunity to promote friendship with Indonesia, which is a regular member of the International Hydrographic Organization (IHO) and the East Asian Hydrographic Commission (EAHC), as well as to strengthen its status in the international community. An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “The Malacca Sea area near Indonesia is an important international shipping route through which our country's ships pass, and this dispatch provides an opportunity to kill two birds with one stone by not only cultivating Indonesia's maritime technology capabilities but also conducting fact-finding surveys of major shipping routes. “It will happen,” he said.

ko-news-notices-381-8372c75064.title: Next year’s tidal forecast for the Korean coast announced
ko-news-notices-381-8372c75064.text:
Next year’s tidal forecast for the Korean coast announced
2022-03-02
Next year’s tidal forecast for the Korean coast announced
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency predicts 52 coastal areas
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (President Yeon Young-jin) announced the results of predicting high and low tide times and heights for 2008 for 52 coastal areas, including major ports such as Busan Port, Incheon Port, and Mokpo Port, and Ieodo Ocean Science Station.
According to the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency, high tide levels will occur in July, August, and September next year, and the highest tide levels of the year are expected to occur around July 3-5 (June 1-3 in the lunar calendar) and August 1-3 (July 1-3 in the lunar calendar).
The highest tide level by major region on the west coast is 935cm in Incheon (August 3, October 16), 947cm in Pyeongtaek (August 3), 736cm in Gunsan Outer Port (August 3), 512cm in Mokpo (July 4), and 146cm in Busan (August 1, 2) on the south coast, and 223cm in Masan (August). 2nd), 294cm in Jeju (July 3rd), and 290cm in Ieodo (June 4th).
Meanwhile, the predicted highest tide level can vary greatly depending on weather conditions such as wind and barometric pressure, and sea levels may rise significantly between July and September when bad weather such as typhoons frequently occur, so special caution is expected in low-lying areas.
In particular, next year's tide forecast includes 4 new tidal observation stations (Janghang, Jindo, Goheung, and Geoje Island), up from 47 in previous years, and 1 Ieodo Station, which has been managed and operated since 2007.
The results of this tidal forecast will be included in the Korean Coastal ‘Tide Table’ published by the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency and sold at hydrographic book stores nationwide (inquiries: 02-701-9981) in early September, and will also be serviced through the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency website (www.nori.go.kr).

ko-news-notices-380-8372c75064.title: Signs of abnormal water quality upstream of Saemangeum
ko-news-notices-380-8372c75064.text:
Signs of abnormal water quality upstream of Saemangeum
2022-03-02
‘Signs of abnormality’ in water quality upstream of Saemangeum
Despite the operation of the Jeonju Advanced Sewage Treatment Facility, the effect is minimal.
While Jeonbuk Province is pursuing various water quality improvement projects to secure water quality in the upper Saemangeum basin, recent water quality measurements in the Mangyeong River revealed that ‘anomaly signs’ were being detected, putting Jeonbuk Province on alert to prepare countermeasures such as cause analysis.
Construction of the Jeonju Advanced Sewage Treatment Facility to perfectly treat the sewage flowing into the Mangyeong River has been completed and is currently in test operation. However, the water quality of the Mangyeong River appears to be declining, calling for a detailed diagnosis of the Saemangeum water quality management system in the future.
According to Jeonbuk Province on the 18th, a water quality survey was conducted to analyze the effect of the Jeonju Advanced Sewage Treatment Facility, which has been in test operation since October of last year, on improving the water quality of the Mangyeong River, which is closely related to securing Saemangeum water quality.
However, the water quality survey results show data that is difficult to understand, and even provincial officials are divided on the cause analysis.
With the operation of the advanced sewage treatment facility, the quality of water discharged from the treatment plant improved from 12ppm BOD before operation to 5.5ppm after operation.
The water quality of Jeonju Stream, where discharged water flows, also decreased from 9.0 ppm to 6.6 ppm, showing that water quality is improving due to advanced sewage treatment facilities.
However, the water quality of the Mangyeong River (near Samrye, Wanju-gun), where Jeonju Stream water with improved BOD flows, was measured to have increased BOD from 5.0ppm to 6.0ppm.
There are conflicting opinions internally regarding the water quality survey results, which do not make sense through common sense.
While there is a view that there may be factors that deteriorate water quality between the points where Jeonju Stream water joins the Mangyeong River, a total of 7 projects currently being promoted to improve water quality in the upper Saemangeum basin, including advanced sewage treatment facilities (26, 4 completed, 22), sewage pipes, Wanggung livestock wastewater treatment facility private investment reinforcement project, individual livestock manure, improvement of natural rivers, and reduction of non-point pollutants through continuous promotion of eco-friendly agriculture, have not been completed temporarily. There is also a view that it is a phenomenon.
In order to analyze the exact cause of these water quality survey results, the province plans to conduct a field investigation by experts from the Environmental Countermeasures Committee under the Office for Government Policy Coordination next month and devise countermeasures.
Reporter Nam Hyeong-jin
2007-09-18 21:14:58

ko-news-notices-379-8372c75064.title: Arctic Ocean sea ice intercontinental Arctic sea route opened
ko-news-notices-379-8372c75064.text:
Arctic Ocean sea ice intercontinental Arctic sea route opened
2022-03-02
It has been found that as the ice in the Arctic Ocean melts due to global warming, close shipping routes between continents are opening up.
The European Space Agency announced that, based on satellite observations, the Arctic sea ice off the coasts of Canada and Alaska is melting, making it possible for ships to travel along the Northwest Passage connecting Europe and Asia.
Japan's Sankei Shimbun also reported that the Northeast Passage, which passes through the Arctic Ocean off the coast of Russia, has partially opened as the ice has melted.
Accordingly, Sankei reported that once the two routes are fully opened, the route connecting Asia, Northern Europe, and the eastern coast of the United States is expected to be shortened by about half of the current route.
[International] Reporter Hong Ji-myeong

ko-news-notices-376-8372c75064.title: Gore says ExxonMobil and other energy companies fund research disputing global warming
ko-news-notices-376-8372c75064.text:
Gore says ExxonMobil and other energy companies fund research disputing global warming
2022-03-02
Former U.S. Vice President Al Gore claimed on the 7th that large energy companies such as ExxonMobil are funding research that contradicts the scientific consensus on global warming in order to mislead the public.
ExxonMobil immediately issued a rebuttal statement.
At an environmental conference held in Singapore, former Vice President Gore criticized, "Some of the world's largest carbon-emitting companies have been disbursing $10 million a year in funds to systematically create the impression that there is controversy within the scientific community about warming."
He argued that warming is a topic on which the strongest consensus has been reached in the history of science, and that the move to overturn this is the same as the American tobacco companies investing large sums of money to create the impression that there is uncertainty and controversy within the scientific community regarding the harmful effects of smoking.
After the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change released a large-scale report last February pointing out and warning that global warming is a man-made disaster, former Vice President Gore criticized, saying, "Those who deny this offered a $10,000 incentive for each article that raised controversy in the UN report," and added, "They are trying to manipulate public opinion and treat us as fools."
He also emphasized that China, which will become the world's largest greenhouse gas emitter next year, should not be excluded from greenhouse gas reduction obligations because it is technically a developing country, and that China should skip technologies that pollute the environment and find ways to maintain growth.
Meanwhile, a spokesperson for ExxonMobil said in a statement that the company's research funding was not intended to influence research, and that repeatedly raising groundless conspiracy theories was ignoring the realistic task of "how to supply the energy needed to improve living standards while reducing greenhouse gas emissions."
Last year, US and British scientists accused ExxonMobil of providing funding to groups that overturn the scientific consensus on climate change. (Singapore AP=Yonhap News)

ko-news-notices-375-8372c75064.title: 2017 Korea
ko-news-notices-375-8372c75064.text:
2017 Korea
2022-03-02
What will our society look like in 2017? Anyone who wants to look ahead to the next 10 years can draw an overall picture by looking at what changes we and society have experienced over the past 10 years, that is, over the 10 years since 1997, when the foreign exchange crisis hit.
There are a lot of stories about rapid change or a rapidly changing environment, but it would be more correct to imagine a gradually changed future that is fully predictable rather than a drastically changed future that is disconnected from the present. No one can accurately predict the future, but in this article, we will carefully summarize important trends that can characterize the future based on the present.
First, the impact of changes in population composition on the growth rate of the Korean economy will become increasingly clear. In other words, a decline in the potential growth rate will not be avoidable, and the Korean economy is expected to gradually lose dynamism, and the variables that have the greatest impact on this can be found in the increase in the elderly population and the decrease in the productive population.
At the end of 2006, the Korea Development Institute published a report titled ‘Economic and Social Ripple Effects of Aging Population Structure and Response Tasks.’ This report forecasts Korea's potential growth rate from 2003 to 2050, predicting that Korea will continue to transform into a low-growth country with 2.91% in the 2020s, 1.60% in the 2030s, and 0.74% in the 2040s. Considering that the potential growth rate in the 2010s was 4%, the growth rate is expected to drop to almost zero percent over the next 30 years.
Of course, there are variables depending on the increasing trend of immigration, unification of the Korean Peninsula, and the direction of institutional reform, but it seems inevitable that the potential growth rate will gradually decline over the next 10 years. In Korean society, the number of the first baby mover generation from 1958 to 1962 was as many as 5 million. In 2015 and 2020, when their retirement becomes a fait accompli, the proportion of the population aged 65 or older will increase to 12.9% and 15.6%, respectively. On the other hand, the number of people over 14 years old falls to 13.7% and 12.4%, respectively. Considering that last year's population over 65 years old and under 14 years old accounted for 9.5% and 18.6%, respectively, we can understand the overall outline of the population composition, and this will be the decade in which we see the impact of this trend on the economic growth rate becoming visible.
Second, the rapid growth of China's economic power will have an impact on all aspects of Korean society, and the impact on manufacturing will be especially evident. The future is currently in progress. The 10 years that the Korean manufacturing industry will face can be inferred from the following article by Beijing-based correspondent Heo Min, which reports on the recent status of the Chinese automobile industry.
“Ultra-cheap Chinese compact cars costing around 6 million won per unit will enter the U.S. market starting in 2008. Although they are made with American technology and are much better in quality than existing Chinese cars, they are cheap cars made using cheap labor, so there is a high possibility that they will become ‘Korean car killers.’” Tom Lasorda, president of Chrysler, the third-largest automaker in the U.S., met with Yin Tongyao, chairman of Qirui, China’s No. 1 domestic automaker, in Beijing on July 4. “An agreement on joint development of small cars was signed and Chirui Motors also signed an export contract with the European market.”
Many manufacturing companies that make and sell mediocre products at mediocre prices will experience difficulties and be caught up in the midst of restructuring. Localization strategies, such as moving manufacturing companies to China, India, and other third countries for survival, are expected to gain further momentum. As a result, unless special circumstances develop, it appears that it will become increasingly difficult to significantly reduce the growth rate and unemployment rate in Korean society. This is expected to further worsen the employment situation for young people who do not have special skills or knowledge and have difficulty finding jobs in overseas markets, and this phenomenon itself is expected to further worsen the phenomenon of low growth and high unemployment.
The automobile industry is a symbolic sector of Korean manufacturing. I believe that the automobile industry suggests the future that Korea's manufacturing industry will face. Fortunately, if a groundbreaking change can occur in labor-management relations, the situation may be reversed, but as long as the current situation continues, the sandwich situation and crisis theory in the Korean manufacturing industry is likely to receive further strength.
On the other hand, the biggest beneficiaries of Chinese industry will be Korean consumers. Korean consumers are expected to enjoy the positive effects of cheap Chinese products.
Third, it is highly likely that society as a whole will experience an increased sense of crisis and an awakening to innovation in the next 10 years. Therefore, if Korea succeeds in choosing a leader who properly reads the changes of the times and has the driving force, Korea can succeed in an unexpected change and innovation project. This may serve as a variable that can greatly improve the situation in Korea.
Crisis situations do not always provide only negative aspects. On the contrary, the difficulties brought about by mediocre product production will greatly highlight the need for innovation in Korean society as a whole to overcome this situation, and this will bring about the strengthening of innovation capabilities such as institutional reform and reform of the atmosphere for improved productivity and creative ideas in various fields such as politics, economy, society and culture.
In particular, there will be a strong need to reform the education system to foster creative talent, and it is expected that some visible results will be achieved. The variable that will have the greatest impact on these changes will be the ever-increasing number of overseas students, not only elementary, middle, and high school students, but also college students, who will contribute to the reform of Korea's education system. It appears that Korean education will change as education demand voters' active voting will bring about a movement for change and innovation, and politicians will accept these demands.
If the reform of the education system that enables the training of creative talent succeeds and the innovation movement across society achieves results, there is still an opportunity to offset the decline in potential growth rate. The direction of institutional reform will also play an important role in determining Korea's shape over the next 10 years, and the choice of political leaders can be said to be decisive. Since the future is not just given but something to be created, it can be said that the selection of leaders relies heavily on the wisdom shown by Koreans.
Fourth, Korean companies will be encouraged to expand overseas, and it is expected that a significant number of companies will emerge that are achieving outstanding results. The exploration of overseas markets by companies will spread not only to large corporations but also to small and medium-sized companies, and the number of companies that have been tested for their capabilities in the domestic market, not only in the manufacturing industry but also in the service industry, is expected to significantly increase in the number of companies that succeed as global players. More than any other sector of Korean society, we can give generous scores to the survival and growth capabilities of Korean companies.
Fifth, the remarkable growth of the financial industry will become another trend that will characterize the next 10 years. The Korean financial industry, which has played a role as an auxiliary to the manufacturing industry, is expected to achieve great growth thanks to institutional reforms such as the Capital Consolidation Act based on the bitter experience of the foreign exchange crisis, and some companies are expected to achieve great results in pioneering overseas markets. The growth of the financial industry means that the financial industry itself can occupy an important position in creating added value. In particular, the emergence of a financial industry that achieves outstanding results in the asset management field will greatly contribute to the creation of added value for investors. In any case, Korea's financial industry will be a case in which we can once again see how much success Koreans can achieve when given autonomy.
In addition to the conclusion of the Korea-U.S. Free Trade Agreement, the arena in which Koreans can operate will be greatly expanded as agreements with Europe, ASEAN, Japan, and China are partially concluded in the future. If the spirit of the times, such as autonomy, creativity, openness, and challenge, can once again occupy the center of Korean society, Koreans will be able to erase the sluggishness of the past and lay the foundation for a leap forward. We believe that the future is not given, but created by ourselves.
Source: Gong Byeong-ho Research Institute, Dr. Gong Byeong-ho, July 2007

ko-news-notices-374-8372c75064.title: 10 East Sea undersea place names registered with the International Geographical Names Subcommittee
ko-news-notices-374-8372c75064.text:
10 East Sea undersea place names registered with the International Geographical Names Subcommittee
2022-03-02
10 East Sea undersea place names registered with the International Geographical Names Subcommittee
‘Jeon Jae-gyu’s disbandment’ name also registered in international organizations
Ten undersea place names in the East Sea are registered after passing the Undersea Place Names Subcommittee.
The government announced on the 11th that at the 20th Subcommittee on Undersea Place Names (SCUFN), which has been held in Monaco since the 9th, it was confirmed that all 10 Korean-style East Sea undersea place names that Korea applied for on the 10th of last month would be successfully registered.
In addition, by hosting the 21st SCUFN (Subcommittee on Undersea Place names) meeting to be held in the first half of next year, Korea is expected to strengthen its international status by expanding its influence in registering additional undersea place names in the future.
The East Sea place names registered by the Undersea Places Subcommittee this time include ‘Gangwon Plateau’, ‘Ulleung Plateau’, ‘Usan Break’, ‘Usan Undersea Cliff’, ‘Onnuri Basin’, ‘Saenal Basin’, ‘Hupotoe’, ‘Kim In-woo Sea Mountain’, ‘I Gyu-won Sea Mountain’, and ‘Anyongbok Sea Mountain’.
This is the first time that an undersea place name in the East Sea has been registered in an international organization in our own style since the international registration process began in 1974, and it is expected that it will become an opportunity for it to be registered in the International Book of Undersea Place Names and be widely used as a standard in the international community.
The government also announced that an undersea place name named after the late Jeon Jae-gyu, who died in an unexpected shipwreck in Maxwell Bay while conducting research at the Sejong Station in Antarctica in 2003, will also be registered.
The name is ‘Jeon Jae-gyu Seamount’, and this seamount was first discovered by an American geological research team (Dr. E. Domack, professor at Hamilton University), established by the American Undersea Geographical Names Committee last year, and now registered with an international organization.
Using this registration as an opportunity, the government plans to continue to discover and establish undersea place names in Korean waters and to promote more Korean place names to be used internationally through additional applications.
■Inquiries: Maritime Law Team Leader Gyeong-gyu Lee, Secretary Jin Jun-ho (☎02-3674-6522) / joon469@momaf.go.kr
