ko-news-notices-362-8372c75064.title: Two plans for Busan North Port redevelopment master plan compressed
ko-news-notices-362-8372c75064.text:
Two plans for Busan North Port redevelopment master plan compressed
2022-03-02
The Busan North Port redevelopment master plan has been prepared as ‘Plan 1’, which focuses on securing waterfront space and views, and ‘Plan 2’, which focuses on expanding commercial functions, and will be subject to public opinion survey by Busan citizens.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the Busan Port Authority (BPA) held a 'Busan North Port Master Plan Amendment Briefing Session' on the afternoon of the 11th and announced the redevelopment direction focusing on these contents. Prior to this, the government reaffirmed the principle of “promoting an eco-friendly plan that maximizes the use of existing docks and minimizes sea reclamation.”
The revised master plan released on this day decided to exclude the international exchange, commercial, and business districts, including high-rise buildings, proposed in the existing master plan from the first stage (Piers 1 to 4, Central Pier) redevelopment plan starting next year, and instead include them in the second stage Jaseongdae Pier redevelopment plan to begin in 2020.
Plan 1 focuses on expanding waterfront space, and plan 2 focuses on expanding commercial functions.
First, ‘Plan 1’ is a medium-low density development plan that minimizes landfill by creating a deck-type waterfront space on the central pier connected to Busan Station and creating an island-style landmark in the form of an artificial island. In particular, of the 1.42 million ㎡ of the redevelopment district, public land including waterfront spaces is 1.03 million ㎡ (73%), which is 12% more than the existing plan's 870,000 ㎡ (61%), while the reclaimed area is 557,000 ㎡, smaller than the existing plan (624,000 ㎡) to enable environmentally friendly development.
‘Plan 2’ is a plan that takes commercial functions into consideration, and plans to place a ‘multiple port district’ ​​that integrates the Nampo-dong commercial district, commercial business district, and port functions on Pier 2, and use Pier 2 as a cruise terminal. It was decided to leave the front of Piers 3 and 4 as a development reserve so that it can be developed into a maritime cultural district in the future.
The total project cost was estimated to be 7.99 trillion won (KRW 1.51 trillion in infrastructure costs) for plan 1, and 8.17 trillion won (KRW 1.53 trillion in infrastructure costs) for plan 2.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and BPA plan to provide sufficient data and information on these two plans to those surveyed within this month, then collect public opinion through a public opinion survey, finalize the redevelopment plan, and begin the project within next year after announcing the basic plan and drafting a business plan in September.
Lee Jae-gyun, head of the Port Redevelopment Promotion Planning Group of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, said on this day, “The existing master plan announced at the end of last year had problems such as blocking sea views and access opportunities, but this plan has been prepared as an environmentally friendly plan by improving these problems.” He added, “We plan to collect a wide range of citizen opinions to ensure that the North Port redevelopment project is promoted without a hitch.”
Seongwon Ahn (witgen21@korea.kr)

ko-news-notices-361-8372c75064.title: Development of a marine survey information system based on marine GIS
ko-news-notices-361-8372c75064.text:
Development of a marine survey information system based on marine GIS
2022-03-02
Providing convenient and rapid marine geographical information services by building digital marine information
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (President Yeon Young-jin) announced that starting this month, it has begun developing a marine geographic information system (GIS) that links the vast amount of data obtained through marine surveys with digital maps to create a database.
Marine GIS is a system that conveniently and quickly provides various marine geographical information by linking various information related to the sea with location information, creating a spatial database, and constructing GIS. It is used for marine policy, marine development and use, navigation safety, and national defense affairs.
The Korea Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency has been working on establishing marine GIS from 2001 to 2006, and this project is a second-stage improvement project to be carried out until 2010, and plans to invest 1.1 billion won this year to build an integrated database of vast marine survey information.
In addition, we plan to convert marine place names into a database and build a database for paper charts and original maps that have not been digitized.
In particular, a basic marine GIS for the seabed topography of the East Sea region will be established, detailed information on the seabed topography of the sea, coast, and port will be accumulated, and a national marine basic GIS management program containing information such as seabed topography and coastline will also be developed.
Meanwhile, the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency is running an open contest for a brand for the ocean research information system through the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency's website (www.nori.go.kr) until the 22nd of this month.
It must be a unique and easily memorable brand while pursuing the image of a world-class digital advanced marine research information, and we plan to select one person each for Best, Excellence, and 10 lucky winners on the 30th of this month to award awards.

ko-news-notices-360-8372c75064.title: Geographical information of the sea and land at a glance
ko-news-notices-360-8372c75064.text:
Geographical information of the sea and land at a glance
2022-03-02
Started production of port basic map
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced that it has begun production of port maps for Mokpo and Donghae Ports, which contain various geographical information of the sea and land.
The port basic map is a drawing that contains information such as land topography and features shown on the map, detailed water depth of the seabed shown on the chart, various port geographical information, coastline, maritime boundaries, tides, currents, etc. in a systematic and scientific manner, making it possible to view various geographical information at a glance.
In order to build a marine geographic information base for Korea's jurisdictional waters, the Korea Maritime Research Institute has produced and distributed port basic maps for 17 trade ports, including Incheon Port, Busan, Gwangyang, and Ulsan, starting in 2001.
We plan to complete the production of basic maps for Korea's 28 trade ports, 51 coastal ports, and coastal waters by 2010.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “The port basic map is expected to be used as important data to support marine and fisheries policies such as port operation, marine development, and marine environment conservation,” and added, “By linking it with the currently underway National Geographic Information System (NGIS) construction project, it will contribute to the implementation of e-government by completing a digital national land where the sea and land become one.”

ko-news-notices-359-8372c75064.title: Publication of new charts in and around the South Sea of ​​Korea
ko-news-notices-359-8372c75064.text:
Publication of new charts in and around the South Sea of ​​Korea
2022-03-02
Reflects the latest water depth information from Busan Port to Mokpo Port and Jeju Island
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced that it has published a new chart reflecting the latest water depth information for the waters around Mokpo Port and Jeju Island from Busan Port to ensure safe navigation of ships.
The new chart (scale 1/500,000) lists territorial sea limits, straight baselines, specific sea areas, and fisheries resource protection zones. It is expected to greatly contribute to safe navigation as it contains various up-to-date information such as seabed depth necessary for safe navigation of vessels engaged in fishing activities in coastal waters of Korea.
The newly published chart (chart number S-No. 418) was published based on the results of a survey of the seabed topography of the sea area around Jeju Island, covering 31,000 ㎢, using the 700-ton marine research vessel “Badaro No. 1” equipped with cutting-edge hydrographic survey equipment such as shallow sea exploration equipment (EM3000) and deep sea exploration equipment (EM300).
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “We plan to quickly produce and distribute the latest charts for Korea’s coastal waters to ensure maritime traffic safety.”
Charts can be purchased through a chart sales agency (☎02-701-9981, 051-466-0760) or through the company's Internet website (www.chartkorea.com).

ko-news-notices-358-8372c75064.title: East Sea water temperature rises by 0.06 degrees every year
ko-news-notices-358-8372c75064.text:
East Sea water temperature rises by 0.06 degrees every year
2022-03-02
Coastal sea levels have risen by 3.2 mm per year over the past 30 years.
It was found that the surface water temperature of the East Sea has increased by about 2℃ over the past 100 years. Additionally, it was found that over the past 30 years, the sea level along Korea's coast has risen by 3.2 mm per year.
Lee Jae-hak, director of the Korea Ocean Research & Development Institute's Marine Climate Change Research Center, announced the results of the ‘Study on the Mid- to Long-Term Fluctuation Response of the East Sea Due to Climate Change’ focusing on these details at the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries on the 28th.
According to research results, since the surface water temperature of the East Sea increased in the 1940s, there has been a large increase of 0.06℃ every year since the mid-1980s.
Unlike in the 1940s, when water temperature rise was limited to winter, water temperature is now rising regardless of the season, and this phenomenon is especially noticeable in the northwestern waters of the East Sea.
In addition, it was found that the water temperature is rising not only along the East Sea coast, but also inside the sea level, and the thermal expansion effect caused by changes in sea water temperature was found to be the biggest cause.
In addition, it was found that sea levels along the coasts of Korea and Japan have risen by 3.2 mm per year over the past 30 years.
In particular, it has risen 6.5mm per year over the past 9 years and 6.4mm over the past 14 years, showing a high rate of increase since the 1990s, and this has been maintained until recently.
This rise in water temperature and sea level is higher than the average value of global ocean change (water temperature about 0.04℃/year, sea level 3.1mm/year), meaning that the seas around Korea are responding greatly to climate change.
According to recent research results at home and abroad, the East Sea has a clear tendency for long-term fluctuations to the extent that changes can be detected not only in the depths but also in the surface layer, and recent changes in the marine ecosystem support this cause.
Director Lee said, “It is necessary to prepare mid- to long-term national policies to prevent disasters such as coastal flooding, coastal erosion, and port flooding due to marine climate change, and to respond to changes in the marine ecosystem and fish farm environment,” and added, “In particular, it is urgent to prepare a response to marine change by presenting a national standard marine change scenario.”

ko-news-notices-357-8372c75064.title: Opening of Janghang Port marine research vessel and tide observatory in commemoration of Ocean Day
ko-news-notices-357-8372c75064.text:
Opening of Janghang Port marine research vessel and tide observatory in commemoration of Ocean Day
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency's West Sea Ocean Research Office (Director Jeong Hyeon) opens its oceanographic research vessel and tide station to celebrate Ocean Day.
The West Sea Ocean Research Office has decided to open the ocean research vessel Hwanghae Ro (77 tons) and the Janghang Port Tide Observatory at Janghang Port on the 31st in order to increase understanding of the ocean to students and the general public.
On this day, citizens will be able to see the latest navigation equipment such as automatic navigation devices and electronic chart systems installed on ships, as well as cutting-edge marine research equipment and facilities such as multi-acoustic sounding and undersea obstacle detectors that can three-dimensionally explore the undersea terrain and find obstacles, giving them a variety of experiences in the field of marine surveys.
In addition, at the Janghang Port Tide Observatory, you can realistically experience the principles of rising and falling sea water through a tour of tide observation equipment and an introduction to the real-time tide information service system.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “We have opened the research vessel to inform the general public about the importance of the sea and to provide an opportunity for young people to develop an enterprising maritime spirit.” He added, “Visitors will have a variety of experiences about ocean research.”
Individuals and groups wishing to participate in the event may apply to the West Sea Ocean Research Office (041-956-2010).

ko-news-notices-356-8372c75064.title: Precision hydrographic survey of major ports on the west coast
ko-news-notices-356-8372c75064.text:
Precision hydrographic survey of major ports on the west coast
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency's West Sea Survey Office (Director Jeong Hyeon) announced that it will conduct precise hydrographic surveys at Gunsan, Janghang Port, Pyeongtaek Port, and Daeheuksando Port for five months from this month to August to ensure safe navigation of ships.
In this survey, we plan to conduct a detailed survey of the water depth, bottom quality, outcroppings, coastline, etc. for a 1,300km sea area using the latest hydrographic survey equipment such as precision echo sounder and precision positioning system (DGPS) for ports and access channels where ships frequently pass.
Gunsan Port, Janghang Port, and Pyeongtaek Port are sea areas that require periodic and precise water depth information as they are topographically ports with large variations in seafloor topography.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “We will quickly provide information to navigators through navigation notifications regarding rapid changes in water depth revealed in this survey, and provide basic data for maritime traffic safety for ships using West Coast ports and development of the maritime and fisheries industries through chart revision.”

ko-news-notices-355-8372c75064.title: Joint government and university current observations around Ganghwa Island and Gyeonggi Bay
ko-news-notices-355-8372c75064.text:
Joint government and university current observations around Ganghwa Island and Gyeonggi Bay
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director General Young-jin Yeon) and Inha University announced that they would jointly observe tidal currents for one month beginning on the 25th to investigate circulation around Ganghwa Island and in Gyeonggi Bay.
The survey forms part of the exchange agreement signed by the two institutions in 2003 covering hydrographic research technology development and shared use of equipment.
Current meters and other instruments will be installed in Yeomha Channel and Seokmo Channel around Ganghwa Island and at the entrance to the lower Han River. These waters adjoin the Han River estuary where seawater and freshwater mix actively and the large tidal range produces strong tidal currents. The survey will investigate circulation characteristics saltwater and freshwater mixing and sediment transport.
An agency representative said that the joint survey would comprehensively analyze physical oceanographic and geological processes as well as produce accurate tidal-current forecast data for the broad area from the Han River estuary to northern Gyeonggi Bay. This would help clarify water circulation and sedimentation for safe navigation and marine environmental conservation and management.

ko-news-notices-354-8372c75064.title: Operation of a real-time navigation safety information collection system
ko-news-notices-354-8372c75064.text:
Operation of a real-time navigation safety information collection system
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (President Yeon Young-jin) announced that it has developed a real-time web-based navigation information collection system to quickly collect and provide navigation safety information and will begin operating it on the 9th.
The navigation information system has improved the navigational beacon facility information that had been collected from each regional maritime affairs and fisheries office in an off-line manner into a real-time collection system in a web environment, creating a quick and convenient navigation safety information system.
Information on navigational beacon facilities has been provided through navigation notices issued by the Oceanographic Survey once a week for the safe navigation of ships. However, as information provided by each local office was processed in off-line documents, the information collection system was not automated, causing delays in information collection and the inconvenience of not being able to immediately utilize the collected information.
This developed collection system was built in conjunction with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Business Management System (OKIS), and when new changes are entered, they are automatically converted to navigation notifications and DB managed in real time. In addition, by linking with the electronic payment system, official document work is minimized and all system users can jointly utilize the information.
An official from the Korea Maritime Research Institute said, “Currently, we have completed the development of only the route sign information, which accounts for about 70% of the total navigation notification information. In the future, we plan to expand it to include information that affects all maritime traffic, such as port construction and shooting training, and convert navigation notification information collection and services to a real-time system.”

ko-news-notices-353-8372c75064.title: KHOA and UNSW develop a tidal prediction model for the Yellow Sea
ko-news-notices-353-8372c75064.text:
KHOA and UNSW develop a tidal prediction model for the Yellow Sea
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director General Young-jin Yeon) announced joint research with the University of New South Wales (UNSW) in Australia to develop a numerical model capable of forecasting tides in the Yellow Sea and East China Sea.
The collaboration was proposed by UNSW. Dr Do-seong Byun of the agency's research laboratory visited UNSW from February 15 to March 30 and worked with the team led by Professor H. X. Wang identified in the original article as a leading sediment transport modeling scientist.
The two institutions first developed a numerical model that forecasts tides and tidal currents in the offshore Yellow Sea. Building on this work they plan to add functionality that accurately represents the repeated exposure and inundation of intertidal areas with the tides.
A successful model would improve prediction of tidal sea level changes in the Yellow Sea where shallow water and a large tidal range produce extensive intertidal flats.
Byun said that the team planned to improve the model using offshore Yellow Sea level observations that the agency would collect for the first time that year. He expected the model to enable offshore tide and tidal-current forecasts not previously available and to support high-accuracy bathymetric surveys.

ko-news-notices-352-8372c75064.title: Online 3D seafloor topography exhibition opens to the public
ko-news-notices-352-8372c75064.text:
Online 3D seafloor topography exhibition opens to the public
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director General Young-jin Yeon) announced that it would operate a 3D Seafloor Topography Exhibition on its website (www.nori.go.kr) allowing anyone to view three-dimensional images of the seabed around Korea.
The exhibition presents for the first time a 3D gallery and videos of seafloor topography in the East Sea including Ulleungdo and Dokdo as well as the Yellow Sea and waters around Jeju Island. In the East Sea presentation a view of Korea and the East Sea gradually appears while the water level drops and rises revealing detailed features such as Wangdolcho. The presentation of the seabed southwest of Jeju begins above Seoul travels through Chungcheong-do and Busan Port and moves toward Marado near Jeju before examining the seabed in detail. It also shows the location and underwater terrain of Ieodo and the Ieodo Ocean Research Station.
The three-dimensional imagery was produced from hydrographic survey data collected since the agency was established in 1949 and seafloor data acquired with multibeam echo sounders.
An agency representative said that giving the public an opportunity to explore the underwater landscape in realistic and accessible 3D detail would help improve public awareness of the ocean. The agency expected to extend the coverage gradually to all Korean waters.
The exhibition is available on the agency's website (http://www.nori.go.kr).

ko-news-notices-351-8372c75064.title: Distribution of BADA MAP trial version
ko-news-notices-351-8372c75064.text:
Distribution of BADA MAP trial version
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (President Yeon Young-jin) announced that it plans to distribute a trial version of the BADA Map, developed to popularize electronic navigation charts, in the middle of this month.
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency developed a sea map (BADA Map) program that can automatically convert electronic charts into various formats (DXF, SHP, SVC, TXT), allowing the general public to use electronic charts even in a typical PC environment.
Electronic charts have so far been used only for navigation, and the generalization of the GIS concept has increased the number of users. However, due to the unique nature of having to use dedicated hardware and software, it has been difficult for those who use them for academic or leisure purposes.
Accordingly, the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency developed a sea map and decided to distribute an evaluation version of the pilot program to a limited number of users to improve performance.
The evaluation version contains about 20 electronic charts of Korea's southeastern and southern coasts converted into various formats, and includes functions to easily extract water depth and coastline.
Applicants will be accepted for the evaluation version through the Research Institute website (www.nori.go.kr) from the 5th to the 13th of this month, and 100 people will be selected according to the purpose of using electronic navigation charts and distributed from the middle of this month.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “To improve the performance of the ocean map, we plan to conduct a survey in June of selected pilot users, supplement the improvements, and distribute it to the entire public starting in October.”
For inquiries regarding ocean maps, please contact the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency electronic chart team (032-880-0551~2).

ko-news-notices-350-8372c75064.title: GeoSR receives Inno-Biz certification with an Aa rating
ko-news-notices-350-8372c75064.text:
GeoSR receives Inno-Biz certification with an Aa rating
2022-03-02
Our company was finally registered after going through due diligence of technology credit guarantee for registration as an Inno-Biz company (technologically innovative small and medium-sized business).
In addition, “Aa grade” is a grade given only to companies with future growth potential and technological excellence, which are among the top 5% of Inno-Biz companies.

ko-news-notices-349-8372c75064.title: After the full-scale water blocking of the Three Gorges Dam...
ko-news-notices-349-8372c75064.text:
After the full-scale water blocking of the Three Gorges Dam...
2022-03-02
The Yellow Sea and East China Sea are showing signs of significant change due to the Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze River. This dam, the world's largest, has been in full operation since 2004 and is the lifeline that accounts for 80% of the fresh water flowing into the Yellow Sea and East China Sea.
On the 22nd, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced the results of the ‘Study on the Marine Environment Impact of the Construction of the Three Gorges Dam in the South Sea (East China Sea)’ conducted between 2003 and 2006 by the Korea Ocean Research Institute and the National Institute of Fisheries Science.
The most noticeable phenomenon after water blocking discovered in this study is the decrease in suspended solids. The suspended solids concentration, which was 3.261 mg/l in 2004, decreased by more than 20% to 1.791 mg/l the following year. The problem is that the nitrogen content in suspended solids is a nutrient that the Yellow Sea desperately needs. The report stated that the decrease in suspended solids, which are nutrients for phytoplankton, will have a significant impact on the marine ecosystem, including fish.
According to a Chinese study, the construction of the Three Gorges Dam is expected to reduce suspended sediments by 23.4%, equivalent to an annual average of 110 million tons, resulting in a 10% decrease in nutrients supplied to the sea.
In addition, the study predicted that the Three Gorges Dam would release more water in the spring, the dry season, and reduce outflow in the summer, the flood season, so that the summer salinity concentration would increase to about 1% at the mouth of the Yangtze River and about 0.04% on the west side of Jeju Island.
Observations showed that lumps of low-salinity water in the Yangtze River frequently approach the waters around Jeju Island. Low-salt water chunks are chunks of fresh water that have not yet mixed with seawater, and often cause red tide and mass death of fish in the South Sea and Jeju Island.
Choi Dong-rim, a senior researcher at the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute who is in charge of the research, said, “Changes in water temperature and salinity concentration can only be identified through longer-term studies. In the second phase of the study, which started this year, we plan to conduct a quantitative analysis of the impact on ecosystems such as fishing grounds and changes in seawater characteristics.”
Hongseop Cho, environmental reporter ecothink@hani.co.kr

ko-news-notices-348-8372c75064.title: The southwest coast development plan only shows a rosy picture.
ko-news-notices-348-8372c75064.text:
The southwest coast development plan only shows a rosy picture.
2022-03-02
The southwestern coastal region, from Incheon through Pyeongtaek and Saemangeum to Yeongam and Haenam, is currently filled with dreams with a rosy blueprint.
All kinds of development plans are being promoted based on the justification of the emergence of the Pan-Yellow Sea economic zone and balanced national development.
In particular, various development projects are complexly intertwined in the Honam and southwestern coastal regions.
What the government has put forward is the ‘Southwest Coast Comprehensive Development Plan’, also called the S Project.
A total of 22.4 trillion won will be invested over 14 years from this year to 2020 to develop the Muan, Mokpo, and Shinan regions into industrial bases in the Yellow Sea Rim region.
Within the S Project, the Saemangeum area is planned to be developed into an agricultural and industrial complex.
The government claims that if this development plan is implemented as scheduled and the area is developed into an industrial and logistics hub with a population of 600,000, it will become one of the central regions of the Yellow Sea Rim Economic Area.
Jeonnam Province is promoting the J Project separately from the government’s S Project.
Project J plans to build an F1 racetrack, marine leisure town, health recreation town, and golf course on 30 million pyeong of land in Samho-eup, Yeongam-gun and Sanmyeon, Haenam-gun by 2016.
The total investment amount is 35 trillion won, and it is a tourism and leisure complex city that will accommodate 300,000 people.
In addition, development plans such as Naju Innovation City and Jangseong Honam Logistics Base are also being promoted.
Commenting on these fluctuating development plans, Kim Eui-jun, a professor at the Department of Community Development at Seoul National University, said, “In Muan Enterprise City, investment from domestic companies and foreign countries is currently unclear, and Muan Airport has also spent tens of billions of won to build facilities, but is not even able to open.” He added, “It is problematic to pour out development plans like this when the investment entity has not been confirmed.”
An official from the Ministry of Construction and Transportation said, "The justification for balanced regional development is good, but the problem is that this plan is being promoted individually without any mast plan." He added, "A development plan that can efficiently connect nearby areas, including Saemangeum, must be developed."
[Planning Reporting Team = Deputy Director Chae Gyeong-ok (Team Leader) / Reporter Kim Ki-cheol (Real Estate Ministry) / Reporter Kim Gyu-sik (Economy Ministry)]

ko-news-notices-347-8372c75064.title: Providing underwater information in the southern coastal waters of Gyeonggi Bay
ko-news-notices-347-8372c75064.text:
Providing underwater information in the southern coastal waters of Gyeonggi Bay
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Yeon Young-jin) announced that it will distribute a product containing the latest submarine topography information on the southern coastal waters of Gyeonggi Bay.
The undersea topography information provided this time includes various marine information such as precise undersea topography, distribution of shallow strata, distribution of surface bottom quality, grain size distribution of bottom quality, tides, and tidal currents surveyed last year in the Deokjeokdo, Daeijakdo, and Seongapdo areas in the southern part of Gyeonggi Province using cutting-edge marine survey equipment such as multi-beam echo sounders.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “The results of seafloor information in coastal waters are used as data for chart correction, provision of navigational information, and selection of suitable sites for artificial reefs, and are expected to be provided as important information needed for review of coastal waters and new route settings.”
Meanwhile, this outcome will be distributed to government agencies and marine research institutes, and will be used as basic data for coastal development and conservation, and construction of basic marine geographical information.

ko-news-notices-346-8372c75064.title: The chart near Gunsan Port changes.
ko-news-notices-346-8372c75064.text:
The chart near Gunsan Port changes.
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency's West Sea Ocean Survey Office (Director Jeong Hyeon) announced that it would conduct surveys of the land topography around Gunsan Port and reflect the results in the latest charts.
The existing Gunsan Port chart left the Gunjang Industrial Complex area blank, causing inconvenience to users.
Accordingly, the West Sea Marine Survey Office conducted topographic surveys for the month of February on industrial infrastructure, roads, ports, and major buildings within the Gunjang National Industrial Complex (around Gunsan Port) using the principles of a navigation system that connects the Hydrographic Survey Data Processing System (Hypack) and the Global Positioning System (DGPS).
An official from the Korea Maritime Research Institute said, “By reflecting the Gunjang National Industrial Complex on the latest charts, it is expected that it will be used as very useful data for ships entering and leaving Gunsan Port and port-related personnel.”
The revised charts can be purchased from a chart sales agency (☎02-701-9981, 051-466-0760) or through the company's Internet website (www.chartkorea.com) starting in April.

ko-news-notices-345-8372c75064.title: A 770,000-pyeong new ocean city will be created in Masan by filling in the sea by 2017.
ko-news-notices-345-8372c75064.text:
A 770,000-pyeong new ocean city will be created in Masan by filling in the sea by 2017.
2022-03-02
A marine city measuring 770,000 pyeong will be built in the West Port district of Masan-si, Gyeongsangnam-do and the Gapo district, the hinterland of Masan New Port, by 2017.
Masan City, Gyeongsangnam-do, decided to promote Masan Marine City, which will reclaim the sea in the area and create a new city, as an urban development method, and held an inaugural general meeting of Masan Marine New City Co., Ltd., which is composed of the city and private operators such as Hyundai Development Company, Sammi Construction, Daekyung Construction, Geonil Engineering, and Kookmin Bank on the 21st.
Masan Marine City Co., Ltd. has a founding capital of 1 billion won, and Hyundai Development Company (29.5%) and Masan City (28.5%) own more than half of the shares.
This project will invest KRW 691 billion to create 770,000 pyeong of land through marine reclamation and other methods to be used as residential and commercial land.
Masan Marine City Co., Ltd. will act on behalf of Masan City for 10 years until the project is completed in 2017, and will be in charge of tasks such as financing and ordering various impact assessment services, various compensation surveys and data preparation in the West Port and Gapo districts, and establishment and distribution of sales plans.
Masan Marine New Town Co., Ltd. will hold a financial agreement signing ceremony for a loan of 150 billion won at the Masan Savoy Hotel at 11:30 a.m. on the 26th with five lenders, including Kookmin Bank, National Nonghyup Bank, Kyongnam Bank, Busan Bank, and Suhyup Bank, attending.

ko-news-notices-344-8372c75064.title: [Saemangeum use plan confirmed after 20 years] 70% of reclaimed land is farmland
ko-news-notices-344-8372c75064.text:
[Saemangeum use plan confirmed after 20 years] 70% of reclaimed land is farmland
2022-03-02
The 'Land Use Plan' for the Saemangeum reclamation project, which began as an election pledge by then Democratic Justice Party candidate Roh Tae-woo during the 1987 presidential election, was finally finalized after 20 years.
The plan is to focus on developing Buan-gun, which is close to Byeonsan National Park, by 2020, and to build foreign direct investment (FDI) areas and logistics facilities in Gunsan-si from 2020 to 2030.
This plan is different from the idea that local governments such as Jeollabuk-do have been advocating for ‘distributed development’, where industrial complexes, new towns, and tourist sites are located in adjacent areas of Gunsan, Gimje, and Buan-gun.
A government official said, "Of the land classified as agricultural land, 41.5㎢ (12.55 million pyeong) has been classified as reserved land so that it can be converted to other uses, so it may be readjusted in the future if additional leisure facilities such as golf courses or industrial complexes are needed."
◆Some farmland can be converted to use
The Saemangeum reclamation project has a total area of 401㎢ (121.3 million pyeong), which is 140 times the size of Yeouido in Seoul and two-thirds of the size of Seoul.
Among these, the internal reclamation area, excluding the 118㎢ (35.7 million pyeong) created as a freshwater lake, is 283㎢ (85.8 million pyeong), which is 100 times the area of ​​Yeouido.
Construction of the Saemangeum project began in 1991, but construction was halted for two years and five months starting in 1999 due to the contamination of Sihwa Lake and lawsuits filed by environmental groups.
The government prioritized ‘securing high-quality farmland’ as the development principle for Saemangeum reclaimed land.
It was decided to develop land (61.25 million pyeong) equivalent to 71.6% of the Saemangeum reclaimed area into rice fields and a horticultural complex.
It is important to secure high-quality farmland as it is expected that 1.288 billion pyeong (4,260 ㎢) of the total agricultural land in Korea (18.36 billion pyeong, as of 2005) will decrease by 2030.
However, the government classified 12.5 million pyeong of Saemangeum farmland as 'reserved land' and initially used it as rice paddies for rental farming, allowing it to be converted to use later.
For example, the FDI area to be created after 2030 is planned to be created by diverting 4.2 million pyeong of farmland classified as reserved farmland.
In addition, as demand for golf courses, etc., is expected to be converted to farmland, Saemangeum farmland is likely to be reduced to 56% of the total reclaimed land.
◆Gunsan for industry, Buan for tourism
The government applied ‘selection and concentration’ as the Saemangeum development principle.
In order to maximize the effect of connection with the Gunjang district, an industrial complex area, it was decided to concentrate industrial sites, foreign investment zones, and logistics facilities in areas adjacent to Gunsan City.
The plan is to first create an industrial complex area of ​​2.8 million pyeong by 2020, and then complete the remainder by 2030, when seawater distribution ends.
It was decided to attract companies related to the automobile, petrochemical, biological and biotechnology industries to the Saemangeum Industrial Complex.
It was decided to concentrate the tourist attractions in the southern area of ​​Saemangeum (Buan-gun) so that they can be developed in connection with Byeonsan Peninsula National Park.
2.4 million pyeong will be allocated to build 8 golf courses (based on 18 holes), and the rest will be used for marine entertainment facilities such as water parks and mariner facilities, health lands, hotels, and pensions.
The government estimates that tourism demand for Saemangeum and surrounding areas will reach 11.51 million people per year in 2020.
◆"No new city construction"
The government decided not to build a separate new city in the Saemangeum area.
The position is that people working in industrial complexes can be absorbed into the 'Gunsan urbanization area', and the population induced by the activation of foreign direct investment can also be developed around Gunsan City.
As a result, Jeollabuk-do's plan to create a new city, such as an enterprise city, in the hinterland of Gimje City was in vain.
Jeollabuk-do has been requesting that land use plans be drawn up in the following areas: 'Gunsan-Industrial Complex', 'Gimje-Foreign Investment Zone/Enterprise City Construction', and 'Buan-Tourism Complex' in the sense of 'dispersed deployment for balanced regional development'.
The concentrated placement of golf courses and leisure complexes in Buan-gun could also be a factor in causing conflict within the region.
In the case of industrial land, some are claiming that it is unrealistic to create an additional 5.65 million pyeong (18.7㎢) at a time when the occupancy rate of the Gunjang Industrial Complex near Saemangeum is only 30%.
Reporter Hyun Seung-yoon/Kim Hong-yeol hyunsy@hankyung.com

ko-news-notices-343-8372c75064.title: [New Maritime Era] Rapid development in advanced maritime countries
ko-news-notices-343-8372c75064.text:
[New Maritime Era] Rapid development in advanced maritime countries
2022-03-02
It was 33 years ago that the resource value of deep ocean water became known to the world. When the oil shock broke out in 1973, the following year, the United States, which was looking for alternative energy to replace oil, began researching ‘ocean temperature difference power generation’, which extracts cold deep ocean water and uses the temperature difference with warm surface water to generate electricity, and the secrets of deep ocean water began to be revealed one by one.
The United States immediately established a natural energy research center in Hawaii and began industrializing deep ocean water, focusing on agriculture, fishing, alternative energy, food, and medicine. Currently, 29 food and pharmaceutical venture companies are housed in this research institute, creating employment for 200 people and generating an income of $30 million annually.
It was Japan that established the concept of developing deep ocean water commercialization technology. Japan, which began researching deep water in 1976, succeeded in developing ‘drinking water’ using deep water for the first time in 1989, forming a significant industry.
In fact, deep water development projects are underway in 18 local governments, including Kochi Prefecture, and as many as 1,000 types of deep water-related products, including bottled water, beer, beverages, salt, cosmetics, and food, are being produced. The market size reaches 2.5 trillion won per year. Drinking water made from deep ocean water in Japan is imported into Korea as a mixed drink and sold at very high prices in department stores.
Norway is using deep water for salmon farming, and Taiwan has also been working on industrialization, including marketing bottled water using deep water since last year.
Reporter Ahn Kyung-ho (Hankook Ilbo, khan@hk.co.kr)

ko-news-notices-342-8372c75064.title: [New Ocean Age] Mysterious water, deep ocean water
ko-news-notices-342-8372c75064.text:
[New Ocean Age] Mysterious water, deep ocean water
2022-03-02
The sea in front of Ohori, Jukwang-myeon, Goseong-gun, Gangwon-do. At the bottom of the sea here, there is a large water intake pipe line about 2.45km long that leads to land. It is intended to raise ‘East Seawater’ at a depth of 300m and 500m. The East Sea water that comes up through the seafloor intake pipe is water that ‘should not be considered water.’ This is because it is deep ocean water, ‘mysterious water’ that has been in the deep sea for at least 300 years.
Spotted for its diverse utility value
Dr. Moon Deok-soo of the Korea Ocean Research Institute's Deep Ocean Research Center emphasized, "Deep ocean water is the life-giving water of the future, with endless potential for development not only as drinking water, but also as agricultural and fishing water, medicine, beauty, and health products. It is an extremely important national resource, especially for Korea, which is a water-scarce country as defined by the United Nations."
Deep ocean water is seawater located at a depth of more than 200 meters where sunlight does not reach. Because there is no sunlight, the water temperature is always maintained below 2 degrees, and since photosynthesizing phytoplankton and seaweed cannot survive, there are almost no pathogens and organic pollutants that feed on them.
On the other hand, as various organic substances on the surface of seawater sink, they are decomposed and accumulated into nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus, making it rich in minerals. It also contains a large amount of minerals such as calcium and magnesium that help cells function.
The uses of deep ocean water with these characteristics are very diverse. A representative example is drinking water. Deep water becomes clean water that can be consumed immediately by removing the salt. It becomes a functional water (drink) containing a large amount of natural minerals. The salt produced during the decontamination process is also a clean salt, different from ordinary salt.
Developed and used only in 5 countries around the world
Deep water maintains a water temperature of 5 degrees even when it is drawn up to land through water intake pipes, so it can be used for air conditioning and ice-making facilities. 100 tons of deep water can provide cooling for 8 to 16 households all day.
It is also rich in nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphoric acid, and silicon, making it an ideal water source for cultivating seaweed and seasonal fish. In actual seaweed farming, the growth rate is about twice as fast as that of general surface water.
In the medical world, deep ocean water is used as a treatment for atopic dermatitis, and in the agricultural field, it is used to prevent overgrowth when cultivating seedlings such as peppers and cabbage. In addition, deep sea water with the salt removed has excellent skin care benefits and is also used as a cosmetics or food additive.
Deep ocean water discharged into surrounding waters after being used for various purposes contains significant amounts of nutrients, contributing to restoring the fishing environment and maintaining balance. The East Sea Fisheries Research Institute confirmed that the number of species of seaweed in the northern waters of Jukdo has increased from 15 to 27 as a result of the continuous discharge of deep ocean water from the waters of Jukdo in front of Ohori, Jukwang-myeon over the past year. In short, deep ocean water is water that cannot be thrown away.
Dr. Seungwon Lee of the research center said, “Currently, there are only five countries, including Korea, the United States, Japan, Norway, and Taiwan, that have succeeded in developing deep ocean water. We are working with domestic universities and research institutes to find areas for the multipurpose development and application of our own deep ocean water.”
The East Coast reports deep water
Deep water, which has emerged as a ‘vein of marine gold’, flows in vast quantities in the East Sea of Korea. The world’s oceanographic community even acknowledges that “the East Sea is a naturally blessed deep-water sea.” Normally, the seawater that circulates around the Earth reaches the Greenland Glacier area, cools, increases in weight, sinks to the bottom of the sea, flows around, rises to the surface of the sea in the northern waters of the North Pacific, cools again, and then falls. It takes 2,000 years for deep water to circulate once around the Earth.
However, the East Sea, which is surrounded by the Korean Peninsula, the Russian coast, and the Japanese archipelago, has an average water depth of 1,684m, but the width of the four straits is narrow and the water depth is low at less than 200m, so the amount of deep water exchanged with the adjacent sea is very small. As a result, deep water is formed, circulated, and transformed within the East Sea.
This is why academics call the deep waters of the East Sea ‘East Sea unique waters.’ Currently, the amount of deep water in the East Sea is estimated to be 19 cubic tons (3×10), and the internal circulation cycle is estimated to be 300 to 700 years.
Napping in the National Assembly on relevant laws for over two years
Although our country has abundant deep water resources, we are unable to actually connect them to ‘money’. This is because the ‘Act on the Development and Management of Deep Ocean Water’, which the government announced as legislation for the systematic development of deep ocean water, has not passed the National Assembly for over two years. Although countries such as Japan and Taiwan do not have laws related to deep water, Korea is pushing for the enactment of related laws due to concerns about the side effects of deep water development and excessive competition.
In fact, eight companies, including Kooksoondang (Baekseju), Aekyung Industrial (cosmetics), Sempio Foods (soy sauce), and Hyundai Pharmaceuticals (ion beverages), have developed deep sea water prototypes but are unable to market them. Deep water development companies are no longer able to tolerate it and are actively taking action, saying, “We will pursue the project even within the limits of the current law.”
Kim Hong-ki, CEO of Ulleung Mineral Co., Ltd., said, “With the National Assembly holding back, the number of domestic development companies has decreased from about 20 to 5.” He added, “As the Drinking Water Management Act was revised in June last year to allow drinking water to be made from seawater, we will pursue deep water development projects based on this.”
Local governments on the east coast, including Gangwon-do, Goseong-gun, Yangyang-gun, Gangneung-si, Uljin-gun in Gyeongsangbuk-do, and Ulleung-gun, who are confident of the growth potential of the deep water market and have jumped into attracting related companies, are also eagerly awaiting passage of the bill. This is because there is a high possibility that deep water will act as a positive factor to revive the stagnant local economy of the East Coast.
Currently, the deep ocean water bill allows deep water developers to collect water fees as taxes and use them for local projects.
Professor Lee Jong-ho (Department of Deep Ocean Mathematics) at Kyungdong University predicted, “Deep water-related projects will have a huge economic ripple effect, such as creating jobs, attracting tourists, and increasing residents’ income.”
Joint planning between Dong-A Ilbo and Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries
Goseong = Reporter Ahn Gyeong-ho (Hankook Ilbo, khan@hk.co.kr)

ko-news-notices-341-8372c75064.title: Saemangeum special bill submitted to the National Assembly
ko-news-notices-341-8372c75064.text:
Saemangeum special bill submitted to the National Assembly
2022-03-02
The Saemangeum Special Bill was submitted to the National Assembly on the 13th. Accordingly, Jeonbuk Province has designated this week as the week of making all-out efforts to enact the Saemangeum Special Act and is planning to make an all-out effort to pass the bill through the National Assembly, drawing attention to the results.
Jeonbuk Province submitted the Saemangeum Special Bill to the National Assembly on this day along with representative sponsor Kim Won-ki (former National Assembly Speaker) of the Uri Party. There were 173 lawmakers who proposed the Saemangeum Special Bill, and most of them were from political parties. Jeonbuk Governor Kim Wan-joo explained, “Considering the situation where there are more than 100 bills submitted to the National Assembly’s Agriculture, Forestry, Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Committee, we have brought forward the schedule for submitting the special law in order to expedite the enactment of the special law.”
The Saemangeum Special Bill proposed this time consists of a total of 9 chapters and 46 articles with the main content of developing the Saemangeum area into an environmentally friendly complex city, including the establishment of the Saemangeum comprehensive development plan, development project promotion system, and designation of a free economic zone.
Jeonbuk Province decided to first pursue a plan to garner full support from the Grand National Party, which accounts for 43% of the seats in the National Assembly, and the presidential candidates. In addition, a public hearing is scheduled to be held with the Grand National Party's Yeouido Research Institute on the 23rd.
Jeonju = Reporter Park Chan-joon (Segye Ilbo)

ko-news-notices-340-8372c75064.title: Tributaries of Sihwa Lake turn black — Fears over human damage
ko-news-notices-340-8372c75064.text:
Tributaries of Sihwa Lake turn black — Fears over human damage
2022-03-02
Black ash from burning reed forests is flowing into Sihwa Lake (top left). Last month, with the support of the Korea Water Resources Corporation, residents burned 500,000 pyeong of reed forest (bottom of photo) to control pests. Ash melts with snow and rain and flows into Sihwa Lake. On the afternoon of the 20th from the aircraft of the Aviation Environment Monitoring Group in Hwaseong-si, Gyeonggi-do.
▲ On the morning of the 20th, the stream of Sihwa Lake in Hwaseong, Gyeonggi-do was dyed black when I got off the plane of the Ansan City Aviation Environment Monitoring Group. This is because ash from the 500,000 pyeong reed forest that residents burned to prevent stink bugs, a pest, with support from the Korea Water Resources Corporation at the end of last month, flowed into rivers due to snow and rain.
Reporter Joo Wan-joong (Chosun Ilbo)
[Reporter Joo Wan-joong wjjoo@chosun.com]

ko-news-notices-339-8372c75064.title: Seosan-Taean, Garorim Bay tidal power generation ‘conflict’
ko-news-notices-339-8372c75064.text:
Seosan-Taean, Garorim Bay tidal power generation ‘conflict’
2022-03-02
Seosan-si and Taean-gun in South Chungcheong Province, which were once in the same pot, are showing signs of conflict as their interests diverge over the tidal power plant being built in Garorim Bay in the West Sea.
According to Seosan City on the 9th, as a result of collecting opinions on the construction of a tidal power plant from 13 fishing villages in 3 townships (Daesan-eup, Palbong-myeon, and Jigok-myeon) surrounding Garolim Bay, 11 of them expressed opposition, and it was found that the Fisheries Cooperative and Seosan Taean Environmental Movement Federation also presented opposing opinions.
In particular, the level of opposition is increasing in the Jigok-myeon area, with residents starting a signature campaign to 'cancel the tidal power plant construction plan'.
There is concern that if a tidal power plant is built in Garorim Bay, the tidal range will change, which will lead to changes in the ecosystem such as a decrease in mudflats, as well as damage to residents' living spaces, such as destruction of the fish food chain and spawning grounds for fish and shellfish due to changes in ocean currents, and a decrease in marine product production.
In addition, Garorim Bay is considered a suitable site for a new port due to its deep water, and one reason for opposition is that even though a tidal power plant is being built, the opportunity to build a new port is fundamentally blocked.
Choi Jang-hwan, chairman of the Jigok-myeon Development Council, said, “Garolim Bay is a spawning ground for fish resources such as crabs, octopuses, and prawns, and is the livelihood of residents.” He added, “There cannot be the construction of a tidal power plant that threatens the right to survive.”
On the other hand, Taean-gun residents secretly hope that the construction of a tidal power plant will serve as an opportunity for regional development.
This is because the Iwon-myeon area of ​​Taean, where only Garolim is located, has a relatively slow development rate compared to southern areas of Taean such as Anmyeondo Island, and the potential for development is low, so tidal power plants are expected to act as a catalyst for development.
Moreover, it is expected that the tidal power plant breakwater will serve as a bridge connecting Daesan in Seosan and Iwon in Taean, thereby increasing accessibility for tourists coming to Taean.
A Taean-gun official said, "Because tidal power plants do not cut off waterways like seawalls, there is little risk of damage to the ecosystem, so it is inappropriate to think that tidal power generation will lead to environmental destruction. In particular, the breakwaters will have the effect of replacing the construction of bridges that cost 170 billion won and will become a new eco-friendly tourism resource."
Regarding this, a Seosan City official said, "It is true that there are differences of opinion between regions and residents regarding the issue of building a tidal power plant, but it is difficult to reveal the city's official position without the project plan being visualized. We plan to review comprehensive public opinion and prepare future response plans."
Meanwhile, Garorim Bay is considered the best location for a tidal power plant in Korea, along with Sihwa Lake in Gyeonggi Province, where a tidal power plant is currently being built due to the large difference in tidal range (7-9m). Korea Western Power has decided to build a 480,000 kW tidal power plant after building a 2km seawall by blocking Garorim Bay and is currently going through feasibility study and environmental impact assessment procedures.
(Yonhap News seokyee@yna.co.kr)

ko-news-notices-338-8372c75064.title: If 10% of beaches are eroded, economic value will be lost by 14%.
ko-news-notices-338-8372c75064.text:
If 10% of beaches are eroded, economic value will be lost by 14%.
2022-03-02
Estimates showed that if the beach erodes by about 10%, it causes a loss of about 14% in the economic value of the beach.
The Korea Maritime Institute (KMI) announced on the 7th in a report titled 'Economic Evaluation of Coastal Erosion Damage Due to Sea Sand Extraction' that it obtained these results as a result of estimating the value loss of the beach for Iile Beach in Woongjin-gun, Gyeonggi-do, which is pointed out as a case of coastal erosion due to sea sand extraction.
In the report, KMI said, “The average daily willingness to pay per person wishing to use Iile Beach was estimated to be 40,846 to 56,930 won,” and “Therefore, the average willingness to pay per 100 m2 of Iile Beach is estimated to be 45.9 to 64 won.”
KMI premised, “However, per unit value multiplied by total area does not reflect the total economic loss of eroded beaches.”
KMI explained, "In order to estimate what effect erosion has on the value and loss of the beach, we analyzed how marginal erosion affects the willingness to pay for beach use. As a result, in the case of Iile Beach, when 10% of the beach is eroded, the maximum daily average willingness to pay for those wishing to use Iile Beach decreased from 56,930 won to 48,985 won."
KMI stated, “Therefore, it was found that 10% erosion of resort beaches causes a loss in the economic value of the beach by approximately 14%.”
According to the KMI analysis results, based on the case of Iile Beach, if the beach was eroded by 20%, the economic value of the beach would be lost by 27%, if 30% of the beach was eroded, 39%, and if 40% of the beach was eroded, 50.55%.
KMI said, "The amount of sea sand collected from the sea area around Iile Beach, which was the basis for the analysis, is officially estimated at several thousand ㎥, but unofficially it is estimated to be enormous. Regarding the sand beach erosion at this beach, residents claim that the main cause is sea sand collection."
“In the case of Korea, the dependence on marine sand extraction is greater than that of any other country, and the development of alternative resources is likely to be difficult in the immediate future. As it is not a situation where a complete ban on sea sand extraction is possible due to environmental issues, it appears that multifaceted policy measures and alternatives will be needed,” KMI pointed out.
KMI proposed that as policy measures to solve this problem in the future, it is necessary to ▲build a database of marine environmental assessment data ▲introduce a cumulative environmental impact assessment system ▲strengthen the maritime collection monitoring system.
(Yonhap News yulsid@yna.co.kr)

ko-news-notices-336-8372c75064.title: Documentary on global warming based on Al Gore's lectures
ko-news-notices-336-8372c75064.text:
Documentary on global warming based on Al Gore's lectures
2022-03-02
‘An Inconvenient Truth’ is a documentary based on former U.S. Vice President Al Gore’s environmental lecture.
In the film, Gore travels around the world giving lectures to warn of the seriousness of global warming and shows his daily life as an environmental activist. The main character of the movie is gore. It was released in the United States in May of last year and earned box office receipts of over $24 million, which is unusual for a documentary. Gore, who had been struggling after losing the presidential election, became an opportunity to draw public attention again. It was released in Korea in September last year, but failed at the box office.
The movie warns that if carbon dioxide produced by burning oil and coal continues to increase at the current rate, the Earth will become too hot in the near future and an environmental disaster will occur. It realistically shows scenes such as melting snow on Mount Kilimanjaro and collapsing polar glaciers, made famous by Ernest Hemingway's novel. Some predict that low-lying areas of Manhattan, New York and Shanghai will be flooded, and there will be alternating periods of severe storms and droughts.
At the same time, he indirectly criticizes President George W. Bush for refusing to ratify the Kyoto Protocol to reduce carbon dioxide emissions. The audience is urged not only to use eco-friendly products but also to vote for politicians who implement eco-friendly policies. Gore published a book with the same title last year. It was also translated and introduced in Korea with the subtitle “Al Gore’s Emergency Environmental Report.”
LA = Reporter Joo Jeong-wan

ko-news-notices-335-8372c75064.title: A new sand supply method is optimal to prevent erosion at Jungmun Beach.
ko-news-notices-335-8372c75064.text:
A new sand supply method is optimal to prevent erosion at Jungmun Beach.
2022-03-02
The service results showed that supplying new sand to the white sand beach was the most appropriate method of preventing erosion at Jungmun Beach.
At the briefing session on the establishment of a monitoring system for erosion changes at Jungmun Beach held at Seogwipo City Hall Building 1 on the 21st, the service provider evaluated the Yangbin method as the most appropriate anti-erosion measure for Jungmun Beach.
According to the service results, the hinterland of Jungmun Beach is mostly formed of sand dunes, but it has recently been found to be experiencing rapid changes due to continuous erosion, including the collapse of sand structure forests, disappearance of vegetation, and collapse due to erosion.
Accordingly, in order to fundamentally prevent sand dune erosion, a reinforcement method for the foundation is necessary, and the Yangbin method was analyzed as an appropriate reinforcement method for the sand dune foundation.
The Yangbin method is a method that protects the beach by supplying sand to the beach, absorbing wave energy that invades the beach, and reducing reflected waves. It is less expensive than other methods and has the effect of directly expanding the width of the beach.
However, it has the disadvantage of requiring additional maintenance and making it difficult to select a sand supply source.
The service team also pointed out that along with the implementation of the Yangbin Construction Method, it is necessary to install a secondary fence to block tourists' access to the sand dunes.
However, due to the nature of Jungmun Beach as a tourist site, in principle, access to tourists is not possible, so a plan was proposed to build a fenced-style promenade and protect the base of the sand dune.
In addition, the service team explained that as a future task for establishing anti-erosion measures, more long-term monitoring is needed to identify the characteristics of beach changes, and a detailed marine survey should be conducted on external factors such as weather, waves, and currents for changes in white sand beach erosion. %scoop@jejunews.com

ko-news-notices-334-8372c75064.title: [New Ocean Era] Uldolmok Tidal Power Plant
ko-news-notices-334-8372c75064.text:
[New Ocean Era] Uldolmok Tidal Power Plant
2022-03-02
The current is very fast due to the narrow channel and rocky seabed.
World's largest tidal power plant produces first electricity in November
“Uuu~shooaa~, rumbling~shooaa~”
It was definitely a cry. It sounded like the cry of a man with a deep voice, or the howl of an animal. Uldolmok, the strait between Jindo, Jeollanam-do and Hwawon Peninsula, Haenam-gun. There is a reason why it is called ‘Myeongryang (鳴梁)’ with the meaning of ‘the road where the sea cries’.
The current of Uldolmok seen from Jindo Bridge during low tide was still strong and unstoppable. The saying of the people here, “If people on the land look at the swirling currents of Uldolmok for a long time, they will get seasick,” was definitely not a lie.
A tidal power plant with an unfamiliar name will be built in Uldolmok, which boasts such fast water currents. It is a facility that produces electricity by utilizing fast currents.
The Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute, which led the technology development, has already completed the production of turbines and power generation facility structures for the development of the world's largest 1,000 kW test tidal current power plant in Uldolmok (November), and only the on-site installation of the structure and electrical and electrical equipment work remain. As this news became known, the Korea Ocean Research Institute received constant requests for technology transfer and joint research from coastal countries around the world, such as Indonesia and Vietnam.
Lee Kwang-soo, head of the Coastal Development Research Division, said, “Our country has almost achieved technological independence, having completed the commercialization of the ‘helical turbine,’ a power generation experimental device, through tidal power experiments since 2002,” and added, “Countries such as the United Kingdom, which installed a 150 kW test power generation turbine one step ahead of us, are also paying close attention.”
The reason Uldolmok is able to demonstrate the value of fast water currents is because of its unique narrow channel and seabed topography. Uldolmok is narrow, about 294m wide, and the water level difference between the south and west widens by up to 2m during high and low tides. The seafloor has no sedimentary layers and is made up of highly curved rock. As a large amount of seawater tries to pass through the narrow strait, the current inevitably becomes faster.
In fact, the current speed of Uldolmok reaches an average speed of 5.5 m per second at the depth and a maximum speed of 6.5 m per second at the surface of the sea. Normally, when a flood occurs in the Han River, the current speed is about 2 to 3 meters per second, enough to wash away a car, which is an incredible speed.
However, the high current speed of Uldolmok also acts as an obstacle to tidal development. Because the current is so fast, it is not easy to install a water turbine power plant structure weighing 790 tons.
Above all, drilling work to insert six large iron pipes (137 cm in diameter), which formed the main frame of the structure, into the Uldolmok seafloor rock was impossible due to the high flow rate. Therefore, Hyundai Engineering & Construction, which was in charge of construction, changed the installation method by first putting down the structure, inserting a drilling machine into the iron pipe, drilling a hole to a depth of 8m, and then inserting another iron pipe to pour concrete.
Kim Joo-sik, head of the Uldolmok Experimental Tidal Current Power Plant construction site, said, “It was impossible to perform drilling work on a barge shaking at a high speed, so we changed the construction method. Although the changed installation method is the first to be attempted in the world, there is a good chance of success.” The structure will be installed at the end of April.
The test power plant's electricity production capacity amounts to 1.2 GWh (1.2 million kW) per year. This is the amount of electricity that 300 households (based on average monthly consumption of 300 kW per household) can use for one year. However, this does not mean that the power originally expected can be stably produced. This is because a barrier must be installed on the structure to prevent marine debris such as refrigerators and TVs, which are swept away by the strong current of Uldolmok, from hitting the water wheel. Experts predict that power generation efficiency will drop by about 10% due to the installation of barriers.
So, why is Uldolmok tidal power generation in the spotlight as a next-generation alternative energy source? First of all, unlike wave power, solar power, or wind power generation, long-term prediction of power generation is possible due to the periodicity of high and low tides.
In addition, it is the most environmentally friendly as it does not require dams like tidal power generation using the ebb and flow of the tides, and has a significant energy import substitution effect. In fact, if the 50,000 kW Uldolmok commercial tidal current power plant is built by 2012, it will produce 123 GWh (123 million kW) of electricity annually, which will not only replace energy imports worth 12 billion won (200,000 barrels of crude oil) each year, but also reduce carbon dioxide by 76,000 tons per year.
Park Jin-soon, a senior engineer at the Korea Ocean Research Institute, explained, “In a situation where the environment and energy are changing toward coexistence, tidal power generation is the most suitable and economical method.”
Uldolmok, where the test tidal power plant will be built, will have a tremendous impact on the local economy. Jindo-gun is already full of expectations that Uldolmok Tidal Power Plant will create new wealth. In order to promote the tidal power plant and turn it into a tourist resource, the county decided to build a marine energy park on a 6,050 pyeong site in Nokjin-ri, Gunnae-myeon by 2009.
Jindo-gun predicts that the Marine Energy Park, which will feature an exhibition hall, an observatory, and amusement facilities where visitors can directly experience various marine energy power generation systems such as currents and tidal forces, will bring about a production inducement effect of KRW 24.597 billion and an income inducement effect of KRW 6.849 billion.
Hwang Gyu-woong, head of Jindo-gun fishing village and fishing port, said, “Once the tidal power plant and marine energy park are built at Uldolmok, the battle site of Admiral Yi Sun-sin’s Battle of Myeongnyang, Uldolmok is expected to not only emerge as a historical tourist site and science education center, but also play a significant role in the local economy.”
Jindo (Uldolmok) = Reporter Ahn Gyeong-ho khan@hk.co.kr

ko-news-notices-333-8372c75064.title: 2007 West Coast hydrographic survey program announced
ko-news-notices-333-8372c75064.text:
2007 West Coast hydrographic survey program announced
2022-03-02
Five projects including tidal-current observations between Gunsan and Imja Island
The West Sea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Office of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Chang-seop Choi) announced its 2007 survey program for the West Coast.
The program covers five areas: tidal benchmark and coastal navigation route surveys in the southern West Sea hydrographic surveying northwest of Wido Island tidal-current observations between Gunsan and Imja Island marine characteristic surveys around the Sibidongpa Islands and tidal observations at 15 locations including Janghang Port.
The 77-ton hydrographic survey vessel Hwanghaero built last year will support this year's surveys and is expected to produce high-quality marine information promptly and accurately.
An agency representative said that the results would be systematically analyzed and organized and provided on the agency's website (www.nori.go.kr). The information would support chart production hydrographic publications safe navigation understanding of the marine environment and the comprehensive use and conservation of the ocean.

ko-news-notices-332-8372c75064.title: Production of sea guide maps and distribution for free
ko-news-notices-332-8372c75064.text:
Production of sea guide maps and distribution for free
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (President Yeon Young-jin) announced that it will produce and distribute for free the “Ocean Guide Map,” which is a re-edited version of the latest charts for Korea's jurisdictional waters in booklet format (A4 size).
The sea guide map contains the latest charts for coastal navigation published between August 2004 and October 2006, and for user convenience, navigation precautions, major shelters, tidal currents, ocean currents, water temperature distribution, and Korean coastal distance list are included.
In addition, the contents of marine survey work were included so that the general public could more easily access information about the sea.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “It is expected that the distribution of sea guide charts will inform the general public and educational sites of the importance of charts, and that workers at maritime and fisheries organizations will be able to easily and conveniently use information about major ports.”
Sea guide maps are provided free of charge to marine and fisheries-related organizations such as local maritime affairs and fisheries offices, the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives, Korea Coast Guard, and related universities, and are also planned to be distributed free of charge to the general public upon request from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency Chart Division (032-880-0560).
