ko-news-notices-329-8372c75064.title: Seasonal tidal-current observations planned for the Janghang navigation channel
ko-news-notices-329-8372c75064.text:
Seasonal tidal-current observations planned for the Janghang navigation channel
2022-03-02
Hydrographic survey to investigate tidal-current circulation at the entrance to the Janghang navigation channel
The West Sea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Office of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Chang-seop Choi) announced plans to observe tidal currents in all four seasons at the channel entrance to Janghang Port in Seocheon-gun Chungcheongnam-do.
The hydrographic survey vessel Hwanghaero will observe seasonal tidal currents near Gunsan Port Light Buoy No. 16 to improve tidal-current forecast accuracy.
Gunsan and Janghang are typical estuarine ports at the Geum River estuary on the central West Coast. Large national development projects including construction at the two ports are being implemented over successive years. Estuarine hydrodynamics and sedimentation are changing rapidly and changes to the wider marine environment could affect safe navigation for vessels of all sizes.
The office said that the observations would support safe navigation and efficient route planning for vessels entering and leaving both ports while clarifying changes in water circulation and sedimentation associated with changes in seabed topography.

ko-news-notices-328-8372c75064.title: Establishment of a marine environment technology center in Busan
ko-news-notices-328-8372c75064.text:
Establishment of a marine environment technology center in Busan
2022-03-02
A tentatively named Marine Environment Technology Center, which will be in charge of marine environment research and development, education, training, and promotion, is expected to be established in Busan.
Busan City announced on the 5th that as the Marine Pollution Prevention Act was completely revised and promulgated as the Marine Environment Management Act on the 19th of last month, the Marine Environment Management Corporation was established and at the same time, a Marine Environment Technology Center is needed as an affiliated organization. Accordingly, Busan City immediately began searching for a site for the center. Currently, potential sites include Centum City in U-dong, Haeundae-gu, Munhyeon Financial Complex in Munhyeon-dong, Nam-gu, and the coastline around Gijang-gun.
The center, which is scheduled to cost about 10 billion won (all government funds), will be built on a 5,000 pyeong site with a floor space of 1,000 pyeong, one underground floor, four above-ground floors, and a total floor area of ​​2,400 pyeong. This center will include a research center, education center, living room, red tide control practice center, coastal control training center, and equipment test team.
As soon as the site is confirmed by the end of this month, this center will establish a basic plan and enter into a design and construction company competition. After completing the selection of a construction company by the second half of this year, ground preparation and construction work will begin in the first half of next year and is scheduled to be completed around December next year.
An official from Busan City said, “Once the Marine Environment Technology Center is completed, it is expected that education and training on prevention of marine oil pollution, which is increasing every year, will be carried out efficiently at the national level at the level stipulated by international conventions.”
(Segye Ilbo Busan = Reporter Jeon Sang-hu)

ko-news-notices-327-8372c75064.title: Real-time Internet provision of new port seawater flow
ko-news-notices-327-8372c75064.text:
Real-time Internet provision of new port seawater flow
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency announced on the 5th that it will provide seawater flow observation results around Busan New Port in real time via the Internet (photo) starting this week.
The real-time seawater flow information service uses two high-frequency radars (HF-Radar) installed on the coasts of New Port and Geoje Island to observe seawater movement every hour from the entrance to Gadeoksuway to New Port and provides real-time information on the Internet.
Unlike general flow measurement equipment, high-frequency radar is a state-of-the-art device that measures the strength and direction of seawater flow by emitting high-frequency waves from a land base station to the sea surface and measuring the frequency change that is reflected and returned, enabling continuous observation even in situations such as nighttime, maritime fog, or typhoons.
Busan New Port has seen an increase in vessel traffic since its opening in January last year, and a significant increase in cargo volume is expected in the future, making it a sea area where seawater flow information services are essential.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, "The real-time seawater flow provision service is expected to not only contribute to the safe operation of ships entering and exiting New Port, Masan Port, and Jinhae Port, but also be used in various fields such as disaster prevention and search and rescue in the event of an oil pollution accident or marine accident."
Seawater flow information in the new port can be found on the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency website (http://www.nori.go.kr) You can check it in the marine data room (tide information). Reporter Lee Sang-yoon

ko-news-notices-326-8372c75064.title: View tide information through navigation
ko-news-notices-326-8372c75064.text:
View tide information through navigation
2022-03-02
It has become possible to search for information on high tides and low tides and sea splits along the coasts of the country even from cars.
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yoo-seop) announced that it will provide the predicted high and low tide times, sea level height and sea split information for 47 major ports along the national coast by including them in car navigation.
The number of users of tidal information is increasing day by day as the population of marine sports such as sea fishing is rapidly increasing due to the improvement of the people's living standards, and it is information that needs to be checked on site at any time. However, as it has been mainly provided through the Internet, there have been limitations in its use in time and space.
In order to use tidal forecasts and sea split information through a navigation system, you can purchase a navigation system that contains tidal information, or those using a navigation system can simply update the information through the website of the map maker. The information included will be updated with new information every year.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “The tidal information included in the navigation this time is an opportunity to overcome the limitations of on-line and off-line, and is expected to be useful in the distribution of various information, including various marine information, in the future.”
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency is currently discussing with each company to ensure that tidal information, which is currently included in only one navigation program development company, will be included in all navigation systems within the first half of this year and that more diverse information can be included.

ko-news-notices-323-8372c75064.title: Busan North Port Redevelopment Comprehensive Plan Briefing Meeting Held
ko-news-notices-323-8372c75064.text:
Busan North Port Redevelopment Comprehensive Plan Briefing Meeting Held
2022-03-02
On the 27th, approximately 150 people from all walks of life, including President Roh Moo-hyun, attended.
The Busan North Port Redevelopment Comprehensive Plan Reporting Meeting was held at the Busan Port Authority on the 27th with the attendance of approximately 150 political and business figures, including President Roh Moo-hyun, Minister of Oceans and Fisheries Kim Seong-jin, and local lawmakers.
The briefing session was conducted in the following order: a report on the current status of the North Port redevelopment comprehensive plan, a video broadcast, and a meeting with attendees.
In the comprehensive report on the North Port redevelopment, Minister Kim Seong-jin reported that the North Port will be developed into a world-class urban marine tourist destination as a landmark that can represent the future and hope of Korea, like Sydney in Australia and Palm Island in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
At the briefing session, plans to connect the city center by utilizing the railway land adjacent to the North Port and plans to secure an alternative pier early due to the redevelopment of the traditional pier were also reported. Following the briefing, President Roh moved to the Lotte Hotel and had lunch with 300 people, including local businessmen and civic groups, to collect various opinions from people from all walks of life on development plans for the Busan region.
The North Port Redevelopment Project is a large-scale national project with a total of 9.3 trillion won invested from 2008 to 2020. The target area is North Port 1, 2, 3, 4 and Central Pier, and has a total area of ​​430,000 pyeong. The direct effect of the North Port redevelopment project is estimated to be 32 trillion won in industrial stimulation and 120,000 jobs created.
■ Inquiries: Busan North Port Redevelopment Event Planning Team Team Leader Byeon Jae-young, Secretary Oh Won-man Tel: 02-3674-6391

ko-news-notices-322-8372c75064.title: Promotion of joint use of marine research vessels
ko-news-notices-322-8372c75064.text:
Promotion of joint use of marine research vessels
2022-03-02
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries has decided to promote joint use of marine research vessels to ensure efficient use of marine research vessels operated by affiliated and related organizations.
In order to jointly operate marine research vessels, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries plans to disclose next year's marine research vessel operation plan on its website to encourage the active participation of relevant universities, research institutes, and other marine-related institutions, and to grant incentives to institutions with excellent joint operation performance.
In order to promote the joint use of all research equipment, including research vessels, in the long term, it was decided to prepare institutional measures such as establishing a tentatively named ‘Marine Research Vessel and Survey Equipment Joint Utilization Center’.
Possible joint research projects include 71 tasks including the National Institute of Fisheries Science's fisheries resource survey, 21 tasks including the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency's survey of Korean coastal ocean currents, and 60 tasks including the Korea Ocean Research Institute's sediment movement phenomenon and sedimentation environment research.
Currently, a total of 25 research vessels under the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, including 15 for the Fisheries Research Institute, 7 for the Ocean Research Institute, and 3 for the Ocean Research Institute, were built at a cost of KRW 100 billion based on new ships, with annual operating costs reaching KRW 10 billion.
However, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries predicts that if research vessels are jointly used, more than 10 million won per day will be saved per vessel.
This year, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries provided marine research vessels to companies, research institutes, universities, and individual researchers for 42 projects through its website.
■ Inquiry: Maritime Development Division Manager Kwon Seok-chang, Secretary Jin Jun-ho (☎02-3674-6532) / joon469@momaf.go

ko-news-notices-321-8372c75064.title: Establishment of Ulsan Port Authority in the second half of 2007, accelerating port privatization
ko-news-notices-321-8372c75064.text:
Establishment of Ulsan Port Authority in the second half of 2007, accelerating port privatization
2022-03-02
Ulsan Port Authority Establishment Planning Team begins operation from January of the new year
Ulsan Port Authority is expected to be established as early as July next year. On the 22nd, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries jointly formed the Ulsan Port Authority Establishment Preparation Committee with related ministries and Ulsan Metropolitan City, and announced that it would establish an Establishment Promotion Planning Team as a working body to support the committee and begin work on January 2 of the new year.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries plans to establish the Ulsan Port Authority in July next year after six months of preparations, including evaluation of national property, investment, and organization and personnel composition.
The Ulsan Port Authority Establishment Committee is chaired by the Vice Minister of Oceans and Fisheries and consists of seven members, including the Director of the National Treasury of the Ministry of Finance and Economy, the Director of the Public Innovation Division of the Ministry of Planning and Budget, the Deputy Mayor of Ulsan Metropolitan City, the Director of the Economic and Trade Bureau, and the personnel of the Ulsan Development Research Institute. It will deliberate and decide on major matters related to the establishment of the Corporation, such as recommending the first president and appointing port members, until the Port Corporation is launched.
The Establishment Promotion Planning Team, which is established as a dedicated organization within the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, consists of a total of 9 people, including employees dispatched from Ulsan Metropolitan City and the Ulsan Regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Office. The planning team will carry out various tasks such as appraisal and investment of state-owned properties necessary for the establishment of the Port Authority, establishment and implementation of staff recruitment plans, registration of establishment, and establishment commemoration ceremony.
So far, Ulsan Port has been evaluated as a port that can successfully introduce Port Authority (PA), following Busan Port and Incheon Port, with stable port revenue and high financial independence among national trade ports.
As of 2005, Ulsan Port's cargo handling volume was 162 million tons, ranking third after Busan Port (217 million tons), and its port usage fee income was 41.7 billion won, which is evaluated as having a foundation for financial independence.
Once the Ulsan Port Authority is established, it is expected that it will be possible to lay the foundation for Ulsan Port to develop into a central port for liquid cargo in Northeast Asia through the introduction of private management techniques and marketing activities that reflect the characteristics of the port.
An official from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced that they plan to gradually introduce PA and privatize ports that have a large impact on the national economy and have a high level of financial independence, such as Yeosu and Gwangyang ports.
■ Inquiry: Shipping Logistics Bureau Port Logistics Department Manager Eom Gi-du Secretary Seo Jeong-ho 02-3674-6663 / F 3674-6665

ko-news-notices-320-8372c75064.title: Establishment of comprehensive marine environment management foundation
ko-news-notices-320-8372c75064.text:
Establishment of comprehensive marine environment management foundation
2022-03-02
On the 22nd, three bills, including the Marine Environment Management Act, passed the National Assembly.
In the future, pre- and post-management of indiscriminate use of the ocean will be thorough, and monitoring of various sources of marine pollution will be further strengthened.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced that the ‘Marine Environment Management Act’, which aims to comprehensively and systematically manage the marine environment and actively respond to new marine environmental demands, passed the plenary session of the National Assembly on the 22nd.
Accordingly, the ‘Sea Area Use Evaluation System’ has been introduced, and anyone who wishes to engage in marine use activities above a certain scale, such as collecting sea aggregates, must undergo a ‘Sea Area Use Impact Assessment’ after collecting opinions from stakeholders.
In addition, even after the impact assessment, if damage to the marine environment occurs due to violation of obligations by ocean users, the government may take necessary measures such as license cancellation, business suspension, and restoration to original condition.
In addition, a new reporting system for marine facilities will be established to strengthen preventive management of marine pollution sources.
A project management team for each sea area will also be established to intensively manage polluted sea areas such as Sihwa Lake and Masan Bay.
In addition, systematic investigations will be conducted on new sources of marine pollution, such as persistent organic pollutants, and the use of harmful anti-fouling paints that have a detrimental effect on the marine environment will be banned.
In addition, in order to produce accurate and reliable marine environmental data, a quality control system for marine environmental measurement and analysis institutions was implemented and a ‘measurement and analysis ability certificate’ was granted to suitable measurement and analysis institutions as a result of evaluations such as verification of data, thereby increasing the accuracy and reliability of basic marine environmental data.
The Korea Marine Pollution Control Association, which was established after the Sea Prince accident in 1996 and has mainly been in charge of oil control work, has been expanded and reorganized into the Marine Environment Management Corporation and is being fostered as a comprehensive marine environment specialized organization that can comprehensively carry out various projects necessary for the conservation and management of the marine environment in addition to oil control work.
With the enactment of this law, marine environment management has so far been limited to passive activities such as post-processing in the event of pollution accidents, but now we have various policy tools to carry out more active marine environment management.
In addition, amendments to the Fishery Products Quality Control Act, the Fisheries Promotion Act, and the Oil Pollution Damages Guarantee Act also passed the National Assembly on this day.
The Fishery Products Quality Control Act strengthens penalties for violators of false labeling of origin and genetically modified marine products to ensure the safety of marine products.
The Farming Fisheries Promotion Act transfers government affairs, such as the establishment of aquatic disease management offices, to mayors and county governors.
The Oil Pollution Damage Compensation Guarantee Act makes administrative procedures transparent, such as skipping entry and exit inspection when a ship owner submits relevant documents such as an insurance contract certificate, and requiring advance notice at the time of entry and inspection and notification of the results.

ko-news-notices-319-8372c75064.title: Electronic charts, the first government publication to adopt a license sales method
ko-news-notices-319-8372c75064.text:
Electronic charts, the first government publication to adopt a license sales method
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yu-seop) announced that it will introduce a license sales method to promote the use of electronic navigation charts and provide services that meet user needs.
The license supply service being introduced grants systematic maintenance service rights for one year upon purchase of electronic navigation charts, and many advanced maritime countries are introducing and operating this sales method.
The Korea Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency has been servicing 212 types of electronic charts for coasts across Korea since 2000. Until now, the price per type of electronic charts had been two-tiered: initial purchase fee (KRW 20,500) and renewal fee (KRW 9,600).
Accordingly, users' demands for price reductions have increased, they have been exposed to the risk of maritime accidents due to the use of non-updated data, and there have been difficulties in international distribution of electronic navigation charts due to differences in supply methods with overseas developed countries.
With the introduction of the licensing method, the price for one year of use of one type of electronic chart will be reduced to 11,000 won, and the quality of the electronic chart update service is expected to improve by managing users more effectively.
An official from the Korea Maritime Research Institute said, “By introducing a license supply method, we have laid the foundation for expanding supply not only domestically but also overseas, and it is expected that price reduction and systematic quality control will expand the number of users of electronic charts, greatly contributing to navigational safety.” He said.

ko-news-notices-318-8372c75064.title: Thermal power generation, electricity generation using leftover water
ko-news-notices-318-8372c75064.text:
Thermal power generation, electricity generation using leftover water
2022-03-02
November 13, 2006 | Post | Kang Jeong-hoon, Donga Ilbo reporter ㆍmanman@donga.com |
A way to generate electricity using effluent (sea water coolant), which was discarded after cooling boiler steam during the thermal power generation process, has been opened.
Korea South-East Power Co., Ltd. (CEO Park Hee-gap), a subsidiary of KEPCO, announced on the 12th, “The offshore small hydro power plant within the Samcheonpo Thermal Power Plant in Hai-myeon, Goseong-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, which began construction in March 2004, has been completed, completed power generation tests and comprehensive commissioning, and recently entered commercial operation.”
This is the world's first small hydro power generation using discharged water from a thermal power plant and the ebb and flow of the tide.
In particular, Korean companies such as Halla Industrial Development and Ssangyong Construction took on the difficult construction work such as dam construction, excluding German-made turbines (water turbines) and generators, and South-East Power is also preparing to apply for an international patent for this power generation system and sell the technology overseas.
The 8m high, 110m long dam was installed on the public water surface 60m downstream of the outlet, and the discharge water is 22 tons per second, with a maximum effective drop of 4.93 m.
This power plant, which cost 18 billion won to build, has a rated capacity of 3,000 kW, which is similar to that of Pocheon in Gyeonggi Province and Yeongwol Small Hydro Power in Gangwon Province. The annual power generation was analyzed to be 22,726MWh, the oil substitution effect was 5,690 tons (KRW 2.4 billion), and the carbon dioxide reduction effect was analyzed to be 17,300 tons.
South-East Power is constructing a small hydro power plant at Yeongheung Thermal Power Plant with the goal of completion in October next year, and plans to introduce it at Taean, Dangjin Thermal Power Plant and nuclear power plant. When these small hydro power plants are completed, the annual power generation will be 200,000 MWh and the oil replacement effect will be 20.8 billion won per year.
Small hydro power plants built in valleys and other areas can operate only in the summer when there is plenty of water, but thermal power plants can operate all year round.
Nam Ho-gi, executive director of Korea South-East Power Company, said, “Foreign engineers were also surprised by the idea of ​​producing electricity from discharged water. The development of large-capacity power sources using marine energy has given momentum to the new and renewable energy development project promoted by the government.”
:small hydropower:
Power generation with a facility capacity of 10,000 kW or less that produces electricity with a high-performance, low-height turbine using the flow of water such as a river or waterfall. It has been built in about 30 locations since 1982.

ko-news-notices-317-8372c75064.title: Global warming and weather change
ko-news-notices-317-8372c75064.text:
Global warming and weather change
2022-03-02
If the average rises by 6 degrees, the Earth will be destroyed.
Chief writer Lee Wan-woo
Climate change due to global warming is emerging as a hot topic today. After the Tokyo Convention took effect, the smokestack industry, which contributes to global warming, improved its carbon dioxide emission facilities, and the oil refining industry mandated desulfurization facilities, but air pollution still exceeds the standard amount. In London's pollution market, companies that emit a lot of pollution are working hard to secure carbon dioxide emissions rights, but air pollution is already so widespread that each country cannot afford emissions rights.
The industry that has the greatest impact on global warming is the automobile industry. The exhaust fumes and carbon dioxide (CO2) emitted by cars driving down the road have the greatest impact on air pollution.
Recently, the U.S. state of California filed a lawsuit seeking damages from the state government against automobile companies that have significantly contributed to global warming. The state of California filed a lawsuit against six auto companies, including General Motors and Toyota, seeking billions of dollars in damages, holding them responsible for global warming.
California has already spent billions of dollars on marine erosion prevention and flood control. They claim that this is due to abnormal weather conditions caused by global warming and that the automobile industry, which has affected global warming, should compensate. Even though regulations had already been established to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the automobile industry below the standard amount, the industry failed to implement them, leading to a lawsuit being filed.
As a result of the lawsuit, if the automobile industry loses the suit for damages, the automobile industry will inevitably incur a huge cost burden. Depending on the outcome of the lawsuit, it is expected that exports to the United States by domestic automobile industries such as Hyundai Motor Company and Kia Motors will be affected.
The effects of global warming can be seen throughout Earth's long history. 200 million years ago, at the end of the Permian period, the Earth, which was the home of various animals and plants, turned into ashes overnight. It was a disaster caused by a series of volcanic eruptions that erupted lava and caused the Earth's temperature to rise rapidly. Over the next 100,000 years, dark red acid rain fell from the sky, the sea spewed out terrible methane gas, and 95% of life on Earth became extinct.
The continued abnormal weather events this century are analyzed as the effects of global warming. A study was recently published in which an expert calculated that the temperature rise at the time was only 6 degrees Celsius. Additionally, if the current temperature rise trend continues, it is estimated that the Earth's temperature will rise by 6 degrees Celsius over the next few decades. It's no different from having a terrible outcome predicted.
The current average temperature of the Earth is about 15 degrees. The upper limit of the annual temperature increase rate is 2.5 degrees. In Europe and Europe, the unit of measurement for temperature is expressed in degrees Fahrenheit. Americans' favorite temperature is 70 degrees Fahrenheit, which is 21 degrees Celsius. The limit temperature for humans is 37 degrees Celsius. The average human body temperature is 37 degrees, so the optimal temperature of the atmosphere should not exceed 37 degrees. Survival is possible only when the temperature is maintained below 37 degrees. When the patient's body temperature reaches 40 degrees, he or she goes into torticollis due to high fever.
The hottest time on Earth was last year, when temperatures in some parts of the United States soared to 115 degrees Fahrenheit. This is 46.1 degrees Celsius. It has already exceeded the human body temperature limit by 9 degrees. The temperature difference on Earth between winter and summer, and between cold and hot regions, is considered to be an average of 4 degrees. The theory is that if the temperature rises by just 6 degrees due to warming, humanity will not be able to withstand it and the Earth will perish.
As the ice sheet in Antarctica melts, global warming is accelerating, with sea levels rising and average temperatures rising by more than 0.1 degrees every year. The island nation of Tuvalu is submerged in water due to rising sea levels, and all citizens are migrating to neighboring countries. Conflicts due to global warming will occur everywhere. California's claim for damages from the automobile industry is only the beginning. The outbreak of war, launching rockets, nuclear tests, or using nuclear weapons affects global warming, and air pollution and water shortages due to depletion of water resources also affect global warming. Ultimately, a situation will arise where humanity will have to completely stop urban development, which is a convenience facility for life, in order to preserve forest resources that neutralize atmospheric temperature.

ko-news-notices-316-8372c75064.title: Mainland China struggles with water shortages
ko-news-notices-316-8372c75064.text:
Mainland China struggles with water shortages
2022-03-02
China's water shortage is becoming increasingly serious. Last year, one in four Chinese people suffered from water shortages. The amount of food production reduced due to water shortage amounts to 35 million tons, or 8.2% of total production.
As China's population peaks at 1.6 billion in 2030, the entire country is expected to suffer from the worst thirst.
▽Water at the mouth of the Yellow River has decreased by 91% in 40 years = According to the South China Morning Post on the 7th, the total amount of water flowing into the sea from the Yellow River in the 1960s averaged 49.6 billion tons every year. In the 1990s, it decreased to 14.1 billion tons, and after 2002, it decreased to 4.65 billion tons. This is a whopping 90.6% decrease compared to 40 years ago.
Currently, the water utilization rate of the Yellow River is about 60%. According to international standards, the utilization limit of river water is 40%. Exceeding this standard will have a serious negative impact on the surrounding ecosystem.
The water resource utilization rate of the Huaihe River and Liaohe River reaches around 60%. The Haihe River, which flows through Beijing to Tianjin, uses up 100% of its water before it reaches the sea.
▽World average of water resources per capita: 1/4 = According to data from the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), China's total water resources last year were 2.83 trillion tons, ranking 6th in the world after Brazil, Russia, the United States, Canada, and Indonesia. However, water resources per person are only 2,140 tons, which is only a quarter of the world average.
However, 1.7 trillion tons simply flows away during floods or flows underground, so the actual usable water resources are 1.1 trillion tons, which is only 840 tons per person.
According to China's Ministry of Water Supply, about 400 out of 669 cities across China are suffering from water shortages. Among these, 110 cities are in a serious situation. 320 million people, or 24.4% of China's population, are experiencing water shortages.
Due to the excessive use of scarce water resources, it is difficult for even plants to cover the surface of 4.42 million km², or 46% of the entire country, including Hebei, Shanxi, and Inner Mongolia autonomous regions.
▽Forecast = China’s total water use last year was 563.3 billion tons. In the future, water use is expected to increase every year, reaching 700 to 800 billion tons in 2030. This amounts to 89% of the total amount of water available for use at this time, which is 800 to 900 billion tons. This is only possible if the average use limit of 40% of the river water is exceeded.
To solve this problem, the Chinese government plans to invest 1 trillion yuan (approximately 120 trillion won) by 2010 to improve water facilities and prepare for water shortages.
However, since the average precipitation is only 600 mm, it is expected to be difficult to fundamentally solve the water shortage crisis.
At the annual academic conference of the Chinese Hydraulic Society held in Hefei, the capital of Anhui Province, Vice Minister Husui of China's Water Ministry warned, "As we currently have a water shortage of 40 billion tons every year, if we do not make thorough preparations 25 years from now when water shortage reaches its peak, a huge disaster could occur."
Source: Beijing = Ha Jong-dae, Donga Ilbo correspondent, orionha@donga.com |

ko-news-notices-315-8372c75064.title: “Conservation of the marine environment is a shared responsibility of all people on earth”
ko-news-notices-315-8372c75064.text:
“Conservation of the marine environment is a shared responsibility of all people on earth”
2022-03-02
The beginning of a new sea movement
“Conservation of the marine environment is a shared responsibility of all people on earth”
2006/10/13
Reporter Yoon Mi-sook
On the 10th, the Korea Federation for Environment Ocean Committee held a discussion commemorating its inauguration under the theme of ‘Sea of Life, Sea of Crisis’ at the Small Auditorium of the National Assembly Library. Includes a summary of the discussion speaker's speech. /Edit Since Yusa, the sea has been an infinitely generous being to us humans. It has provided us with a variety of food, provided economic benefits and channels for exchange, provided us with peace of mind, and has become the basis for our survival. However, while life in the land area changed significantly, the sea began to deteriorate steadily. Humans have worsened the health of the ocean in a variety of ways, from landfill, illegal dumping, and oil spills to increasingly intense fishing practices and marine sand extraction. These actions threaten the diversity of marine species and further sharply deteriorate the quality of human life.
Reporter Yang Gye-tak
The Korean Federation for Environmental Movement is holding a campaign to protect “Antarctica of Life, Antarctica in Crisis” to commemorate the launch of the Ocean Committee at Cheonggye Plaza in Seoul on the morning of the 10th. Along with models of penguins, elephant seals, minke whales, sea lions, krill, and albatrosses that symbolize the Antarctic ecosystem, it informs citizens of the crisis facing Antarctica and conveys to citizens the need for Antarctic protection.
Insufficient response to marine environment
Moreover, although Korea is a maritime country with sea on three sides, its response to the marine environment has been progressing at a very low level. The reality is that there are only relief or one-time events limited to local areas. Unfortunately, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, which should be at the forefront of research and analysis of ocean health measures, has only focused on port construction and has been struggling due to budget imbalance and imbalance for a long time. If things continue like this, even the pessimistic alternative theory that it would be better to transfer marine environment conservation policies to the Ministry of Environment will no longer be a completely unfamiliar discussion.
The consequences of human actions on land all affect the ocean. Most of the marine waste comes from land and drifts, and various wastewater discarded from land flows straight into the sea. Toxic wastewater and waste that are difficult to dispose of are poured into the sea under the plausible justification of ‘ocean dumping.’ Large-scale coastal reclamation is currently in progress despite its harmful effects being widely known, and the remaining natural coastline is disappearing in the name of tourist coastal roads or coastal maintenance. Even now, the breakwater is being built in a pathetic way that causes it to rot due to stagnant water in the bay, and the current state of our maritime industry is that the contradiction of ‘a fish eating its own flesh’ is constantly being played out by digging up sand from the seabed and using it to build a port.
Inability to control desire for development
Although the Coastal Management Act was enacted only belatedly, it is insufficient to control the development desires of local governments. Some local governments even believe that the Coastal Management Act is a law that only requires humans to manage and develop the coast, so they are consistent with a rather ambitious plan to build three or four coastal golf courses along with the creation of a coastal industrial complex. These are natural results of a lack of publicity for national policies.
It may be late, but despite knowing the facts, we are trying to solve the problem that has been postponed all along by gathering the will of the citizens. Although the work done by the government or affiliated research institutes, the methods, and the range of issues raised may be slightly different, in the end, the representative discussion to keep and save the ocean healthy is not expected to be any different. I believe that a serious ocean protection movement will be able to establish itself when the government, research institutes, and civic groups share their respective roles and communicate with each other.
In fact, the sea movement is not without its difficulties for ordinary citizens to access. First of all, it is too deep and too wide. It's too hot in the summer and too cold in the winter, and currents, waves, typhoons, eddies, tsunamis, and interactions with distant oceans are a challenge. It cannot be denied that access was not easy due to limitations in the survey method, the vastness of the survey volume, and excessive costs. However, with difficulty, the Sea Committee of the Korean Federation for Environmental Movements was formed to gather the voluntary arguments of several activists who have lived with the sea and seek to view and approach Korea's seas and the world's seas from a new perspective.
Protecting global common property
With great difficulty, money was raised to increase the number of rubber boats to two, local training for marine adaptation has begun, and it is expected that a campaign vessel will be available in the near future. Since the desire to care for and love the ocean has already been firmly established, all that remains is to take it step by step, starting with things that are accessible and possible, such as suggesting alternatives or making joint efforts. Based on the experience of monitoring various ocean problems in each region for over a dozen years, activists will continue to work in solidarity and struggle for a healthier and more beautiful ocean for our oceans. In addition, we will be more active in solidarity with various international organizations through activities to eradicate ocean dumping to implement the London Agreement, the Antarctic Conservation Union, which we have been involved with for a long time, the whale protection movement in connection with Greenpeace, and the London Agreement.
This is because the sea is a huge axis that connects the world. It is a global common property and a shared responsibility of all people on the planet. Moreover, in order to secure proud sovereignty as a maritime nation with seas on three sides, it is urgent to restore our identity through efforts to preserve the marine environment.
Yoon Mi-sook, member of the Ocean Committee of the Korea Federation for Environment

ko-news-notices-314-8372c75064.title: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries establishes land-based marine pollution source management strategy
ko-news-notices-314-8372c75064.text:
Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries establishes land-based marine pollution source management strategy
2022-03-02
Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries establishes land-based marine pollution source management strategy
Source: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries
(Seoul = Newswire) October 13, 2006-- A detailed action strategy has been established to protect the marine environment from land-based activities.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced on the 23rd that, in collaboration with the Ministry of Environment, it has established a ‘National Action Strategy’ for land-based pollution source management, which aims to invest a total of $6.4 billion (approximately KRW 6.4 trillion) by 2010 in three areas: land-based pollution source management, marine ecosystem conservation, legal system improvement, and policy base strengthening.
This action strategy will be submitted to the 2nd intergovernmental meeting on the ‘Global Action Plan (GPA) for protecting the marine environment from land-based activities’ held in Beijing, China from the 16th to the 20th.
※ GPA: Global Program of Action for the Protection of the Marine Environment from Land-based Activities
According to the implementation strategy, coastal management regional plans of relevant local governments will be established early to ensure implementation of the integrated coastal management plan established in 2000. As of last year, 17 out of 80 local governments had completed establishment and 25 were in the process of establishment.
In addition, the function of the ‘Central Coastal Interest Committee’ will be strengthened to review whether coastal development plans such as ports and fishing ports, coastal use activities according to individual laws, etc. are consistent with the integrated coastal plan.
The action plan also calls for the establishment of a joint management system between ministries, including the establishment of a comprehensive estuary management plan, jointly with related ministries such as the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, the Ministry of Environment, and the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry starting next year.
In addition, starting this year, the National Institute of Fisheries Science of the Ministry of Oceans and the National Institute of Environmental Research of the Ministry of Environment will jointly establish an ‘estuary monitoring system’ to lay the scientific foundation for estuary management.
In addition, in order to improve the marine environment, which is the final receptor for land-based pollutants, the ‘pollution factor burden principle’, which jointly shares finances with upstream regions, will be introduced, and a basin management system for marine inflow waste will be introduced in the Han River and Nakdong River.
In addition, the implementation strategy involves non-governmental organizations (NGOs) such as the Han River Citizens' Alliance and Sihwahwa Environmental Protection Agency in national research projects to strengthen the pre-coordination function of policies such as collecting local opinions and promoting them, and networks with stakeholders through information systems such as the coastal information system, tidal flat information system, and waste marine discharge comprehensive information network are also activated.
In addition, we continuously provide training for honorary wetland guides and natural environment guides, and promote local residents' participation in environmental conservation by publishing guidebooks and holding seminars.
In order to strengthen the policy decision support system based on scientific data, a basic survey of the marine ecosystem will be conducted from this year to 2015, and a public-private cooperation program will be developed by activating private participation in marine environment monitoring projects such as estuary surveys and marine environment measurement network operation.
In addition, from this year to 2008, the ‘National Marine Environment Information Integration System’ will be established to integrate national data from the National Institute of Fisheries Science, Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency, Coast Guard, and Ocean Research Institute, thereby increasing the disclosure and accessibility of marine environment information produced by the nation.
In addition, next year, management priorities appropriate for marine characteristics, such as domestic sewage in Masan Bay and heavy metals and hazardous chemicals in Gwangyang Bay, will be set to efficiently use financial resources and establish a reasonable management plan.
In particular, a plan to apply the ‘emissions trading system’, which is being piloted for air pollution, to water pollution is being promoted as a long-term task.
The implementation strategy also plans to revise the Coastal Management Act to introduce the coastal use zoning system and the Total Coastal Pollution Control Act to introduce the Total Pollution Control System next year, and to suppress indiscriminate reclamation by revising laws related to reclamation, such as the Public Waters Reclamation Act and the Public Waters Management Act.
In addition, international cooperation will be strengthened, including continued cooperation in the field of marine environment conservation with neighboring countries such as China, Japan, and Russia, and the establishment of the Korea-US Environmental Cooperation Joint Committee with the United States.
In order to efficiently pursue this project, a total of $6.4 billion will be invested, including $320 million for ecosystem conservation and restoration, $5.83 billion for reduction of land-based pollutants, and $270 million for strengthening policy base.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries has not received adequate evaluation from the international community despite Korea investing a large amount of budget to manage land-based pollution sources and implementing advanced management policies such as implementation of the Total Pollution Control System. However, the submission of this national action strategy is expected to significantly improve our image.
Meanwhile, GPA was adopted by 108 countries, including Korea, Japan, and the European Union, at the Washington Conference of the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) in 1995, and the first intergovernmental conference was held in Montreal, Canada in November 2001.
More than 100 countries will participate in this second intergovernmental meeting, and about 34 countries, including Korea and China, are expected to announce their national implementation strategies.
The GPA Intergovernmental Conference is held every five years and the secretariat is located in The Hague, Netherlands.
Media Inquiry
Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Marine Policy Bureau Marine Environment Division Manager Ki-Ji Han 02-3674-6545

ko-news-notices-313-8372c75064.title: Relocation of Daeheuksando Tide Observatory
ko-news-notices-313-8372c75064.text:
Relocation of Daeheuksando Tide Observatory
2022-03-02
Relocation of Daeheuksando Tide Observatory
Relocation to the landing wharf by December
Entry date: 2006. 10.24
The Daeheuksando Tide Observatory will be relocated to monitor sea level changes and marine weather in the southern West Sea.
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency West Sea Ocean Research Office (Director Choi Chang-seop) announced on the 23rd that it will relocate the tide level observation station located next to the Daeheuksando Port Passenger Terminal to the landing wharf in order to more precisely observe changes in sea level in the southern West Sea and provide various tide information services.
The current tide station has been recording tidal waves arriving from offshore and other marine information in the southern West Sea area transmitted from the open sea for 36 years since its construction at Heuksan Island Port in 1970.
However, due to the aging of facilities and observation equipment and the expansion of the passenger terminal, the need to build or relocate a state-of-the-art tide station for accurate ocean observations has emerged.
Accordingly, construction of the new tide observatory will begin this month and is scheduled to be completed at the end of December. With the relocation of the tide level observatory, it will serve as a comprehensive marine observatory that monitors various marine information by providing real-time tide level data essential for the arrival and departure of large ships, as well as observing sea level changes (tidal level changes), sea water characteristics (water temperature and salinity), and marine weather (temperature, barometric pressure, wind direction and speed).
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, "We plan to provide various observed marine information in real time through the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency website (www.nori.go.kr)," and added, "This data is expected to be greatly used for fishing activities, ship operations, port construction, and the marine environment, as well as support for disaster prevention work." Mokpo = Reporter Jeon Ho-young

ko-news-notices-312-8372c75064.title: ‘Contemplating measures’ for global temperature and sea level rise
ko-news-notices-312-8372c75064.text:
‘Contemplating measures’ for global temperature and sea level rise
2022-03-02
‘Contemplating measures’ for global temperature and sea level rise
There is much controversy as to whether global warming is the direct cause of abnormal climate, but scientists also acknowledge that the Alaskan glacier has shrunk significantly over the past 100 years, raising global sea levels by 10 to 25 cm and raising the average global temperature to about 0.3 to 0.6 degrees Celsius.
According to data released by the government in December 1994, Korea also reported that global warming is bringing about various changes in the fields of water resources, agriculture, forests, ecosystems, coastlines, and coastal structures, according to the ‘National Report on Climate Change Convention’.
#Global warming and weather changes
The global warming phenomenon is believed to be caused by the phenomenon in which solar radiation energy (ultraviolet rays) entering the Earth's atmosphere falls on the Earth without being filtered due to the destruction of the ozone layer in the stratosphere above the Earth's atmosphere due to the excessive use of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
As the global temperature rises due to direct solar irradiation of the Earth and the use of greenhouse effect gases such as carbon dioxide, methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and aerosol particles, part of the solar energy reaching the Earth's surface from the troposphere (10 to 15 km from the surface) must be emitted back to the outside of the Earth through the tropospheric boundary in the form of infrared energy, but these gases act like a greenhouse in the upper troposphere of the Earth. This is a phenomenon that causes the temperature of the Earth to rise by forming a film and preventing the release of energy.
The Earth's greenhouse gases that cause global warming have the greatest effect through the actual water vapor in the troposphere, which is due to the influence of the entire Earth's energy flow and temperature system.
The most important thing is that carbon dioxide generated during human activities is 55%, chlorofluorohydrocarbons 24%, methane 15%, and nitrous oxide 6%.
When 1 kg of each of these substances is emitted into the atmosphere, the warming intensity is 21 times that of methane, 21 times that of methane, 300 to 3,500 times that of chlorofluorohydrocarbons, and 1,500 times that of nitrous oxide when carbon dioxide is set as 1 and the evaluation period is 100 years. Although it is small in terms of the overall composition, its contribution is quite large.
Accordingly, the second report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) in 1995 stated, ‘The impact of global warming and climate change on human activities is already being seen, and the main cause is the use of fossil fuels and the increase in greenhouse gases due to agriculture.’
Comparing the concentration levels of major greenhouse gases before the Industrial Revolution and in 1992, carbon dioxide increased from 280 ppm to 360 ppm, and methane increased from 770 ppb to 1,720 ppb.
When the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere doubles, the isotherm line shifts, affecting the existence of 1/3 of the Earth's forest area. Considering the tendency of forest destruction to occur during this change and greatly weaken the Earth's carbon dioxide absorption function, it can be estimated that a considerable amount of damage has been done in the past 100 years.
In particular, climate experts predict that by 2050, carbon dioxide will reach 575ppm, twice the level before the Industrial Revolution, and by 2100, it will reach 1,330ppm, resulting in a rise in global temperature by as little as 1.7℃ or as much as 5.3℃.
As a result, various weather changes occur throughout the Earth, with desert areas accelerating desertification and drying out many areas, while some areas turn into wet areas with a lot of rain.
There are concerns that these changes will change the distribution of arid areas, semi-arid areas and farmland, disrupt the ecosystem, and lead to the extinction of many plants and animals.
And the current biggest concern is the decline of glaciers in polar regions and alpine regions. Although accurate predictions are impossible, it is expected that sea levels will rise by 15 to 19 cm over the next 100 years, and in the worst case, the territories of low-lying countries where 20% of the world's population are concentrated will be flooded.
This is related to food production, and it is expected that the global food shortage will further worsen.
#International trends related to global warming
▲Climate Convention
In the late 1980s, direct evidence of global warming, such as increased carbon dioxide concentration and rise in global temperature, appeared around the world, and in the 1990s, signs of actual abnormal climate appeared.
In response to this, in 1988, the IPCC, an official intergovernmental organization responding to climate change, was first formed by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP), and finally, in 1992, the ‘Convention on Climate Change’ was adopted as a UN basic convention at the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), the largest environmental conference of mankind.
The main goals of this Convention on Climate Change to prevent global warming, which came into effect in March 1994, are to prepare national reports on the greenhouse gas emissions and absorption status of each country, establish and implement domestic policies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and reduce carbon dioxide emissions to the 1990 level by 2000 in developed countries.
At the COP, in which 168 countries participated, 38 developed countries, including the United States, agreed to reduce total greenhouse gas emissions by 5.2% on average between 2008 and 2012 compared to 1990, and by -8 to +5% by country.
It also emphasized efficient management of energy, protection and promotion of sinks such as forests that can absorb greenhouse gases, development of environmentally friendly technologies related to new and renewable energy, abolition of market imperfections, financial incentives, and subsidies that cause an increase in greenhouse gases, reform of policies and measures, and management of the transportation sector and waste.
In addition, at this meeting, for the first time, the ‘Joint Implementation System’ and ‘Emission Trading System’ were introduced as economic means to reduce carbon dioxide, and there was an attempt to submit an agenda for discussion on ‘Voluntary Agreements’ of each country to encourage the participation of developing countries, but it was met with strong opposition from several developing countries, including India.
*Emission Trading = As a policy tool that can be applied to a wide range of environmental issues along with the emission charging system, it is a property rights system designed to clearly define the rights and obligations for polluting activities or pollution prevention activities and achieve environmental quality at the minimum social cost through autonomous adjustment.
It is a system that sets the global warming gas emissions and gives each country a certain amount of emission limit. If it exceeds this limit, it purchases emissions rights, and if it falls below this limit, it sells the remaining amount.
*Joint Implementation = This is a system in which a country, such as a developing country, changes its inefficient energy industrial structure to a highly efficient industrial structure through the expansion of social overhead capital or the development of technology, and as the country's fossil fuel use decreases, the reduced amount is recognized as a reduction for any developed country that implemented this in return.
*Carbon tax = It is also called carbon dioxide tax (COP's official term, carbon-dioxide tax) or carbon burnt tax. The tax is imposed differently depending on the carbon content of fossil fuels, and the goal is to fundamentally suppress the consumption of fossil fuels.

ko-news-notices-311-8372c75064.title: If there was a radioactive leak, it would take 5 days for Gangneung to be contaminated.
ko-news-notices-311-8372c75064.text:
If there was a radioactive leak, it would take 5 days for Gangneung to be contaminated.
2022-03-02
“If there was a radioactive leak, it would take 5 days for Gangneung to be contaminated.”
Although it is unlikely, Cookie News reported that if radioactivity leaked from North Korea's underground nuclear test, the entire groundwater on the Korean Peninsula could become radioactively contaminated.
The Korea Institute of Nuclear Safety and Technology under the Ministry of Science and Technology, which monitors environmental radiation in Korea, said, “The closest area to the site of the nuclear test is Gangneung, about 320 km away. If radioactivity occurred, it is expected to take about 5 days for Gangneung to be contaminated, and we are currently operating an emergency response team to monitor radioactivity 24 hours a day.”
An official from the Korea Institute of Nuclear Safety and Technology explained, “Even if the underground nuclear test was perfect, it could not completely block radiation, resulting in about 0.1% of the total radiation. However, even assuming the worst case scenario, there will be no direct effect on the human body, and the radiation dose is expected to be significantly below the 0.1 millisievert (mSv) allowed per year for natural radiation under the Atomic Energy Act.”
However, some foreign media and experts are pointing out that the safety of North Korea's nuclear testing facilities cannot be trusted. Foreign countries conduct underground nuclear tests in areas without groundwater, such as deserts, but the area where North Korea's underground nuclear tests were conducted is different, and problems may arise.
China's Global Times warned that if North Korea goes ahead with nuclear testing, the entire groundwater on the Korean Peninsula could be contaminated with radioactivity. David Albright, director of the International Institute for Science and Security (ISIS), who served as a UN weapons inspector, said, “If there is a flaw in the design of the nuclear test site, not only can a significant amount of radioactivity leak out, but it can also blow up everything outside the test site.”
Satoshi Morimoto, a professor at Takushoku University and a Japanese security expert, also said, “There must be a 3,000㎦ desert to avoid groundwater contamination due to radioactive leaks.”
/ Chosun.com internetnews@chosun.com

ko-news-notices-309-8372c75064.title: Suspicions of environmental destruction and preferential treatment for aggregate collection at New Port
ko-news-notices-309-8372c75064.text:
Suspicions of environmental destruction and preferential treatment for aggregate collection at New Port
2022-03-02
Suspicions of environmental destruction and preferential treatment related to the extraction of aggregates such as sea sand required for the construction of Busan Port's new port were raised.
On the 16th, Uri Party lawmaker Cho Kyeong-tae pointed out in a government audit of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries of the National Assembly's Agriculture, Forestry, Oceans and Fisheries Committee, "The government granted exclusive permission to Busan New Port Co., Ltd. and Samsung C&T to extract aggregates for the first phase of the Busan New Port project, but the unit price for aggregate extraction and reclamation is only 8,467 won per ㎥ as of 2000."
Commissioner Cho said, “Considering the price of aggregates at the time, this was to sell aggregates at cost price, and through this, Samsung C&T was able to reduce costs by 120 billion won,” raising suspicions of preferential treatment related to aggregate extraction during the construction of the new port.
Rep. Cho said, "Among the numerous port construction projects, Samsung C&T is the only company that has received permission to extract aggregates. Please clarify why." He added, "The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries should conduct an audit on suspicions of preferential treatment related to aggregate extraction by Samsung C&T."
Rep. Cho said, "The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and Samsung C&T, while conducting a new port development project, collected more than 40 million ㎥ of sea sand from the EEZ (Exclusive Economic Zone) near Yokjido, Tongyeong-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, which is an act of self-destruction of the marine ecosystem." said.
He emphasized, "In most developed countries, the priority for reclaimed soil is the development of stone mountains in the landfill site, followed by dredged soil generated during the course of port dredging and recycled aggregates such as construction waste." He emphasized, "In the future, sea sand collection should be prohibited in port construction."
In addition, Rep. Cho said, "Despite the government supporting a huge amount of construction costs for port construction, construction companies are making huge profits by selling shares to foreign logistics companies at the end of the construction period. We must prepare legal measures to prevent this." Reporter Lee Dong-hyeon (Busan Ilbo)

ko-news-notices-308-8372c75064.title: The southern coast is ruined - the sea is dying due to marine pollution.
ko-news-notices-308-8372c75064.text:
The southern coast is ruined - the sea is dying due to marine pollution.
2022-03-02
Not only is the coastline around the southern coast damaged by indiscriminate reclamation of public waters, but the clean waters are dying without losing their original blue color due to various wastes and wastewater flowing into the sea. The bleaching phenomenon is progressing rapidly at the bottom of the sea along the southern coast. The 'ocean desertification phenomenon' is in progress, where white calcareous substances stick to the rock like moss, causing algae and corals to disappear and the food chain to collapse. Additionally, coastal waters are turning into underwater garbage dumps due to household waste being secretly thrown away.
#Tongyeong Coast, the heart of Hallyeohaesang National Park
Hallyeohaesang National Park, including the waters of Hansando in Tongyeong, Gyeongsangnam-do and parts of the southern coast, including Namhae and Geojedo Island. The heart of this place is Gangguan in Tongyeong. The sight of waves rolling in from the sea and crashing against the long breakwater boasts a spectacular view that is reminiscent of a painting.
However, the bottom of the Gangguan sea, which the reporting team explored with the special task force of the Tongyeong Marine Police Station on the 28th of last month, was suffering from various trash thrown away by people, contrary to appearance.
Scuba divers who dived to the coast at a depth of 6 to 7 meters appeared after about 5 minutes. When two divers pulled the line, a rusty oxygen tank came up. After a while, they picked up various trash, including crab pots. The coastal area was full of discarded nets, various fishing gear, and household waste. Household waste secretly thrown away from land is covering the sea.
Police officer Oh Gyeong-hoon (30), who completed the exploration, said, "This is high tide time, so visibility under the sea should be good, but I couldn't see even 30 centimeters in front," and added, "The sea bottom around the Gangguan coast is heavily polluted."
The situation on the coast of Misu-dong, Tongyeong, was not much different. Divers who went into the sea pulled up a rusty children's bicycle about 20 minutes later. Even under the sea here, you can't see 30cm in front of you.
#Fishing mouth of Dundeok-myeon, Geoje Island, coast of Samcheonpo Port
After passing through Tongyeong Gangguan, we arrived at the fishing mouth coast of Dundeok-myeon, Geoje-si, Gyeongsangnam-do. As we approached the coast where oyster farms were concentrated, suspended materials that appeared to have originated from the farms were floating here and there. The scene in the sea at a depth of about 10 meters was even more miserable. Oyster shells from the oyster farm were scattered here and there. While oyster farms were cultivating more oysters than the appropriate amount to increase profits, the oysters, unable to withstand their weight, fell, died en masse, and became entangled in white rocks.
Because of this, seaweed and microorganisms growing on rocks are disappearing, and as a result, the lowest level of the aquatic ecosystem food chain is collapsing, turning the sea into a dead sea where fisheries resources cannot live.
Superintendent Ko Young-hwan (36), who inspected the bottom of the fish farm, explained, "Due to the nature of algae, in the summer when the water temperature rises, oysters that fall due to overcrowding rot and become a cause of pollution," adding, "It was difficult to secure visibility under the fish farm."
A fish farm a few kilometers away from the oyster farm. This place, with a depth of about 15m, looked a little different from the sea we explored earlier. We explored for about 10 minutes, but unlike the fishing gear coast, visibility under the sea was good, perhaps due to the normal current flow, and no special contaminants were found.
Professor Kim Seong-jae (majoring in marine environmental engineering) at Gyeongsang National University's College of Marine Science said, "Pollution near coastal oyster farms and cage farms is serious, and in particular, various secretions are deposited, causing eutrophication and polluting the ocean." Professor Kim explained, “Indiscriminate construction of breakwaters that disrupt the flow of tidal currents also causes loss of natural purification ability,” adding, “Even when constructing breakwaters on the coast, construction methods that reduce waves and smooth the flow of water should be applied.”
#Addu Island Coast, Sacheon City
Addu Island was designated as a natural monument by the Cultural Heritage Administration on the 20th of last month. This island, located in Sinsu-dong, Sacheon-si, is entirely a source of dinosaur fossils and is where sedimentary structures from the Cretaceous period were discovered.
However, the coast of this island was also littered with various types of trash. Household waste, including beverage bottles and cans and discarded fishing gear, was strewn everywhere. On the 25th of last month, about 100 volunteers from the Sacheon Environmental Movement Federation, the city, and the Samcheonpo Fisheries Cooperative worked tirelessly to collect trash, but there was no end in sight.
The Korea Federation for Environmental Movement analyzes that the largest amount of trash discarded here comes from beach tourist attractions, accounting for 60% of the total. Additionally, it is estimated that approximately 33% of waste comes from fishing and maritime transportation. Garbage carelessly thrown away by vacationers during the summer is said to be the main culprit of marine pollution. In the sea near Samcheonpo Port, abandoned motorcycles and bicycles were even found. Garbage in the sea is difficult to collect, and the exact situation is not even known.
Jin Han, team leader of the Sacheon Environmental Movement Federation, said, "We carry out purification activities near Samcheonpo Port every year, but so much household waste is thrown away that it is not enough to collect it."
# Tongyeong Coast Guard Lieutenant Koo Young-hwan
- "A nationwide movement to save the ocean"
“The sea off the southern coast is losing its blue color to the point where you can’t see even an inch ahead when you go under the sea.”
Lieutenant Koo Young-hwan (53, photo), commander of the special task force at the Tongyeong Coast Guard, which has jurisdiction over the waters of Gyeongnam, is a veteran with more than 30 years of diver experience since enlisting in the Navy Marine Rescue Unit (SSU).
Inspector Koo expressed regret, saying, “Just 30 years ago, the southern coast had a blue ink color like the beaches of Hawaii, but as time goes by, the color of the sea is becoming more turbid and pollution is getting worse.” He gave a clear example, saying, “The southern coast is rotting to the point that when ROVs (unmanned underwater vehicles) are deployed to investigate sunken ships, there is so much floating material under the sea that it is impossible to take proper pictures.” Inspector Koo pointed out that the main cause of marine pollution is lack of awareness of the sea, including the act of recklessly dumping various harmful substances into the sea. He advised, “The level of pollution in the coastal waters adjacent to the land is more serious than expected, but the more distant seas are still clean waters,” and added, “If sea pollution continues to be neglected, the next generation will no longer be able to see the blue sea.”
“It is my belief that ‘the sea is a national asset.’ We must return the benefits we have received so far to the sea before it loses its ability to purify itself.” Inspector Koo emphasized, “There are limits to how organizations can save the ocean,” and added, “We need to launch a large-scale ‘nation-wide movement’ at the national level.”
# Marine debris increases by 25,000 tons per year
- Side effects such as annual fishing loss of KRW 320 billion
It was found that the amount of various wastes, including waste nets and ropes, abandoned in the sea exceeds 400,000 tons, and 25,000 tons of new waste is generated every year.
According to the government audit data recently submitted by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries to Grand National Party lawmaker Kim Myeong-ju (Tongyeong and Goseong, South Gyeongsang Province), 400,470 tons of marine waste, including 167,978 tons in the West Sea, 86,412 tons in the South Sea, and 86,080 tons in the East Sea, is dumped at the bottom of Korea's coast. In addition, 115,000 tons of silted waste that interferes with fisheries resources and the safe operation of navigation vessels is left unattended, and with 25,000 tons of trash generated every year, the amount of trash deposited on the coast of Korea is continuously increasing.
These marine wastes are mainly floating waste, discarded fishing nets, discarded ropes, etc., and have been found to not only cause safety accidents on ships, but also cause problems such as damage to marine life spawning grounds and habitats and damage to coastal landscapes due to sedimentary waste. In addition, it was found that the loss of fishing production due to the decrease in catch amounted to 320 billion won per year.
Rep. Kim said, “Not only is the marine ecosystem damaged by the increase in marine waste, but marine pollution is worsening, causing enormous damage to local fishermen,” and added, “There is an urgent need to increase the budget to smoothly carry out marine waste collection and disposal projects.”

ko-news-notices-307-8372c75064.title: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, “Opposes reclamation of Geumgang Janghang mudflat”
ko-news-notices-307-8372c75064.text:
Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, “Opposes reclamation of Geumgang Janghang mudflat”
2022-03-02
Regarding the Janghang National Industrial Complex development project at the Geumgang Estuary, which is causing controversy over mudflat damage like Saemangeum, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries expressed its opinion that it is opposed to mudflat reclamation.
Lee Eun, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, said at a regular briefing on the 27th, “It is the opinion of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries that the Janghang mudflats should not be reclaimed.” Vice Minister Lee said, “As a result of the field investigation, it has been revealed that the Janghang mudflats have high conservation value as a migratory bird habitat,” and added, “Large-scale reclamation projects should no longer be carried out on the west coast, which is one of the five largest mudflats in the world.”
Regarding the fact that compensation for fishing rights, land expropriation, and road construction have already been made to build an industrial complex, he said, “National resource management should not be dragged down by existing investments,” and added, “We must seek ways to revitalize the economy of the area without reclamation of mud flats.”
Vice Minister Lee said, “The final decision (on the reclamation of the Janghang mudflats) will soon be made through consultation with relevant ministries.”
The Janghang National Industrial Complex project was decided in 1989 to create an industrial complex by filling 3.74 million pyeong of mud flats (1.5 times the area of ​​Yeouido and 1/33 the size of Saemangeum reclaimed land) in the western part of Maseo-myeon and Janghang-eup in Seocheon-gun, Chungcheongnam-do, which is the northern end of the Geum River Estuary.
South Chungcheong Province and Seocheon-gun are insisting that the construction of an industrial complex, which has been in the works for 17 years, should be completed as soon as possible to revitalize the local economy, while fishermen and environmental groups are opposing reclamation for the sake of fishermen's right to survive and the preservation of mudflats.
This project was continuously postponed due to lack of demand for industrial complex land, but began to be promoted in earnest in 2004 when the environmental impact assessment began. Currently, the third environmental impact assessment consultation is in progress. Hongseop Cho, environmental reporter ecothink@hani.co.kr

ko-news-notices-306-8372c75064.title: The introduction of fishing vessel VMS is causing excitement in the fishing industry.
ko-news-notices-306-8372c75064.text:
The introduction of fishing vessel VMS is causing excitement in the fishing industry.
2022-03-02
The fishing industry is in an uproar, with seafarers' unions joining in opposition to the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries' enactment of a notice on the mandatory installation of VMS (automatic vessel positioning system), which raised concerns about infringement of intellectual property rights on fishing grounds that captains and fishing grounds have held for decades (reported on page 16 of our July 19 issue).
On the 14th, a public hearing on VMS installation held by the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries at the Busan Community Fish Market was initially canceled due to opposition from the industry and the National Democratic Seafarers' Union, leading to extreme confrontation.
△Fisheries Industry Claims = On the 20th, the National Democratic Seafarers' Union published material refuting the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries' basis for enacting the VMS-related notice in detail and raised its voice, saying, "For whom is this policy?"
The union argued, "The Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries claims that the installation of VMS is to prevent casualties from marine accidents, but the majority of accidents like this are caused by safety accidents rather than failure to locate the ship, so this cannot be the basis for installation."
Related industries are also opposing the issue of VMS installation costs as well as infringement of intellectual property rights that expose information such as fishing grounds locations.
An official in the large steamboat trawl industry said, "It is expected that the installation cost for the 30,000 vessels nationwide will cost more than 100 billion won. Even if 50% is supported by the national treasury, it will be a huge burden on fishermen who are at a crossroads of life and death due to high oil prices and declining catches, and it will be difficult to avoid criticism that taxpayers' money is being used for a place where the expected results are unclear."
△ Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries position = The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries plans to install VMS on fishing boats for rapid rescue, given the domestic conditions in which about 120 of the 170 casualties from marine accidents occur annually due to fishing boat accidents.
Regarding infringement of intellectual property rights, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries explained that the concerns of the fishing industry are unfounded as data received from VMS will be thoroughly blocked from exposure except for rescue purposes and will not be received in other countries. Regarding the installation cost, it was revealed that the fishing industry is misunderstood based on the expensive VMS installed on large ships such as commercial ships.
Jeong Seon-moon, secretary of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, said, “The VMS for fishing boats currently under development costs 500,000 to 700,000 won each, and can be installed on all 30,000 ships for about 18 billion won.” He added, “The government is considering a plan to cover most of the cost.”
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries believed that the opposition from the fishing industry was due to chronic external factors such as conflicts over fishing areas by industry, and decided to newly adjust details such as the implementation period and target vessels through the Policy Deliberation Committee and the Central Regulatory Review Committee.
Reporter Lee Sang-yoon (Busan Ilbo)

ko-news-notices-305-8372c75064.title: First introduction of marine accident electronic video review system
ko-news-notices-305-8372c75064.text:
First introduction of marine accident electronic video review system
2022-03-02
An electronic video referee system developed with domestic technology will be introduced into the marine accident referee system for the first time in the world.
Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Central Maritime Safety Tribunal decided on the 20th to introduce an electronic video adjudication system using cutting-edge information and communication technology into the marine accident adjudication system and begin operating it in earnest from next month in order to scientifically determine the cause of marine accidents.
Choi Jang-hyun, director of the Central Sea Trial and Appeal Board, said, "This system has never been introduced in similar domestic administrative trial institutions such as civil courts or patent trials, or in foreign marine accident investigation and adjudication institutions," and added, "With the introduction of this system, the cause of marine accidents can be revealed scientifically and objectively, increasing the reliability of trials domestically and internationally."
Accordingly, the marine accident adjudication system, which was conducted offline using paper documents and statements, was transformed into an advanced scientific adjudication system incorporating cutting-edge information and communication technology.
