In addition, the hearing, which was previously conducted as a one-way Q&A between the investigator who investigated the marine accident and requested a judgment, the judge who must reveal the cause of the accident, and the person involved in the marine accident who is being judged, can now freely conduct a judgment through two-way statements between the investigator/judge and the person involved in the marine accident based on digital video.
This system can record and preserve the trial process, ensuring transparency in the trial, and the necessary trial data can be checked at all times, shortening the trial period through speedy proceedings, thereby improving the convenience of complainants.
The electronic imaging system consists of software such as a 3D ship collision simulator and an interactive electronic video referee assistance program, and cutting-edge hardware equipment such as a ship operation situation map, radar images, and an actual imager.
The Central Sea Trial Center plans to install this system in four regional sea trial centers, including Busan, Incheon, Mokpo, and Donghae, within the year and promote sharing of various referee data and remote video referees through organic network connection between the center and each region starting next year. Reporter Lee Dong-hyeon (Busan Ilbo)

ko-news-notices-304-8372c75064.title: A company preparing to develop deep ocean water prepares for full-scale production
ko-news-notices-304-8372c75064.text:
A company preparing to develop deep ocean water prepares for full-scale production
2022-03-02
As the Deep Ocean Water Development and Management Act is expected to be submitted to the National Assembly's Agriculture, Forestry, Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Committee on the 20th, companies that have been preparing for deep ocean water development projects are expected to begin full-scale business implementation starting next year.
According to the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the industry on the 18th, as it is certain that the Deep Ocean Water Development and Management Act submitted to the National Assembly by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries in February will be submitted to the Standing Committee on the 20th, companies that have prepared various products such as bottled water, salt, tofu, soy sauce, beer, and cosmetics are rushing to prepare for full-scale production next year.
The industry estimates that the deep ocean water market size will exceed 200 billion won per year. Companies and items for which prototype development has been completed include △ Kooksoondang - Baekseju △ Aekyung Industrial - Cosmetics △ Sempio Foods - Soy Sauce △ Dongwon F&B - Sea Green Tea Beverage △ Hyundai Pharm Industry - Ion Beverage △ Gangneung Chodang Tofu - Tofu △ Doosan - Cheongju △ Daehakchon (Kyungpook National University of Science) - Fermented Beverage.
The government plans to introduce a marine sediment water development license system and a user fee collection system. Reporter Lee Dong-hyeon (Busan Ilbo)

ko-news-notices-303-8372c75064.title: Diversification of Oceanographic Observation Activities
ko-news-notices-303-8372c75064.text:
Diversification of Oceanographic Observation Activities
2022-03-02
In the future, domestic coastal passenger ships will also be used to observe various changes in the marine environment, such as the occurrence of red tide or cold water zones.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced on the 18th that it had recently instructed each regional office across the country to cooperate with the National Institute of Fisheries Science to use coastal passenger ships to identify changes in the marine environment. Currently, ocean observations are only conducted through the National Aquarium's test research vessel.
The National Aquarium decided to install equipment on the Hyundai Seolbong, which will sail between Busan and Jeju, until next month to observe changes in the Tsushima Warm Current and the occurrence of a water temperature front in the Korea Strait.
In addition, changes in passenger ship operating sea areas will be observed on the Sunflower, Mukho-Ulleungdo Hankyoreh, and Incheon-Baengnyeongdo Mandarin on the Pohang-Ulleungdo route.
To this end, the National Aquarium has already installed equipment on the Hanil Car Ferry 2, which travels between Wando, Jeollanam-do and Jeju, last month to test and observe sea conditions, including the occurrence and spread of red tide and the movement of jellyfish.
The biggest reason for using coastal passenger ships for marine observation is that since they regularly operate designated routes, observational data on the relevant sea area can be continuously accumulated, and it is easy to identify and respond to changes in the sea at any time.
In addition, the surge in oil prices is causing disruption in the operation of test research ships.
The National Aquarium expects that marine observation data from coastal ferries will be useful in analyzing unusual sea conditions such as cold water zones, low-salinity waters, and typhoon occurrences.
An official from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries explained, "It can also be used as short-term forecast data to protect coastal fishing grounds and fish farms. Furthermore, if we establish observation techniques in cooperation with private companies, we can expand the target area to international routes and diversify the observation contents."
Reporter Kyung-sik Lee (International Newspaper)

ko-news-notices-302-8372c75064.title: Environment Minister Lee opposes further tidal flat reclamation
ko-news-notices-302-8372c75064.text:
Environment Minister Lee opposes further tidal flat reclamation
2022-03-02
(Seoul = Yonhap News) Reporter Kim Seong-yong = Minister of Environment Lee Chi-beom said, “The development-oriented mudflat (public waters) management policy originated from a legal problem that allowed the development department to establish plans autonomously, without the control of even the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, the responsible ministry,” and added, “There should no longer be indiscriminate tidal flat reclamation.”
Minister Lee revealed this in an interview with Yonhap News on the 20th and emphasized, "Currently, all related organizations, including the Sustainable Development Commission, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, and the Ministry of Environment, are participating in preparing fundamental measures to prevent the indiscriminate development of tidal flats." He added, "It is time to establish broad policy principles to prevent tidal flat reclamation."
Minister Lee's comments are interpreted as expressing his will to put the brakes on the Janghang wetland development issue, which has recently been causing controversy surrounding development, and to manage the Saemangeum project through as strict an environmental impact assessment as possible. Attention is focused on whether and how the government's mudflat reclamation policy will change in the future.
Regarding the issue of changing the use of the Saemangeum project, Minister Lee emphasized his position on phased use designation, saying, "I think it would be desirable to first designate a use for only some areas rather than determine a use for the entire Saemangeum area, and then leave the rest as is and use it later as needed."
In the case of the Saemangeum project, if the land use plan changes by more than 15% of the total site, it is subject to change consultation. If a tourist complex (300,000㎡) or an industrial complex (150,000㎡) is created instead of farmland, a separate environmental impact assessment consultation process will be conducted for each project. The joint land use service of five organizations, including the Korea Research Institute for Human Settlements and the Environmental Policy Evaluation Institute, is scheduled to be completed in December.
Minister Lee announced that the unification of water management, which has caused controversy over duplication and excessive investment, is being discussed among ministries on the issue of establishing a water management committee and the Basic Act on Water Management, and that the Ministry of Construction and Transportation and the Ministry of Environment are considering a method of handling it by preparing a bill through joint legislation and unifying the relevant National Assembly standing committees into the Environment and Labor Committee.
Minister Lee expressed his will to discuss discussions with the Ministry of Construction and Transportation on integrating ministries or policies, saying, "I understand that a plan to integrate national land development and environmental conservation policy functions will be prepared by the end of this year through the Government Innovation and Local Decentralization Committee. I will actively reflect the position of the Ministry of Environment in the process of discussing the integration plan, and will also actively contact and discuss with the Ministry of Construction and Transportation when necessary."
Minister Lee also said, "We are pushing for the establishment of the Waterside Ecological Zone Management Corporation under the Ministry of Environment in order to resolve operational problems and systematically manage the four major river waterfront areas. Although there are differences of opinion with some local governments, the establishment of the Corporation is urgently needed for comprehensive management, including ecological surveys for each watershed and establishment of conservation and restoration plans."
He expressed his position, saying, "It is undesirable to argue that a dam should be built without an accurate investigation into the cause of flood damage. Dam construction should be promoted with social consensus as a last resort, and even in this case, the construction of large dams should be actively avoided."

ko-news-notices-301-8372c75064.title: North Port Redevelopment Sea Reclamation of 190,000 pyeong
ko-news-notices-301-8372c75064.text:
North Port Redevelopment Sea Reclamation of 190,000 pyeong
2022-03-02
It has been revealed that 190,000 pyeong of sea is scheduled to be reclaimed for the redevelopment of Busan Port's North Port. In addition, a financial analysis showed that 1.6 trillion won will be invested in infrastructure construction, including land development and the construction of an international passenger terminal, and that more than 300 billion won in government funding will be needed to finance this project.
The Busan Port Authority (BPA) announced on the 17th that it plans to secure the land needed for redevelopment by reclaiming 190,000 pyeong of the sea in addition to the existing 150,000 pyeong of land for piers 1 to 4 and central pier in the North Port.
This is a 90,000 pyeong reduction in the reclaimed area from the originally set 280,000 pyeong. Kwon So-hyeon, head of BPA's North Port Redevelopment Team, explained, "The reclaimed area was reduced as we prepared a basic redevelopment plan that involved creating a waterway about 4km long and 40m wide in front of the port."
It was estimated that it would cost 1.6 trillion won to create infrastructure, including 900 billion won for site development, 300 billion won for the construction of the international passenger terminal, and 400 billion won for land purchase. However, it was analyzed that there was a shortfall of about 300 billion won, so BPA requested government support. This is a measure in response to the 'Act on the Sustainable Use of Ports and Surrounding Spaces', which will be processed in the regular National Assembly next month, specifying that project costs can be subsidized or financed from the government budget.
Team leader Kwon said, "We plan to raise the project cost by selling or distributing the site after creating the site, but when we drew up the financial plan, we calculated that 300 billion won would be short. Considering the precedent of large-scale projects such as the construction of a new port, where 30% of the project cost is usually covered by government funds, government support is an essential requirement, and this can be used as a stepping stone to attract private investment."

ko-news-notices-300-8372c75064.title: Haeundae's white sand beach has decreased by 30% in 60 years...
ko-news-notices-300-8372c75064.text:
Haeundae's white sand beach has decreased by 30% in 60 years...
2022-03-02
The sandy beach of Haeundae in Busan, the largest beach in Korea, has shrunk by more than a third over the past 60 years, and this is believed to be mainly due to the development of surrounding areas, including tourist hotels. This means that the coastal environment can be severely damaged not only by direct development of the coast, such as the construction of breakwaters and ports, but also by development of surrounding areas. Researcher Yang Ji-yeon of the Busan Development Institute and Professor Choi Cheol-woong of the Department of Satellite Information Science at Pukyong National University recently published a paper in the Journal of the Korean Society of Geographic Information titled ‘Analysis of Coastal Topography and Land Cover Changes at Haeundae Beach’ and revealed that the sandy beach of Haeundae has decreased by more than one-third over the past 60 years.
Researchers analyzed changes in the area of ​​Haeundae's sandy beach and land use in the surrounding area of ​​2.71 million m2 between 1947 and 2005 using satellite images. As a result, in 2005, the forest area near Haeundae decreased by 50% compared to 1947, while the built-up area and bare land increased by 66% and 55%, respectively. The area of ​​sandy beaches decreased by 35% from 88,658 m2 in 1947 to 578.93 million m2 in 2005.
Regarding the reason for the shrinking of the sandy beach, the researchers said, “This is because a large amount of soil in the forest area was washed away as the land was dug up for development in the area around Haeundae, while the inflow of sand was blocked by covering the Chuncheon Stream around Haeundae.” In fact, in 1947, the amount of soil lost annually was only 81 tons, but in 1970, when full-scale development began, the number increased five-fold to 410 tons. In the academic world, it has been assumed that the main causes of coastal changes are natural factors such as erosion and direct coastal development such as breakwaters and ports, rather than development of surrounding areas.
Professor Choi said, “This is the first time to prove that the coastline can change due to development of the surrounding area,” and added, “Artificial development has a greater impact on shrinking the coastline than natural change.” He warned against reckless development around the coast, saying, “This means that if beach development is severe, it could lead to the disappearance of the sandy beach.”
Reporters Yoo Ji-hye and Seo Jae-hee (s123@seoul.co.kr)

ko-news-notices-299-8372c75064.title: Undersea topography survey conducted near Osan Port in Uljin
ko-news-notices-299-8372c75064.text:
Undersea topography survey conducted near Osan Port in Uljin
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency's East Sea Oceanographic Survey Office (Director Kim Jeong-gi) announced that it will conduct a detailed survey of the seafloor topography of the sea area near Osan Port in Uljin by August 11.
This survey will be conducted using cutting-edge survey equipment such as a satellite positioning system (DGPS) and a precision echo sounder (MK-Ⅱ), as the reef near Osan Port can act as a risk factor for safe navigation of ships.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “We will take measures such as navigation notices after data processing for the reefs and low water depths revealed in this survey, which will contribute to safe navigation and marine leisure activities for sailing vessels as well as to increasing the income of local fishermen.”
In the future, the East Sea Marine Research Office will conduct detailed surveys of the seafloor topography of major ports and routes on the East Coast, national fishing ports, etc., provide data necessary for securing maritime traffic safety and port management and operation, and will do its best to produce marine information desired by consumers.

ko-news-notices-298-8372c75064.title: 43 tons of discarded shellfish after completion of Saemangeum seawall
ko-news-notices-298-8372c75064.text:
43 tons of discarded shellfish after completion of Saemangeum seawall
2022-03-02
After the 33km Saemangeum seawall was completed, seawater circulation was restricted and the number of shellfish deaths exceeded 40 tons.
According to the Saemangeum Project Division of the Korea Rural Community Corporation on the 2nd, after the seawall construction was completed in late April, seawater distribution was restricted to two drainage locks, and shellfish mortality rapidly progressed, centering on the mudflats of Geojeon Port, Jinbong-myeon, Gimje-si, and 43 tons were collected.
From May to July, the Saemangeum Project Group mobilized approximately 1,800 people to collect dead shellfish and dispose of them at a waste disposal site, with some of them being stored in the open air.
The reason why such a large number of clams died is because the seawall blocked the circulation of seawater, creating an extensive mud flat with almost no seawater inside the seawall.
For this reason, a fisherman claimed, “Considering that about 40 tons of shellfish died in the Geojeon Port area, hundreds of tons of shellfish will disappear if we consider the entire area of ​​Saemangeum,” and added, “The bad smell of waste shellfish is also a problem.”
The Saemangeum Project Group said, “It is a natural phenomenon that occurs when the inflow and outflow of seawater is restricted,” and added, “As fishing has stopped inside the seawall, we will collect all of it to prevent problems such as environmental pollution.”
Reporter Hong In-cheol ichong@yna.co.kr (Gimje = Yonhap News)

ko-news-notices-297-8372c75064.title: Pilot installation of red tide barrier at fish farm
ko-news-notices-297-8372c75064.text:
Pilot installation of red tide barrier at fish farm
2022-03-02
Local governments such as Busan, Ulsan, and Gyeongnam are busy preparing red tide prevention measures. Recently, a series of red tide damage prevention meeting meetings have been held and various measures, such as distributing red tide organism testing supplies and installing equatorial barriers, are being proposed.
The Busan Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries announced on the 30th that it has decided to supply Mueller gauze for red tide organism testing to 20 fish farms. The purpose is to install a Muller gauze in aquaculture farms that supply seawater to immediately detect the presence of red tide organisms.
Gyeongnam Province decided to pilot the installation of red tide bioblocks and pre-release of fish for marine cage aquaculture, which is most exposed to red tide. The plan is to spend 250 million won to surround five cage fish farms in Tongyeong with red tide bioblocks, connect oxygen supply devices inside them, and release 60,000 rockfish. Jeong Un-hyeon, in charge of aquaculture at Gyeongnam Province's Fisheries Production Department, said, "Except for 2004, Gyeongnam Province has continued to suffer damage from red tide, so we are currently looking for alternatives other than red clay spraying. If we achieve good results this year, we will be able to expand this method and dramatically reduce damage to fish farms."
Ulsan City also decided to station a high-speed small surveillance ship and staff in the waters around Seosaeng-myeon, Ulju-gun, Ulsan-si, where the risk of exposure to red tide is high when a red tide warning is issued. In addition, as soon as red tide appears in an area, a local situation room will be established and a 24-hour surveillance system will be established.
Although Busan has not suffered red tide damage since 2002, it is no exception in red tide prevention activities. Hong Seok-tae, manager of the Busan City Fisheries Promotion Department, said, "Gijang-gun decided to purchase red tide remedies such as powdered red clay with its own budget of 20 million won in addition to 60 million won in national budget, and the Coast Guard also promised helicopter surveillance support, so we will do our best to prevent damage for the fifth year."
International Newspaper (Reporter Kim Dong-su)

ko-news-notices-296-8372c75064.title: Tensions grow between fishermen and the fisheries ministry over the South Sea aggregate extraction complex
ko-news-notices-296-8372c75064.text:
Tensions grow between fishermen and the fisheries ministry over the South Sea aggregate extraction complex
2022-03-02
The controversy is growing as fishermen and environmental groups are escalating their struggle over the government's designation of a large-scale aggregate extraction complex within the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of the southern coast, saying they are concerned about damage such as destruction of the marine ecosystem and depletion of fish resources.
Fishermen's groups and fishermen in the Tongyeong region are strongly demanding the withdrawal of the complex designation policy, saying, "If an aggregate extraction complex is built near Yokjido, the largest fish spawning ground on the southern coast, the marine ecosystem will be destroyed and the livelihood of fishermen will be completely taken away."
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and representatives of fisheries cooperatives and fishermen held a meeting in downtown Tongyeong on the 27th to discuss the promotion of the aggregate extraction complex, but only confirmed the positions of both sides and failed to reach an agreement.
Cho Yong-jae, chairman of the committee to oppose sand mining in the Bad Sea, said, "Through two meetings, we only confirmed that the claims of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (government) and the fishermen are in conflict, so there is no room for further negotiations. We plan to hold a plenary meeting of the opposition committee soon to collect the opinions of the fishermen and seek all possible ways to protect their right to survival."
The opposition promotion committee plans to increase the level of struggle in the future by visiting the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries to protest and holding large-scale maritime demonstrations mobilizing ships.
Experts are continuously raising concerns about the government's unilateral plan to designate an aggregate extraction complex.
Professor Bae Ki-seong (Department of Marine and Civil Engineering) at Gyeongsang National University said, "If sand deposited on the seabed is collected, it is impossible to restore it to its original state due to the nature of the sea, which is different from land. In particular, the changed seafloor environment and floating sand that occurs during the sand extraction process are very likely to drive migratory fish species, including anchovies, to other places."
Meanwhile, with regard to the plan to designate an aggregate extraction complex, following the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries' opinion of 're-negotiation after supplementation' and the Ministry of Environment's opinion of 'reconsideration necessary', the Ministry of National Defense announced on the 28th that it 'cannot designate the complex', attracting attention.
Seong-Hoon Lee and Byeong-Gyun Kang (lee777@busanilbo.com)

ko-news-notices-295-8372c75064.title: Damage to marine products due to lack of oxygen in Masan and Jinhae Bay
ko-news-notices-295-8372c75064.text:
Damage to marine products due to lack of oxygen in Masan and Jinhae Bay
2022-03-02
Hypoxic water masses, which result in a lack of oxygen in the water, have occurred in the waters of Masan Bay and Jinhae Bay in Gyeongsangnam-do, raising concerns about damage to fishery products of fishermen.
The Marine Environment Headquarters of the National Institute of Fisheries Science announced on the 28th that as a result of investigating the area on the 27th using Exploration 17, a hypoxic water mass with a dissolved oxygen concentration of less than 3 mg/L was found. Additionally, this phenomenon is expected to expand further once the monsoon rains stop and solar radiation increases, causing greater damage to fish and shellfish, so fishermen need to be careful.
The hypoxic water mass is created from the bottom of the sea and gradually rises to the surface, and has been confirmed to have occurred at a depth of 10m. If solar radiation increases, it is likely to rise to a water depth of 5 to 6 m, which is the low temperature layer, causing damage to cage farms and submerged fish farms (aquaculture methods in which aquaculture plants are suspended in water) such as oysters and snail fish.
Researcher Jin Hyeon-guk of the Aquarium's Environmental Management Team said, "If a hypoxic water mass phenomenon occurs, in a submerged fish farm, the fish should be folded in half in a U-shape and placed close to the surface of the water."
International Newspaper (Reporter Kim Dong-su)

ko-news-notices-294-8372c75064.title: Withdraw the Janghang tidal flat reclamation plan.
ko-news-notices-294-8372c75064.text:
Withdraw the Janghang tidal flat reclamation plan.
2022-03-02
(Seoul = Yonhap News) Reporter Kim Byeong-gyu = The Korean Federation for Environmental Movement and the Seocheon Janghang Tidal Flat Restoration Coalition held a press conference in front of the government building in Sejong-ro, Seoul on the 27th and urged, “Withdraw the plan to reclaim the Janghang Tidal Flat to create the Janghang National Industrial Complex.”
These groups claimed, "The Janghang tidal flat in Seocheon, South Chungcheong Province, is a place where fishermen earn more than 300 billion won in income every year and has important meaning in preserving the ecosystem. However, the government is pushing ahead with the plan to create the Janghang National Industrial Complex and is trying to reclaim it," and added, "The government must stop threatening the livelihoods of fishermen and the ecosystem by stopping the tidal flat reclamation plan."
bkkim@yna.co.kr

ko-news-notices-293-8372c75064.title: ‘Development turbidity’ kills tidal flats at the Han River estuary
ko-news-notices-293-8372c75064.text:
‘Development turbidity’ kills tidal flats at the Han River estuary
2022-03-02
Among the four major rivers in Korea, the Han River estuary, the only one remaining, is under threat because it crosses the Military Demarcation Line. The estuary ecosystem is in danger of being damaged due to successive development pressures such as tidal power plant and new city construction plans, bridge and road construction, and aggregate extraction. The problem is that development is accelerating without a responsible ministry to coordinate the development and preservation of the Han River Estuary.
“It is said that the tidal flat area at the southern end of Ganghwa is being discussed as a site for a tidal power plant. It is a place where hundreds of thousands of migratory birds that travel back and forth between Southeast Asia, Australia, and Siberia each year eat and rest, but I am worried that it will become an ecological disaster.”
Dr. Lee Ki-seop (Korea Institute of Environment and Ecology) said while looking around the Seondori mud flat south of Ganghwa, the coastal estuary of the Han River. At the Gaksi Rock on the mudflat reflected through a telephoto lens, an adult spoonbill (Natural Monument No. 205) chick was nodding its head and begging its mother for food. The mud flats were busy early this month with ring-tailed curlews scurrying through the mud flats in search of kudzu crabs, flocks of seagulls searching for midges in the red turkey colonies, and well-fed cormorants.
Dr. Lee said, “The Gimpo tidal flat has already become a landfill, and the Songdo tidal flat and Sihwa tidal flat have also been reclaimed.” He asked, “Shouldn’t this, the only remaining tidal flat in the Han River estuary, be protected?”
The energy shortage is why the tidal power plant plan, which had been dormant several years ago due to opposition to the idea of ​​destroying the ecosystem, is emerging again this year. An official from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, the responsible ministry, admitted that its Marine Research Institute is investigating the feasibility of the project this year.
He explained, “The development of alternative energy is necessary to resolve the rise in oil prices and the pressure from the international community to mandate a reduction in greenhouse gases in accordance with the Kyoto Protocol starting in 2013.” The west coast area, where the tidal range reaches 9m, is a suitable location. It is known that the area targeted for construction of the power plant connects Ganghwa Island, Jangbong Island, Yongyu Island, and Yeongjong Island. In fact, both sides of the tidal flat at the southern end of Ganghwa are blocked.
When water flow changes, changes in tidal flat topography are inevitable. Professor Gyeongnam Han (Inha University Department of Oceanography) called for a detailed investigation, saying, “The seawater flow on the east side of the Yeongjongdo landfill site has slowed, leading to increased tidal flat sedimentation, while on the west side, the flow has sped up and the mudflats have been cut away, showing the impact of development.”
The development of inland estuarine wetlands is also accelerating. Large-scale residential land development is being carried out one after another in places such as Gimpo and Paju.
In addition to the previously approved Ilsan Bridge, two additional bridges crossing the wetland protection area are scheduled to be built. Extraction of aggregates, an ‘estuary bonanza’, is also being promoted as part of inter-Korean economic cooperation. It is pointed out that fishery resources in the West Sea will decrease. The species most affected by such environmental changes are expected to be the summer spoonbill, which is considered the ‘flagship species’ of the Han River estuary ecosystem, as well as the spring and fall snipe and winter white-naped crane (Natural Monument No. 203). In an environment where they cannot survive, it becomes difficult for other migratory birds, such as herons, egrets, geese, and whooper geese, to survive.
Dr. Changhee Lee of the Environmental Policy Evaluation Institute said, “Estuarine development is progressing and planned at a rapid pace, but environmental impact assessments are only conducted for individual projects,” adding, “There is no integrated monitoring of the ‘cumulative impact’ of development.”
It is pointed out that a ‘master plan’ that unifies the Han River Estuary policies of the Ministry of Construction and Transportation, Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Ministry of Environment, and Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry is needed before inter-Korean economic cooperation is activated at the latest.
〈Reporter Choi Min-young min@kyunghyang.com〉

ko-news-notices-292-8372c75064.title: Concerns about low salinity in Jeju sea
ko-news-notices-292-8372c75064.text:
Concerns about low salinity in Jeju sea
2022-03-02
Diluted water flowing in from the Yangtze River in China will not only have a significant impact on the marine environment and fish conditions in the southwest of Jeju Island, but is also expected to move to the coastal waters of Jeju Island, so countermeasures are urgently needed.
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency announced on the 25th the results of an oceanographic survey conducted jointly with the Korea Ocean Research Institute and the National Institute of Fisheries Science in the East China Sea, the waters west of Jeju and near the Ieodo Science Base, to reveal the water circulation phenomenon in the Yellow Sea since the 18th.
As a result of the investigation, the influence of diluted water from the Yangtze River in the East China Sea in the summer, which is known to have a significant impact on Korea's marine environment and fish conditions, was clearly visible all the way to the seafloor southwest of Jeju Island, and the influence of cold water from the bottom of the Yellow Sea was visible even to the seafloor northwest of Jeju Island.
In addition, it is expected that diluted water from the Yangtze River will be moved to the coastal waters of Jeju Island in the future.
In particular, the completion of the world's largest Shansha Dam, which connects the gorge of the middle and upper reaches of the Yangtze River, resulted in the generation of a large amount of fresh water, which was found to have a significant impact on Korea's marine ecosystem, including the waters around Jeju Island in the summer.
These results are expected to have a significant impact on the marine ecosystem in light of previous research showing that large amounts of harmful red tide occur when runoff from the Yangtze River in China approaches Jeju and the southern coast.
The East China Sea fishing ground is a major fishing ground for cutlassfish and tilefish fishing boats in the province, and changes in the marine ecosystem are directly related to the catch of fishing boats in the province, raising concerns about the death of fish and shellfish due to low salinity.
In 2002, low-salinity water with a salinity concentration of 25.2 to 26.7 per mill was confirmed in ports and communal fishing ports in the northwestern part of Jeju, causing some damage to fishermen's conch and abalone.
Prior to this, in August 1996, 184 tons of abalone, conches, and sea urchins in the village community fishing ground died due to low-salinity water of 19 to 25 per mill, causing damage of 5.9 billion won.
When the salt concentration of seawater falls below 28 permil, physiological disorders occur in some aquatic organisms, and when it falls below 25 permil, fish and shellfish die.
The Ocean Research Institute will comprehensively analyze data such as frankincense, current speed, water temperature, salinity, and plankton surveyed in the East China Sea by the end of this year. The plan is to understand the Yellow Sea's water circulation structure and the impact of the Shansha Dam, built on the Yangtze River in China, on the southwestern waters of Jeju.
Jeju Ilbo (Reporter Hyeon Bong-cheol)

ko-news-notices-291-8372c75064.title: Fishermen outside Saemangeum demand compensation
ko-news-notices-291-8372c75064.text:
Fishermen outside Saemangeum demand compensation
2022-03-02
(Jeonju = Yonhap News) Reporter Lim Cheong = Fishermen outside the Saemangeum Seawall are demanding compensation for various damages from Jeonbuk Province and the government.
About 10 residents of islands outside Saemangeum, including Yami Island, Shinsi Island, and Seonyudo, held a press conference at the provincial office on the 26th and urged, "The government should compensate all island residents in the Gunsan area who lost their port function due to the construction of the seawall."
They claimed, "So far, the fishermen living outside Saemangeum have endured the pain caused by the construction of the Saemangeum seawall, which was carried out as a national project. However, even with the seawall completed, the government and Jeonbuk Province are ignoring the damage suffered by residents living outside Saemangeum."
The fishermen also said, “The government should convert the limited licenses of fishermen outside Saemangeum to general licenses and compensate fishing boats for closure,” and added, “If our demands are not met, the 4,000 residents outside Saemangeum will fight strongly for their right to survive.”
In the meantime, residents inside the Saemangeum seawall have continued to demand compensation for damages, and the government and the Uri Party are recently preparing support measures to support bare-handed fishermen inside the Saemangeum seawall to maintain their livelihoods, so attention is being paid to what kind of variable this collective opposition from outside residents will play in.
In response to this, Jeonbuk-do said, "As the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries is in charge of license management and the government prepares livelihood support measures, there is no specific plan that Jeonbuk-do can do. However, we will make efforts to ensure that the demands of fishermen are accepted by conveying the demands of foreign fishermen to the government and political circles."
lc21@yna.co.kr

ko-news-notices-290-8372c75064.title: Promotion of Jeju-Udo submarine water pipe burial
ko-news-notices-290-8372c75064.text:
Promotion of Jeju-Udo submarine water pipe burial
2022-03-02
(Jeju = Yonhap News) Reporter Kim Seung-beom = A project to lay an underwater water pipe connecting Udo Island in Jeju City, which is attracting attention as an 'island within an island' tourist destination, and the main island of Jeju Island is being promoted.
The Jeju Special Self-Governing Province Water Resources Headquarters announced on the 24th that it plans to invest 10 billion won over three years from 2010 to 2012 to lay a water pipe connected to the seabed after conducting a feasibility review and basic design service in 2008 to fundamentally solve the water problem of Udo Island, which has recurring water supply shortages every summer when tourists flock to the island.
This water supply pipe has a total length of 18.5 km, including a 3.1 km underwater section between Jongdal and Udo, Gujwa-eup, and a plan is being planned to install it semi-permanently using PE special pipes to minimize corrosion caused by salt, waves, tsunamis, and damage to trawl fishing boats.
Udo Island spent 3.5 billion won between 1999 and 2001 to build a facility to desalinate up to 1,000 tons of salted sewage per day, so there is no problem with water supply for about 1,800 residents. However, in the summer, up to 3,400 tourists visit per day, resulting in a water shortage of about 500 to 600 tons.
Meanwhile, in Jeju Island, a 75mm submarine water pipe was laid in a 700m section between Hyeopjae, Hallim-eup and Biyangdo in 1972, supplying 38 tons of tap water per day.
ksb@yna.co.kr

ko-news-notices-289-8372c75064.title: Even in clean water, sand can become contaminated.
ko-news-notices-289-8372c75064.text:
Even in clean water, sand can become contaminated.
2022-03-02
Even in clean water, sand can become contaminated.
Beach sand can be teeming with bacteria even when the ocean water is clear, according to a study published Tuesday.
Health officials know that urban runoff contaminates seawater with microorganisms such as E. coli and enterococci found in feces.
“Even on days when the water is very clear, bacteria can still remain in the sand for about a week,” said Jennifer Jay, a UCLA environmental engineering professor who led the study. “We believe this is an important exposure route for contamination.”
Jay and his graduate students surveyed three beaches during the 2003 storm: Surfrider Beach in Malibu, Santa Monica Beach and Mothers Beach in Marina del Rey.
The survey found that bacterial concentrations on protected beaches, which parents enjoy visiting with their children, were up to 1,000 times higher than on beaches open to the ocean.
However, Jay said it is difficult to prove the health threat these bacteria pose because no health standards have been established for beach sediments.
Next, the researchers will investigate viruses present in the sand.
Heal the Bay plans to release a list of the most polluted California beaches on Wednesday.
Dated May 24, 2006 http://www.enn.com/today.html?id=10527

ko-news-notices-288-8372c75064.title: Songdo Beach's underwater breakwater is effective
ko-news-notices-288-8372c75064.text:
Songdo Beach's underwater breakwater is effective
2022-03-02
(Busan = Yonhap News) Reporter Park Seong-jin = It was found that the underwater breakwater installed at Songdo Beach in Busan is effective in preventing sand loss.
Professor Kim Do-sam of Korea Maritime and Ocean University reported the results of the Songdo Beach monitoring survey at the Seo-gu Office in Busan on the afternoon of the 19th, saying that the amount of sand increased due to the underwater breakwater installed off Songdo Beach.
According to Professor Kim, the amount of sand put into the white sand beach of Songdo Beach in July last year was 190,093 ㎥, but when measured in December last year, the amount was 164,935 ㎥, indicating that erosion occurred throughout the white sand beach.
However, from December of last year to February of this year, overall sand deposition occurred, and the amount of sand on the white sand beach increased again to 211,619㎥.
Professor Kim said, "If we look at the changes in the amount of sand at each point of the beach, the total amount of sand decreases in the summer due to general erosion, but the total amount of sand increases in the winter due to sedimentation. Although it is within the overall error range, the phenomenon of sand deposition is occurring."
Professor Kim explained, “This appears to be because the underwater breakwater created during the Songdo Coastal Comprehensive Development Project that started in 2000 prevented sand erosion.”
Through the Songdo development project, the Busan Seo-gu Office installed an underwater breakwater 40m wide and 300m long 50m below the water depth at 300-350m in front of the beach in 2004, greatly reducing the strength of waves to minimize sand loss and damage to surrounding shopping malls from summer typhoons.
sungjinpark@yna.co.kr

ko-news-notices-287-8372c75064.title: Joint promotion of water quality improvement in the waters off Incheon
ko-news-notices-287-8372c75064.text:
Joint promotion of water quality improvement in the waters off Incheon
2022-03-02
(Incheon = Yonhap News) Reporter Shin Min-jae = To improve the water quality of the sea off Incheon, a plan is being promoted where three local governments, including Incheon City, Seoul City, and Gyeonggi Province, and the central government to jointly share related project costs.
On the afternoon of the 19th, Incheon City held a service report on pollution factors and cost sharing plans in the sea off Incheon at the City Hall conference room and discussed ways to share the budget of 62.7 billion won needed for water quality improvement and marine waste disposal projects for five years from next year to 2011.
In April 2001, the city signed an agreement to jointly share (Incheon 50.2%, Gyeonggi 27%, Seoul 22.8%) the cost of 28.5 billion won for disposing of waste that floats to the sea off Incheon through the Han River and Imjin River for four years until the end of this year.
As the contribution support between Seoul City and Gyeonggi Province ends at the end of this year, the city provided research services to the Incheon Development Institute to prepare the basis needed to conclude a new agreement.
As a result of the service, while the existing agreement only jointly shared the cost of the marine waste disposal project in the sea off Incheon, the new agreement is analyzed to require sharing of project costs necessary for processing sediment pollutants to improve marine water quality and monitoring and investigating marine pollution. The city plans to actively pursue this.
In particular, we plan to request the central government to share the cost, considering that the pollution problem in the sea off Incheon is limited to the three cities and provinces in the metropolitan area, including Incheon, and that the area that actually benefits is wider.
For a total of KRW 62.7 billion, including KRW 42 billion in marine waste disposal project costs and KRW 20.7 billion in marine water quality improvement project costs over the next five years, the city organized the sharing ratio as 34.0-35.2% for Incheon City, 22.1-25.2% for Seoul City, 28.2%-32.6% for Gyeonggi-do, and 11.3-11.4% for the central government.
Based on the results of this service, the city plans to conclude a joint sharing agreement by the end of the year through working-level consultations and the Seoul Metropolitan Area Administrative Council.
matilda@yna.co.kr

ko-news-notices-286-8372c75064.title: Need to reexamine large-scale aggregate extraction on the southern coast
ko-news-notices-286-8372c75064.text:
Need to reexamine large-scale aggregate extraction on the southern coast
2022-03-02
(Tongyeong = Yonhap News) Reporter Lee Jeong-hoon = The Ministry of Environment expressed the opinion that a reexamination of the Korea Water Resources Corporation's plan to designate a large-scale aggregate extraction complex in the waters of Yokjido, Tongyeong, Gyeongsangnam-do is necessary due to the negative impact on the marine ecosystem.
According to the Tongyeong-Geoje Environmental Movement Federation and Tongyeong City on the 12th, the Ministry of Environment recently notified the Ministry of Construction and Transportation of the opinion that 'a reexamination of the project is necessary' regarding the preliminary environmental review data submitted by Korea Water Resources Corporation to designate an aggregate extraction complex in the southern exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of Yokjido.
In its opinion, the Ministry of Environment predicted that large-scale sea sand extraction will have a significant impact on marine animals and plants by causing changes in the topography of the seabed, and that fishermen will continue to demand compensation for damage to marine resources and fishing industry.
In addition, it was pointed out that there was not a sufficient process of gathering opinions, such as briefing sessions and public hearings, and that the review of the cumulative environmental impact of large-scale intensive development was insufficient because aggregate extraction was already taking place nearby.
However, the Ministry of Environment stated, "The notified opinion does not mean a complete 'disagreement' with the aggregate extraction project, and once all problems are resolved, there remains room for 'renegotiation' by determining implementation in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act."
Korea Water Resources Corporation is pursuing a plan to collect 73 million ㎥ of sea sand from this year to 2011 in the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) 50km south of Yokjido Island to ensure a stable supply of aggregate for the new port construction project.
seaman@yna.co.kr

ko-news-notices-285-8372c75064.title: Completion of the first field survey in the southwestern waters of Mokpo for the National Ocean Basic Map Survey
ko-news-notices-285-8372c75064.text:
Completion of the first field survey in the southwestern waters of Mokpo for the National Ocean Basic Map Survey
2022-03-02
The second field survey will be conducted from September to October and the survey in the southwestern waters of Mokpo will be completed.
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yoo-seop) announced that it completed the first field survey of the National Ocean Basic Map Survey on 4,700㎢ of the southwestern waters of Mokpo from April to June.
This survey was conducted on the ocean research vessel Badaro No. 1 (700-ton class) equipped with cutting-edge marine research equipment such as a multi-acoustic sounder and shallow stratum probe, and conducted comprehensive marine scientific exploration activities such as observation of underwater topography, gravity, sedimentation phenomena, and geomagnetic force. It has been conducted annually since 1996, targeting all seas of Korea. This year, a detailed survey was conducted in the southwestern waters of Mokpo.
This survey area is near Daeheuksan Island, Sojongwan Archipelago, and Chuja Archipelago. This sea area has abundant fish resources, so many fishing boats fish throughout the year. In particular, it is a major passageway for ships entering and leaving Mokpo Port and Daeheuksan Island Port, so it was a sea area that required precise surveys of underwater reefs and navigational hazards for safe navigation of ships.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “After reviewing the data from the first survey, we plan to conduct a second field survey from September to October to complete the survey of the southwestern waters of Mokpo, analyze the survey results, and use them as basic data for publishing the National Ocean Basic Map, which is the basis of maritime territory, publishing charts for navigational safety, establishing maritime development and maritime policies, and academic research.”

ko-news-notices-284-8372c75064.title: Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency Marine Research Laboratory launched
ko-news-notices-284-8372c75064.text:
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency Marine Research Laboratory launched
2022-03-02
Creation of high-quality marine information through scientific research and analysis
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yoo-seop) established a plan in 2006 to create high-value marine information through scientificization of marine research. 7. 3. A new marine research laboratory was launched.
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency was established in 1996. 8. 8. With the launch of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and a new start as a comprehensive marine research institute, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries has accumulated a vast amount of marine research data by deploying cutting-edge equipment and vessels. However, it has had significant limitations in producing high-value marine information that can meet the diverse needs of the public by systematically and scientifically analyzing this data.
In particular, as the former 12 nautical mile maritime territory concept was expanded to a 200 nautical mile exclusive economic zone with the entry into force of the United Nations Law on the Sea in 1994, competition for marine surveys and research is intensifying among Korea, China, and Japan to secure the upper hand in securing a 'new maritime territory'.
The Marine Research Laboratory is responsible for ▶ research on EEZ and continental shelf boundaries ▶ development of tsunami monitoring and forecasting technology to prevent marine-related disasters ▶ provision of basic data for marine resource development through analysis of ocean and seabed geological structures ▶ research and development of marine prediction technology that can minimize damage to life and property in the event of various marine accidents.
Meanwhile, the newly launched Marine Research Laboratory is comprised of a total of six doctoral-level researchers in the marine and fisheries field, including one researcher and five researchers.

ko-news-notices-283-8372c75064.title: Latest chart published near Daesan Port
ko-news-notices-283-8372c75064.text:
Latest chart published near Daesan Port
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yu-seop) announced that it has published a new revised chart near Daesan Port that reflects the latest information on the sea area near Daesan Port, Seosan-si, Chungcheongnam-do, and Taean Port, Taean-gun, for safe navigation of ships.
The chart published this time (chart number No. 357, scale 1:35,000) reflects precise bathymetry data and port geographical information surveyed using state-of-the-art multi-acoustic sounding and satellite positioning equipment.
In particular, it is expected to be of great help to port management operations and ship operations near Daesan Port by displaying changes in sea routes, anchorages and areas around Dolphin at Daesan Port and Taean Port, where many ships enter and depart, water depth, navigational hazards, etc.
Meanwhile, Daesan Port is a major port that is being developed as a multi-purpose pier to accommodate general cargo ships and container ships for the purpose of securing a maritime logistics center in the central West Sea. Active port construction is in progress for ship docking, and up-to-date port information is desperately needed.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “We plan to continue producing and distributing the latest charts in the future to ensure maritime traffic safety and provide information necessary for marine development and conservation.”
Charts can be purchased through a chart sales agency (☎ 02-701-9981, 051-466-0760) or through the company's Internet website (www.chartkorea.com).

ko-news-notices-282-8372c75064.title: New tide stations in Yeomha Channel and the Han River estuary
ko-news-notices-282-8372c75064.text:
New tide stations in Yeomha Channel and the Han River estuary
2022-03-02
Tidal forecasts for the Han River estuary to begin in 2008
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director General Yu-seop Jeong) announced that tidal observations would begin in August at Jeollyu in the Han River estuary and at Ganghwa Bridge. The Han River estuary is a major tidal river influenced by freshwater discharged from the Han River and strong tides in the surrounding waters.
An agreement with the Han River Flood Control Office to share facilities enabled two new tide stations to be established. Long-term tidal observations would allow accurate tidal forecasts for the Han River estuary and waters around Ganghwa Island from 2008.
Strong tides in the estuary are known to influence the Han River as far upstream as Jamsu Bridge in Seoul. Accurate estuarine tidal forecasts are therefore essential to prevent flood damage and plan countermeasures during heavy rainfall in Seoul and Gyeonggi-do.
Strong currents and extensive tidal flats had previously made long-term observation difficult preventing the provision of accurate sea level prediction data.
An agency representative said that the new stations would improve public services by providing accurate information for coastal disaster prevention and for increasingly popular leisure activities such as tidal flat visits around Ganghwa Island.
The Han River estuary observations will be provided in real time from August on the agency's website (http://www.nori.go.kr).

ko-news-notices-281-8372c75064.title: 2006 marine and fisheries development implementation plan confirmed
ko-news-notices-281-8372c75064.text:
2006 marine and fisheries development implementation plan confirmed
2022-03-02
KRW 5.7464 trillion invested in 214 projects in 7 fields
The ‘2006 Marine and Fisheries Development Implementation Plan’ for the rational development and conservation of marine resources was finalized through a resolution at the Cabinet meeting on the 27th.
This implementation plan is a detailed annual implementation plan of the ‘Ocean Korea 21’, a 10♡ mid- to long-term plan established in 2000, and was jointly prepared by 12 central administrative agencies, including the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Energy, and the Ministry of Environment.
This year, a total of KRW 5.7464 trillion is planned to be invested in 214 projects in 7 fields, including creating a marine land for life, production, and living, establishing a sustainable fisheries foundation, and establishing a shipping and logistics center in Northeast Asia. By ministry, ▲ Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries KRW 3.9663 trillion (69%) ▲ Ministry of Environment KRW 673.4 billion (11.7%) ▲ Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry KRW 349.5 billion (6.1%) ▲ Ministry of Culture and Tourism KRW 123.9 billion (2.2%).
In particular, this year, key tasks will include strengthening the management of marine territories such as Dokdo, uninhabited islands, and EEZs, establishing a fisheries industry base such as developing fisheries technology and fishing village business models, and promoting a strategy to become a high value-added international logistics hub.
Meanwhile, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries is promoting the establishment of a ‘Future Maritime Strategy’ with the goal of finalizing it in September in order to respond to the trends of advanced maritime countries and neighboring countries that are strengthening their maritime policy stance and to promote a national maritime policy that is a step forward from the perspective of policy consumers and the public.
This strategy plans to include maritime policy strategies for Korea to become one of the top five maritime powers within the next 10 years.
Based on this, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries plans to establish a plan linked to the basic plan for maritime and fisheries development and confirm it as a national plan in the first half of next year.
An official from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries said, “This year is a meaningful year as it marks the 10th anniversary of the launch of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. We plan to prepare a roadmap that will take a leap forward by supplementing the basic plan for ocean and fisheries development based on the future ocean strategy plan.”

ko-news-notices-280-8372c75064.title: [Busan/Gyeongnam] “Are they going to ruin the golden fishing grounds by sand mining?”
ko-news-notices-280-8372c75064.text:
[Busan/Gyeongnam] “Are they going to ruin the golden fishing grounds by sand mining?”
2022-03-02
[Busan/Gyeongnam] “Are they going to ruin the golden fishing grounds by sand mining?”
“Why are we spending hundreds of billions of won to promote the ‘sea ranching project’? Extracting sea sand will completely destroy the golden fishing grounds…”
Citizens and fishermen of Tongyeong, South Gyeongsang Province, are holding a protest to cancel the government's policy of designating a sea sand mining complex.
Korea Water Resources Corporation has decided to extract 72 million m³ of sea sand from 27 km² within the exclusive economic zone, 50 km south of Yokjido, Tongyeong City, by 2012.
To this end, we applied for designation as an ‘aggregate extraction complex’ to the Ministry of Construction and Transportation last month. The Ministry of Construction and Transportation is currently discussing the use of sea areas according to the complex designation with six government ministries, including the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the Ministry of Environment.
The Yokji Sand Extraction Opposition Struggle Committee and the Tongyeong Development Citizens’ Council will hold a ‘Citizen Rally Against the Designation of Aggregate Extraction Complex’ at Gangguan Cultural Center in Tongyeong City at 10 am on the 28th with over 4,000 people in attendance.
The Struggle Committee argued, “The sea, the ‘second food warehouse’ that feeds our people, must not be damaged any further,” and “the Ministry of Construction and Transportation must immediately withdraw its policy of designating an aggregate extraction complex.”
Cho Yong-je, chairman of the Struggle Committee, said on the 25th, “The sea on the southern coast has already been seriously damaged due to sea sand extraction by individual operators, with seaweed dying and bleaching occurring,” and “it is impossible to restore the sea damaged by aggregate extraction.”
They argue that it is desirable in the long run to import sand for construction projects from China or North Korea, even if the unit price is slightly higher.
After the rally ended, the Struggle Committee decided to hold a street protest all the way to the Donam-dong Passenger Ship Terminal and send a protest group of about 30 people to the Ministry of Construction and Transportation and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
If the demands are not accepted, a maritime protest will be held by mobilizing hundreds of fishing boats in the sea sand mining area.
Reporter Kang Jeong-hoon manman@donga.com

ko-news-notices-279-8372c75064.title: Emergency disposal of sewage and wastewater contaminated sediments
ko-news-notices-279-8372c75064.text:
Emergency disposal of sewage and wastewater contaminated sediments
2022-03-02
‘Do not throw any more sludge (contaminated sediment) into the sea.’
The Ministry of Environment was given the task of disposing of more than 5,000 tons of sludge that had been dumped into the sea per day on land within five years. This is because ocean dumping of waste has been banned in accordance with the ‘London Convention’ since 2011.
Currently, the amount of sewage and wastewater polluted sediment (organic sludge) produced from domestic sewage and wastewater treatment plants is 7,052 tons per day. Of these, 5,418 tons, or 76.8%, are abandoned in the sea. Sludge is loaded onto large ships and taken out to sea in the East and West Seas.
Special measures must be taken to treat this 100% on land by 2010. The organic sludge treatment facility currently in operation has a daily capacity of only 1,798 tons, but the amount generated is increasing. In 2011, the daily sludge production is expected to reach 11,303 tons, which is 6.3 times the current daily processing capacity (1,798 tons).
According to the comprehensive plan prepared by the Ministry of Environment on the 23rd, the urgent priority is to install 106 new treatment facilities across the country, including 86 sewage sludge treatment facilities and 20 wastewater sludge treatment facilities. This project requires a total of KRW 859 billion over the next five years, including KRW 418.7 billion from the national treasury, KRW 376.4 billion from local governments, and KRW 63.9 billion from private funds. Once the sludge treatment facility is complete, the Gangwon and Chungcheong regions, which have many cement factories, will use sludge as a raw material for cement, and rural areas such as Gyeongnam and Jeonnam will focus on decomposing it into compost or producing fecal soil through raising earthworms. The area near the landfill is planned to be recycled as cover materials.
An official from the Ministry of Environment said, “Since the amount of sludge generated from wastewater from individual businesses is similar to that from sewage and wastewater treatment plants, we will prevent it from being dumped into the sea from 2011 through separate guidance and promotion.”
〈Reporter Kim Jeong-seop〉

ko-news-notices-278-8372c75064.title: 8 islands disappeared in 100 years... Impact of reclamation in the sea off Gunsan
ko-news-notices-278-8372c75064.text:
8 islands disappeared in 100 years... Impact of reclamation in the sea off Gunsan
2022-03-02
Eight islands disappeared from Gunsan, Jeollabuk-do alone due to over 100 years of land reclamation. In addition, the Saemangeum project, which is scheduled to be completed in 2011, is expected to soon turn four islands into land, bringing the number of islands that will disappear to 12.
According to the ‘Gunsan Island Journal’ published by Gunsan City, Jeollabuk-do on the 22nd, there were 71 islands in the Gunsan area until the 1880s, but now only 63 islands remain, including 16 inhabited islands and 47 uninhabited islands.
First, three islands, including Ipido, Muuiin, and Ganaedo, disappeared due to successive farmland development projects on the northern bank of the Mangyeong River by Lee Wan-yong in the early 1890s and in Okseo-myeon, Bulheungeopsa, Japan between 1920 and 1923. Afterwards, with the completion of the Gunsan Regional Industrial Complex in 1978, the Gunsan National Industrial Complex in 1988, and the Gunsan District of the Gunjang National Industrial Complex at the end of this year, five islands, including Osikdo, Naecho, Jangsando, Jodo, and Bieungdo, disappeared. Most of the eight disappeared islands only have traces of the past, like hills around industrial complexes.
The total land obtained through five rounds of large-scale reclamation is approximately 16.17 million pyeong, with 8.61 million pyeong being used as industrial land and 7.56 million pyeong being used as agricultural land. In the future, when the Saemangeum reclamation project connecting Gunsan and Buan is completed, four additional islands, including Yami Island, Shinsi Island, Namga-ryeok Island, and Bukgaryeok-do, are scheduled to become land.
Gunsan = Reporter Kim Yong-kwon ygkim@kmib.co.kr

ko-news-notices-277-8372c75064.title: Yellow Sea joint conservation project drifting
ko-news-notices-277-8372c75064.text:
Yellow Sea joint conservation project drifting
2022-03-02
The yellow sea ecosystem conservation project is on the verge of collapse.
The National Institute of Fisheries Science announced on the 21st that the Yellow Sea Wide Ecosystem Conservation Project (YSLME), which has been jointly promoted by the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), Korea, and China since March of last year to improve the marine environment in the West Sea, has not even been able to conduct a survey of the marine environment even one year after implementation due to China's refusal to share survey data. In particular, although China agreed to share data at a secretariat meeting at the end of last month, it did not provide data at a scientific meeting held two days later.
This project is one of the international cooperation projects to protect the rapidly deteriorating environment of the West Sea, and is divided into three stages: joint investigation (TDA) to diagnose the environmental condition of the West Sea, protection of fisheries resources, preparation of a strategic action plan (SAP) to reduce environmental pollution, and implementation through law and system improvement.
The YSLME Secretariat is proposing that if China continues to refuse joint investigation, the investigation should be conducted first on the Korean coast where the investigation is possible. However, in this case, only the information on our coast will be unilaterally transferred to the Chinese side, which goes against the purpose of a joint project between countries.
However, as a joint investigation between Korea and China is essential to prevent the deterioration of the marine environment in the West Sea, there are growing criticisms that the government should take action directly rather than leaving this issue to the secretariat. In 1995, the World Watch Institute designated the West Sea as one of the seven dying seas, along with the Black Sea and the South China Sea. In 1999, 560 million tons of wastewater flowed into the West Sea through Bohai Bay (Bohai Bay), but the tidal flats that purify pollutants continued to shrink. In China, 2.94 million ha of mudflats were lost from 1950 to 1985, in North Korea about 290,000 ha since 1981, and in Korea, about 80,000 ha since 1987 through land reclamation projects.
An official from the National Institute of Fisheries Science said, "Most marine environment survey projects that require China's cooperation, such as the Korea-China joint buoy installation project that has been in progress since last year and the Yangtze River basin environmental survey, are drifting. As the number of factors that threaten the marine environment of the West Sea, such as the Three Gorges Dam, is increasing, the government needs to strongly request China's cooperation on environmental issues."
Reporter Nam Seung-pyo

ko-news-notices-276-8372c75064.title: “Harmful red tide is expected to appear in early August this year.”
ko-news-notices-276-8372c75064.text:
“Harmful red tide is expected to appear in early August this year.”
2022-03-02
Harmful red tide, which causes enormous damage to fisheries on the southern coast, is expected to appear in early August this year.
Dr. Oh Hyeon-joo of the National Institute of Fisheries Science South Sea Fisheries Research Institute said this at the 2006 South Coast Red Tide Countermeasures Symposium held at the Yeosu Regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Office Situation Room on the morning of the 19th.
Dr. Oh predicted, "Red tide caused by Cochlodinium, a harmful red tide, is expected to first occur in the central waters of the South Sea around early August, when the surface water temperature along the southern coast reaches 23-26℃, especially in the Nado-Namhaedo sea area where a strong coastal water temperature front is formed."
He also claimed, “It is very difficult to accurately forecast red tide at this stage due to the strength of the Kuroshio Warm Current, precipitation, and typhoons,” and added, “There is a need to continuously compare and analyze the sea conditions in the coastal waters of Korea in the future to consider the relationship with the occurrence of red tide.”
Also, on this day, Kim Doo-yong, in charge of red tide at the Yeosu Maritime Affairs Office, said, "Recent red tide has the characteristics of being early, simultaneous, high density, persistent for a long time, and distributed in large quantities in the lower floors, making it difficult to confirm with the naked eye." He added, "There is an urgent need to prepare countermeasures against this."
In particular, Kim in charge pointed out the problems with red tide countermeasures, saying, "Red tide control is implemented under the government's lead, with a lack of participation from fishermen, and relies only on red clay spraying, so the control effect is insufficient when large-scale outbreaks occur, and there are limitations in monitoring a wide area with small red tide surveillance ships."
He also emphasized, "In the case of the control equipment's oxygen supply, it is not effective when large-scale red tide occurs, and it is difficult to install and use the cage fish farm barrier facility, so fishermen are avoiding it." He also emphasized, "For effective eradication, it is necessary to develop new relief materials other than red clay, modernize and scientificize surveillance ships and survey equipment, suppress the development of fishing grounds, and form an autonomous red tide control group."
At the symposium on red tide control measures held for the first time this year, officials from red tide-related organizations such as the Yeosu Maritime Administration, Jeonnam Province, and the National Institute of Fisheries Science served as presenters and presented trends in red tide occurrence in foreign countries, measures to prevent red tide damage in fish farms, and cases of development of red tide control technology.
Last year, red tide in Yeosu waters appeared about 20 days earlier than the previous year and spread widely at high densities, causing the death of 1.56 million sea bream, rockfish, and sea bass being farmed, causing damage worth 870 million won.
Reporter Nam Hyun-ho hyunho@yna.co.kr (Yeosu = Yonhap News)

ko-news-notices-275-8372c75064.title: “Destruction of fish habitat on the southern coast of the public sea sand extraction complex.”
ko-news-notices-275-8372c75064.text:
“Destruction of fish habitat on the southern coast of the public sea sand extraction complex.”
2022-03-02
There are concerns that the project to designate a public aggregate (sand) extraction complex, which the government is pursuing to prevent indiscriminate mining of sea sand on the southern coast, may actually destroy the marine environment.
According to related ministries such as the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the Ministry of Construction and Transportation on the 19th, Korea Water Resources Corporation plans to submit an application to the Ministry of Construction and Transportation on the 25th to designate a public aggregate extraction complex with 10 tools and an area of ​​​​27km2 in the sea area 50km south of Yokjido, Tongyeong-si, Gyeongsangnam-do.
The Ministry of Construction and Transportation plans to allow sand extraction as early as August after consulting with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries on sea area use.
The expected extraction volume is approximately 72 million m³ over 5 years and will be used for large-scale port development national projects such as Busan New Port, Ulsan New Port, and Gwangyang Port.
However, related industries and local residents are protesting, saying that the government is encroaching on private business areas and destroying the marine ecosystem.
This is because a private company has been mining sand just 11km away from the sea area that the government is trying to designate as a public extraction complex.
Fishermen and some environmental groups claim that “if additional large-scale sand extraction complexes are designated and developed, the fishing infrastructure will be damaged by vibration, noise, muddy water, changes in fish migration routes, and destruction of marine ecosystems such as spawning and habitats.”
The Tongyeong City Council also adopted a ‘proposition opposing the designation of a public extraction complex’ and sent it to the Blue House and the National Assembly.
Opinions within the government are mixed.
A government official said, “In the past, individual companies have been extracting sea sand indiscriminately, causing controversy over preferential treatment, and post-sale environmental management has been inadequate. To resolve these problems, we revised the Aggregate Extraction Act in 2004 and introduced the Aggregate Public Management System, allowing the Korea Water Resources Corporation, a public enterprise, to systematically manage the public extraction complex.”
However, another government official countered, saying, “The law stipulates that the designation of public extraction complexes should be ‘limited only when it causes significant disruption to the operation of the national economy.’” He added, “There is no immediate shortage of aggregates, so there is no need for the government to unreasonably invade the private sector.”
Reporter Bae Geuk-in bae2150@donga.com

ko-news-notices-274-8372c75064.title: Tidal benchmark survey results for the northern West Coast
ko-news-notices-274-8372c75064.text:
Tidal benchmark survey results for the northern West Coast
2022-03-02
54 benchmarks at 19 locations along the coast from Seongmun-myeon Dangjin-gun to Ganghwa Bridge in Ganghwa-eup
The West Sea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Office of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Chang-seop Choi) announced the results of its tidal benchmark survey along this coast. These benchmarks provide reference elevations for sea level.
The survey covered 54 benchmarks at 19 locations including Incheon Daebu Island and Jebu Island. Fifteen missing benchmarks including those at Songdo in Incheon Sanggarido in Siheung and Jebu Island were replaced. Where soft ground had subsided by less than about 1–2 cm the reference elevations were measured accurately and corrected.
Tidal benchmarks (TBMs) are installed and managed by the agency. After tidal observations establish local mean sea level the benchmark elevation is marked. The information is important for port and coastal development and coastal flood prevention.
The results are available through the agency's tidal data service at http://oceandata.nori.go.kr/.
The office is checking the presence loss and subsidence of benchmarks in the northern West Sea to manage them effectively. The coastal survey ran from March 15 to April 15. A further survey of 54 benchmarks at 19 island locations is planned for two months beginning in September.

ko-news-notices-273-8372c75064.title: ‘Environmental Impact Assessment’ appears on the Internet
ko-news-notices-273-8372c75064.text:
‘Environmental Impact Assessment’ appears on the Internet
2022-03-02
The environmental impact assessment contents and process for determining whether major development projects are eco-friendly can be viewed at a glance online.
The Ministry of Environment announced that its Environmental Impact Assessment Information Support System (http://eiass.go.kr) opened to the public on the 1st. It contains original environmental impact assessment reports consultation opinions environmental conditions at project sites environmental quality measurements and geographic information.
This system is the world's first environmental evaluation management and disclosure system and is expected to have effects such as expanding the public's right to know and surveillance, improving the level of environmental evaluation, and shortening the evaluation period.
The information subject to disclosure includes 22 items, including the original text of 494 environmental impact assessments negotiated since 1998 that business operators and evaluation agencies agreed to disclose (including the text and consultation opinions), business overview, environmental status, and environmental quality measurement data.
By building a geographic information database, business location within the selected region, results of animal and plant surveys, various conservation areas, environmental quality measurement points, environmental impact assessment regulations, research reports, reviewers and progress status of ongoing evaluations are provided in real time.
The government has built a database of 1,810 original texts out of 3,061 cases for which environmental impact assessment consultations were completed from 1982 to the end of last year, and has been collecting opinions on consent for disclosure from business operators and preparation agents to resolve copyright issues resulting from the disclosure of environmental impact assessments.
However, evaluation documents that objected to disclosure for reasons such as security facilities and trade secrets, or opinions could not be collected due to unknown addresses, and environmental impact assessments of national defense and military facilities were excluded from this disclosure.
Considering that the evaluation documents in the early stages of the introduction of the evaluation system were qualitatively different from the current evaluation documents and had little value for use when writing evaluation documents, evaluation documents made after 1998, when the Environmental Policy Evaluation Institute began reviewing evaluation documents, were subject to disclosure.
A database of environmental impact assessments will continue to be built by the end of this year, and 1,400 environmental impact reports, which are the results of an investigation into environmental changes over a certain period of time after the evaluation consultation, will soon be made public.
In addition, it was decided to add a resident opinion collection system that allows residents to express their opinions during public notice and public inspection of the draft evaluation report, and a system that provides information at a glance on the progress of the environmental impact assessment, such as receipt, review, supplementation, and consultation of the environmental impact assessment report.
We plan to post various statistical data related to environmental impact assessment, such as registration of technical personnel and administrative disposition details of environmental impact assessment preparation agents, and environmental impact assessment consultation results, and use them as administrative data.
The Ministry of Environment said that when revising the 'Environment, Transportation, Disaster, etc. Impact Assessment Act' in the future, it will establish new regulations for disclosure of evaluation reports and establish a system in which evaluation reports will be automatically disclosed from the stage of receipt without a separate consent process.
(Seoul = Yonhap News)

ko-news-notices-272-8372c75064.title: Undersea terrain exploration in the central waters of the southern coast was conducted.
ko-news-notices-272-8372c75064.text:
Undersea terrain exploration in the central waters of the southern coast was conducted.
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency's South Sea Ocean Survey Office (Director Jae-seop Lee) announced that it will conduct a precise hydrographic survey of the southern waters of Yokjido, Tongyeong, Gyeongsangnam-do for five months starting in May.
This survey plans to conduct a comprehensive ocean exploration, including the topographical shape and sedimentation phenomenon, by mobilizing the ocean research vessel Namhae-ro, which is equipped with a multi-beam acoustic probe and a satellite positioning device, which are state-of-the-art submarine topography survey equipment.
