The survey results are used as publication data for precise and electronic charts through 3D graphic analysis of the shape of submarine hills, etc., and are also used as basic data needed for the development of the marine industry, such as producing submarine topography maps for the entire southern coast and exploring submarine mineral resources in the future.
In addition, navigational hazards such as sunken ships and reefs discovered during the investigation are expected to be quickly provided as navigation information and greatly contribute to securing maritime traffic safety.

ko-news-notices-271-8372c75064.title: Spring tidal-current observations begin in the Gunsan navigation channel
ko-news-notices-271-8372c75064.text:
Spring tidal-current observations begin in the Gunsan navigation channel
2022-03-02
The West Sea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Office of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Chang-seop Choi) announced that spring tidal-current observations would be conducted at the entrance to the Gunsan navigation channel for one month starting on April 29.
The hydrographic survey vessel Hwanghaero will observe spring circulation near channel Light Buoy No. 2 following winter observations in February to improve the accuracy of tidal-current forecasts.
An office representative said the observations would support safe navigation and efficient route planning for vessels entering and leaving Gunsan Port. They would also help explain changes in water circulation and sedimentation caused by changes in seabed topography. Seasonal observations would continue to characterize tidal currents in both the Gunsan channel and the Saemangeum waters.
Port construction at Gunsan and Janghang and seawall construction have rapidly changed hydrodynamics and sedimentation in the Gunsan Port and Saemangeum waters. The final Saemangeum seawall closure was completed on April 21 2006. Changes to the wider marine environment could affect safe navigation for both small and large vessels making continued marine monitoring necessary.

ko-news-notices-270-8372c75064.title: Promotion of 3D video production in the South Sea area of ​​southern Jeju
ko-news-notices-270-8372c75064.text:
Promotion of 3D video production in the South Sea area of ​​southern Jeju
2022-03-02
You will be able to see the bottom of the sea in the southernmost waters of Korea's EEZ (Exclusive Economic Zone) in three dimensions.
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yoo-seop) announced that it will invest a total of 100 million won from April to November to create 3D underwater images of the southern waters of Jeju Island.
The data used this time will be reprocessed into 3D by reprocessing the seabed topographical data produced by the National Oceanographic Research Institute from 2000 to 2002 through the National Ocean Basic Map Survey project, and a vast amount of data with a total survey volume of 91,000 km and a data volume of 25 GB will be used.
This video clearly identifies the topography of the seabed near the exclusive economic zones of Korea, China, and Japan, about 300 km away from Jeju Island, including Ieo Island, where the comprehensive marine science base built for marine forecasting and disaster prevention is located.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “Once this video is created, it will be used as important data for maritime administration as it will allow you to see the shape of the seafloor easily and in detail by visualizing the sea covered with water in three dimensions. It will also contribute to raising public awareness of the ocean.”

ko-news-notices-269-8372c75064.title: A glance at the shape of the seafloor in Ulsan Port...
ko-news-notices-269-8372c75064.text:
A glance at the shape of the seafloor in Ulsan Port...
2022-03-02
Ulsan Port 3D underwater video production
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yoo-seop) announced that it had produced a 3D undersea video that provides a three-dimensional view of the seabed in the waters around Ulsan Port and Onsan Port.
This video was created in 3D using seafloor information surveyed for 1,720km of this sea area, and the shape of submarine facilities such as submarine pipes was identified by visualizing the sea in three dimensions.
This was carried out jointly with the Ulsan Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries under the technical cooperation of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency, and was produced as a 3D video using seafloor data accurately surveyed using the latest marine survey equipment, such as the multibeam echo sounder (Multibeam Echo Sounder) and obstacle detection equipment (Sidescan Sonar), from August last year to February this year.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “This video has the effect of allowing you to see the seabed directly as if you were seeing it with your own eyes, so it is expected to be actively used as data for safe ship operation and port operation management, including maritime traffic control.”
Meanwhile, the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency plans to produce 3D undersea video for the southern coast and waters around Jeju this year.

ko-news-notices-268-8372c75064.title: Production of latest charts for Onsan Port
ko-news-notices-268-8372c75064.text:
Production of latest charts for Onsan Port
2022-03-02
Reflection of 3D precise seafloor survey information
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yu-seop) announced that it has published a new revised chart that reflects the latest information on the waters of Onsan Port in Ulsan City for safe navigation of ships.
The newly published chart (scale: 1/10,000) reflects 3D precision seafloor survey information surveyed using state-of-the-art surveying equipment, multi-acoustic sounding equipment and satellite positioning equipment, and includes changes in water depth, coastline, and navigational hazards.
The area with newly revised information in this chart is the entry route to Onsan Port, where ships enter and depart frequently, and is very important for port operation management, such as extending the No.B submarine pipe for crude oil transfer, reef dredging within the port, and construction of Ulsan New Port.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “The publication of this chart is expected to be of great help to the safe navigation of ships sailing in the waters of Onsan Port,” and added, “We plan to continue producing and distributing charts to provide information necessary for maritime safety and fishing activities in the future.”

ko-news-notices-267-8372c75064.title: Controversy over dredging work off Sinseondae
ko-news-notices-267-8372c75064.text:
Controversy over dredging work off Sinseondae
2022-03-02
The government's port policy is going back and forth over dredging of the sea in front of Sinseondae Pier, Busan's representative container terminal.
On the 11th, the Busan Regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Agency announced that it had decided to provide expert services as it needed an economic feasibility analysis to carry out the deep dredging work to deepen the sea in front of Sinseondae Pier as a non-administrative port construction project. After the Busan Maritime Administration announced its policy to implement increased dredging work, the immediate implementation of the dredging work was put on hold at a recently held meeting with officials of the Busan Maritime Administration, Busan Port Authority (BPA), and Shinsundae Container Terminal (PECT).
Because of this, the dredging work for Sinseondae Pier, requested by PECT, was delayed again. Non-administrative port construction refers to a construction method in which port construction, which should be carried out with the government's budget, is first implemented with private capital and then the construction costs are compensated by the government through reductions in port usage fees, etc.
Prior to this, the Busan Regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Agency tentatively decided to carry out dredging work to deepen the water depth of the entry/departure and circling water routes at Sinseondae Pier from the current 14.5m to 15m to 16m in a non-administrative port construction manner in order to avoid difficulties in berthing of ultra-large container ships.
It is known that the reason Busan Port's facility improvement policy is losing consistency is due to differences in opinions between the Port Logistics Department within the Busan Maritime Administration and the Busan Port Construction Office. The Port Logistics Department announced its policy to approve dredging work at Sinseondae Pier, citing sufficient social feasibility for dredging work. However, the Busan Port Construction Office insists that, as it is a port construction project that involves substantial government budget, it must first investigate through services whether there is a sufficient reason to carry out the construction and predict fleet demand.
Meanwhile, PECT is investing 14 billion won to promote dredging work as a non-administrative port construction project due to difficulties in using the dock for very large ships full of cargo, but it was canceled last year due to the Busan Port Authority's refusal to preserve the investment cost.
Reporter Cho Jin-man jmcho@kookje.co.kr

ko-news-notices-266-8372c75064.title: Reclamation for the New Port South Container Terminal gets back on track
ko-news-notices-266-8372c75064.text:
Reclamation for the New Port South Container Terminal gets back on track
2022-03-02
Reclamation work on the South Container Terminal at Busan Port New Port has resumed with the resolution of the sand dispute between companies.
According to the Busan Regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Agency on the 2nd, Daelim Industrial, the contractor for Phase 2-2 of the South Container Terminal, and Dado Shipping, a sand extraction supplier, reached an agreement on the sand supply price issue. These companies have shown sharp differences in their positions on the price of sand, which has resulted in significant delays in reclamation work, but they have made concessions one by one after deciding that they cannot delay it any further, and have not disclosed the exact price.
As a result, the supply of sand, which had been suspended since December 15 of last year, was resumed from this day, allowing the construction of the New Port South Container Terminal to become active again.
For this purpose, Dado Shipping is mobilizing all nine ships it currently has, scooping up sand from the sea 50km southeast of Yokjido on the south coast, and supplying it to the new port in earnest. Dado Shipping decided to increase sand supply as much as possible by securing additional ships if necessary.
Daelim Industrial also plans to invest more manpower and equipment into reclamation work to make up for the disruption caused by the interruption of sand supply this year to ensure that there are no disruptions in the completion of the dock in September 2008.
A total of 7.5 million ㎥ of sand will be used for the construction of the South Container pier, but only 500,000 ㎥ was supplied for sand pillar driving (SCP) last year. Accordingly, it appears that more than 4 million ㎥ of sand will need to be supplied in the future, including 1.7 million ㎥ that was not brought in last year and 2.4 million ㎥ this year.
However, the Busan Port Construction Office of the Busan Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Agency, the construction ordering agency, has become difficult to avoid criticism for neglecting actual management and supervision, such as claiming that there was no disruption to the overall construction period because the construction of the South Container pier was not completed for about three months due to the suspension of sand imports, as it was not a major process.
Construction of the lower part of the New Port South Container Terminal began in December 2004 and is scheduled for completion in September 2008. The current progress rate reached 25% as of the end of February, and the construction cost was 233.8 billion won.
In relation to this, an official from the port industry in the Busan region said, "Only when the new airline, which is a national project, is carried out smoothly will Busan Port be able to step up as a logistics hub in Northeast Asia." He added, "Supervisory authorities need to be thoroughly prepared for various disputes related to the import of construction materials and construction." Reporter Cho Jin-man jmcho@kookje.co.kr
Reporter Cho Jin-man jmcho@kookje.co.kr

ko-news-notices-265-8372c75064.title: ″Saemangeum, agricultural water available in 2012″… Seoul National University College of Agriculture
ko-news-notices-265-8372c75064.text:
″Saemangeum, agricultural water available in 2012″… Seoul National University College of Agriculture
2022-03-02
A survey showed that Saemangeum Lake, which has caused controversy over water pollution, will meet the level 4 water standards for use as agricultural water in 2012, when construction was completed.
The research team of Professor Park Seung-woo of Seoul National University's College of Agriculture announced on the 2nd that as a result of a six-month investigation at the request of the 'Saemangeum Environmental Measures Working Committee' in August last year, the total phosphorus (T-P) content in the Mangyeong waters of Saemangeum Lake in 2012 was predicted to be 0.094 mg/l, meeting the level 4 water quality standards (less than 0.1 mg/l).
Mangyeong Water Station is a place where a water quality prediction survey conducted by the Ministry of Environment and a public-private joint investigation team in 2001 concluded that even if the government's water quality conservation measures were applied, the total phosphorus content in 2012 was 0.103㎎/ℓ, making it difficult to achieve the level 4 water quality goal.
First, the research team revealed that since August 2002, approximately 300 million tons of power generation water from the nearby Yongdam Dam has been flowing into the upper reaches of the Mangyeong River annually, causing a clear dilution effect of pollutants. In addition, it was analyzed that the population of Jeonbuk decreased by 52,000 people in 2002 compared to 1998, and the number of Korean beef and dairy cows decreased by 8.9% and 2.7%, respectively, during the same period, resulting in a significant decrease in pollutant emissions.
In addition, the research team added that the government implemented strong water quality conservation measures after the Ministry of Environment's investigation in 2001, which significantly reduced the amount of pollutants flowing into the Mangyeong Water Area, which is also evidence for meeting the level 4 water standards.
Professor Park said, “As of 2003, major water quality items such as biological oxygen demand (BOD) and total phosphorus have improved significantly, so if the original water quality measures are implemented without a hitch, it is expected that water quality can be improved beyond the target.” Kookmin Ilbo Cookie News Reporter Noh Yong-taek nyt@kmib.co.kr

ko-news-notices-264-8372c75064.title: Tidal flat area reduced by half in 32 years
ko-news-notices-264-8372c75064.text:
Tidal flat area reduced by half in 32 years
2022-03-02
A study showed that the area of ​​Korea's mudflats, known as a treasure trove of marine ecosystems, will decrease by half in 32 years from 1964 to this year.
According to the Korea Environmental Policy Evaluation Institute (KEI) on the 30th, the area of ​​domestic tidal flats in 1964 as shown in the ‘Korean Maritime Handbook’ was 3,905 ㎢, but considering the reclamation of the west coast, the tidal flat area is expected to decrease to 2,000 ㎢ this year and further decrease to less than 1,500 ㎢ in 2015.
It was found that 810.5㎢ of tidal flats have been officially reclaimed since 1987, when development on the west coast began in earnest, until this year, with the Saemangeum project (208㎢) and Sihwa Lake in Gyeonggi Province (180㎢) accounting for 48%, leading to the loss of tidal flats.
Currently, Jeonnam is the largest tidal flat in Korea at 44%, followed by Gyeonggi at 35%, Chungnam at 13%, Jeonbuk at 5%, and Gyeongnam (including Busan) at 3%. Jeollanam-do and Gyeonggi, which are on the west coast, account for the majority (80%).
The researcher pointed out that in the past 10 years, coastal mudflats have rapidly decreased by 30-40%, especially on the west coast, due to large-scale reclamation projects, and that there are frequent cases of marine reclamation work being stopped, reduced, or changed due to indiscriminate development and environmental destruction.
In fact, among the 51 marine reclamation projects for which environmental impact assessment consultations were completed over the three years since 2002, 15 (30%) projects were reduced or canceled due to environmental problems, resulting in 3 out of 10 projects being halted.
Accordingly, the researcher proposed a plan to install an anti-fouling membrane during the construction process to prevent the spread of floating soil due to landfill and dredging, and to establish an eco-friendly management system by dividing landfill targets into conservation areas, development management areas, and development maintenance areas.
Reporter Kim Seong-yong ksy@yna.co.kr (Seoul = Yonhap News)

ko-news-notices-263-8372c75064.title: U.S. FDA: “Yeosu Gamak Bay sea sanitary environment is good”
ko-news-notices-263-8372c75064.text:
U.S. FDA: “Yeosu Gamak Bay sea sanitary environment is good”
2022-03-02
The sanitary environment of the sea in the Gamak Bay area on the southern coast of Jeollanam-do was found to be good.
Jeonnam Province announced on the 27th that two employees, including a shellfish hygiene expert from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), recently conducted an on-site investigation in the Gamak Bay (4,188 ha) area of ​​Yeosu and assessed that the sea hygiene was very good.
Michael Anti, an employee of the U.S. FDA, said in an evaluation held at Yeosu City Hall after an on-site inspection, “The level was satisfactory in terms of maintaining a certain distance between the designated sea area and fish farms, cleanliness of the sea and coastline, marking the boundaries of the designated sea area, and blocking the discharge of land-based pollutants,” and added, “It is very systematically and well managed.”
U.S. FDA employees also expressed satisfaction with measures to reduce water pollution through thorough record management of antibiotic use in offshore fish farms.
From the 22nd to the 24th, the U.S. FDA conducted an on-site inspection of hygiene management in designated waters in the Jeollanam-do region, including Gamak Bay in Yeosu and Narodo in Goheung. FDA inspections are conducted every two years based on the Korea-US Shellfish Sanitation Agreement signed in 1972 and the Memorandum of Understanding between the two countries exchanged in 2003. It mainly focuses on the sanitary environment of Gamak Bay, including the management of pollutants.
The U.S. FDA's safety assurance has a ripple effect of externally acknowledging the safety of all marine products produced in Jeonnam waters, which has a significant impact on future fish and shellfish exports. Gamak Bay produces approximately 7,000 tons of shellfish such as oysters, clams, and clams annually, of which 2,000 tons of oysters are exported to the United States.
An official from South Jeolla Province said, “In preparation for the U.S. FDA inspection, we have conducted management inspections of designated sea areas three times with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Yeosu City, and Goheung-gun, etc.,” and added, “As the safety of the designated sea areas has been recognized, we expect that export routes to the United States will be secured without difficult separate procedures.” Mokpo = Kookmin Ilbo Cookie News Reporter Lee Sang-il silee062@kmib.co.kr

ko-news-notices-262-8372c75064.title: New Port South Container Terminal construction faces prolonged delays
ko-news-notices-262-8372c75064.text:
New Port South Container Terminal construction faces prolonged delays
2022-03-02
Due to the 'sand war' at Busan New Port, the construction of Phase 2-2 of the South Container Terminal continues to be disrupted, but the ordering agency, Busan Regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Office, is responding passively, claiming that since it is not the main process, there will be no disruption to the overall construction period. In particular, if Dado Shipping, a sand extraction transport company, does not collect the quantity originally permitted by the government on the southern coast by July, the permit itself will expire and the sand supply source for the entire new port will disappear, and an uncontrollable sand crisis is expected to be inevitable.
▲Price negotiations are parallel = Daelim Industrial, which is in charge of the construction of Phase 2-2 of the South Container Terminal, and Dado Shipping, a sand mining company, are continuing to discuss the price issue, but have not reached any agreement to date. Daelim Industrial made a construction plan to begin sand reclamation work on December 15th of last year, but has not been able to purchase sand, so it cannot even think about carrying out any other reclamation work other than the SCP construction. Daelim Industrial Manager Ko Gwang-guk said, "When we received the construction order, the sand price was set at around 6,000 won per ㎥, but currently we are unable to accept it as it exceeds 10,000 won. From the 3rd of next month, we will have to secure sand and start construction no matter how expensive the price is."
In addition, Dado Shipping stated that it is impossible to lower the price because it supplied sand to Daewoo Engineering & Construction, which is in charge of the construction of the multi-purpose pier at the new port, and the Gwangyang Port construction site at the same price as Daelim Industrial. Dado's claim is that if only Daelim lowers the price, opposition from other companies is expected due to issues of fairness, and the price cut will lead to damage to small and medium-sized transport companies.
▲ Outlook = There is no suitable way to mediate or resolve the conflict between the two companies waging a sand war. There is a growing possibility that this will lead to a delay in the construction of a new port, a national project, and a weakening of the competitiveness of Busan Port. The Busan Maritime Administration is considering a plan to integrate the first and second reclamation construction sections under the stance that it will not intervene in the price issues of individual companies, but even this will increase the total amount of sand supplied, so it remains unclear whether the construction company will be able to accept it.
There are also concerns about the disappearance of sand mining permits on the southern coast. Due to delays in sand extraction and supply work, Dadohae Shipping received an extension from the Ministry of Construction and Transportation to the sand extraction period in the sea area 50km southeast of Yokjido on the south coast until July. However, the extension of the permit period is limited to one time, and if extraction work is not carried out in the future, there is a possibility that the permit for extraction in Yokjido waters will disappear. If this happens, it is expected that the construction of the new port will be a major setback as it will not be possible to obtain at least 40 million ㎥ of sand needed to build the container terminal and hinterland for the 2-3 and 2-4 sections of the new port, as well as the 2-3 and 2-4 sections that will begin construction in the future.
In relation to this, Cho Jong-hwan, head of the Busan Port Construction Office, said, "Because the sand reclamation work is not a major process that will delay the entire construction period, there will be no major problems with the completion of the pier in 2008."
Reporter Cho Jin-man jmcho@kookje.co.kr

ko-news-notices-261-8372c75064.title: ‘Artificial sea’ for marine experiments completed
ko-news-notices-261-8372c75064.text:
‘Artificial sea’ for marine experiments completed
2022-03-02
In Korea, a world-class marine engineering tank, also known as the 'small sea', has been completed and is beginning full-scale operation.
The Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute announced on the 26th that it held a completion ceremony for the installation of a large controlled towing tank (CPMC) in the marine engineering water tank at the Marine System Safety Research Center in the Daedeok Research Complex in Daejeon and began full-scale operation.
The Ocean Research Institute's Ocean Engineering Water Tank, which has been in operation since 1998, is a comprehensive test facility to simulate the sea conditions of actual sea areas and is 56m long, 30m wide, and 4.5m deep. In addition, it is a high-performance marine engineering research facility equipped with a deep-sea pit facility with a diameter of 5m and a depth of 12m to create a deep sea.
This time, the marine engineering water tank equipped with CPMC facilities has major equipment such as equipment for reproducing irregular waves in various directions, uniform currents, and winds with spectral characteristics, and a wave wave machine capable of vertical movement, and can reproduce various types of waves under almost the same conditions as those in the actual sea.
As a result, the seaworthiness performance of ships, the handling performance of ships and underwater objects, and the transportation, installation, and exercise testing of various marine structures, etc., which were previously performed overseas, can now be carried out domestically, which is expected to contribute to protecting domestic technology and securing the international competitiveness of the shipbuilding and marine industry.
At the event, the director of the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute's Yeomgi University said, "Now that our country has a state-of-the-art marine-related research and experiment facility, it will greatly help in the development of shipbuilding and marine-related technology." Reporter Cho Jin-man

ko-news-notices-260-8372c75064.title: Comprehensive seawater flow observation in the sea area from Yeosu to Mokpo
ko-news-notices-260-8372c75064.text:
Comprehensive seawater flow observation in the sea area from Yeosu to Mokpo
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yu-seop) announced that it will conduct seawater flow observations in the waters around Mokpo in Yeosu from the 21st of this month to the end of October.
For this survey, observation points were selected with advice from about 20 marine-related organizations and 10 university professors, and real-time wide-area sea level observation devices, seabed-mounted floor current meters, and sea level height monitors were mobilized to continuously observe comprehensive seawater flows, including tides, currents, and ocean currents, horizontally and vertically for 7 months.
This sea area is the sea area of ​​Dadohae Maritime National Park, and the flow of sea water due to many islands is complicated and the current speed is strong, causing frequent ship accidents. It is also the source of harmful red tide, causing repeated damage to the surrounding aquaculture industry, so providing sea water flow information is essential.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “Once this observation result is released, it will reveal the complex characteristics of seawater flow and calculate tidal current forecast constants. It is expected to contribute to securing maritime traffic safety and red tide disaster prevention by implementing accurate seawater flow information services for this sea area.”
The seawater flow prediction information service is scheduled to be implemented through the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency website (www.nori.go.kr) starting next year.

ko-news-notices-259-8372c75064.title: Jeju Island's tides disappear
ko-news-notices-259-8372c75064.text:
Jeju Island's tides disappear
2022-03-02
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Jeong Yoo-seop) announced that around April 5, 2006, a no-tide phenomenon with almost no difference between tides would occur in the Jeju region for the first time in 19 years since September 16, 1987.
According to this forecast, the sea level in Jeju on this day is expected to fluctuate by 7cm from 11:44 to 14:34, and by 4cm in Seongsanpo from 10:17 to 13:10, resulting in a phenomenon where the difference in height between high and low tides is almost eliminated compared to the normal level of about 1m.
This is the smallest change since the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency observed that the change in sea level was less than 2 cm for 6 hours and 30 minutes from 0:30 to 07:00 on September 16, 1987 in Jeju.
This phenomenon is because the lunar declination, which is the angle formed between the Earth's equatorial plane and the Moon's orbital plane, is the largest on this day, making the force causing the tides the smallest. It occurs globally every 18.6 years and is expected to appear again around November 2024.

ko-news-notices-258-8372c75064.title: Supreme Court allows Saemangeum project to continue in government victory
ko-news-notices-258-8372c75064.text:
Supreme Court allows Saemangeum project to continue in government victory
2022-03-02
[Edaily Reporter Cho Yong-cheol] Regarding the Saemangeum project, which was a conflict between environmental groups' "tidal flat conservation" and the government's "development of high-quality farmland," the Supreme Court ruled in favor of the government, which said, "Let's block the seawall and create reclaimed land to develop high-quality farmland."
On the 16th, the full court of the Supreme Court confirmed the lower case ruling that the plaintiff lost in the appeal trial of the Saemangeum project plan cancellation claim filed by 3,538 Jeonbuk residents and environmental groups against the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry and North Jeolla Province.
In the ruling, the court said, "Although there are some theories, the basic plan for the Saemangeum project was found to be economically feasible as a result of the economic feasibility analysis by the public-private joint investigation team, so the lower court was justified in ruling that there was no clear evidence to acknowledge the claims of environmental groups and others that it was not economically feasible."
The court explained, “The Saemangeum project is an important task in national management to prepare for changes in domestic and international conditions such as future food crisis and unification of North and South Korea due to increased demand for land, need for alternative development of marginal farmland, and opening of rice imports.”
The court also added, "Environmental groups claim that the government conducted a poor environmental impact assessment while hiding the purpose of the Saemangeum project, but there is a lack of evidence, and the environmental impact assessment was a legal one that came out of a resident opinion collection process in accordance with the law at the time."
Regarding the environmental issue, the court then pointed out, "It is difficult to say that a significant change in circumstances has occurred since the water quality standards for the freshwater lake are expected to be met through a sequential development method that separates the Dongjin Water Area and the Mangyeong Water Area and distributes seawater to the Mangyeong Water Area to gradually desalinate it."
However, Supreme Court Justices Kim Young-ran and Park Si-hwan expressed a dissenting opinion, saying, "The Saemangeum project should be canceled in light of the fact that the need to secure farmland has decreased significantly at the expense of the Saemangeum tidal flat, which is a valuable resource not only for the current generation but also for future generations, and that the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry's environmental impact assessment and economic feasibility review were inadequate or exaggerated."
He added, "It is a request of the times to protect the living environment and natural environment from infringement and damage and to ensure a healthy and comfortable environment for all citizens so that they can lead a decent life."

ko-news-notices-257-8372c75064.title: Tidal benchmark survey begins along the coast from Pyeongtaek to Baengnyeong Island
ko-news-notices-257-8372c75064.text:
Tidal benchmark survey begins along the coast from Pyeongtaek to Baengnyeong Island
2022-03-02
A detailed survey will check whether tidal benchmarks along the coast from Pyeongtaek to Baengnyeong Island remain in place have been lost or have subsided. These benchmarks provide sea level reference heights and require effective management.
The West Sea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Office of the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (Director Chang-seop Choi) announced that it would survey 105 benchmarks at 37 coastal and island locations in two phases: March 15 to April 15 2006 and September 1 to October 30 2006. Missing or damaged benchmarks will be restored and digital levels and GPS instruments will be used to determine their precise elevations and locations.
Tidal benchmarks (TBMs) are important national marine vertical reference points. Following short-term tidal observations in each area benchmarks are installed and their elevations above mean sea level are determined and officially announced. They support decisions on breakwater height and port dredging depth coastal development and sea level monitoring the determination of chart depth reference levels and estimation of inundation levels during coastal surges.
An office representative said that regular surveys of the national marine vertical reference network would continue to manage and maintain these benchmarks effectively. This would help establish reference levels for port and coastal development and improve responses to coastal flooding along the West Coast.

ko-news-notices-256-8372c75064.title: Real-time coastal environmental monitoring system established
ko-news-notices-256-8372c75064.text:
Real-time coastal environmental monitoring system established
2022-03-02
The National Institute of Fisheries Science will hold a meeting at the South Sea Fisheries Research Institute on March 15. About 40 experts representatives of relevant institutions and fishermen will discuss the development and use of a real-time coastal information service.
The system automatically measures water quality in coastal waters and around fishing grounds and sends the observations to a server through a wireless communication network. The resulting database is provided through the institute's Korea Oceanographic Data Center website (http://kodc.nfrdi.re.kr). The institute's ocean research team began the project in 2003 and has installed and operated the system at 22 observation stations.
At locations selected for effective coastal monitoring the system automatically observes water temperature salinity dissolved oxygen and other variables every 30 minutes. Observations are provided online in real time and sent by email to registered users.
By observing multiple waters simultaneously at the desired interval the system provides information on coastal environments that vary greatly in time and space. Real-time information on fishing-ground conditions also enables an effective response on site.
Rapid detection is necessary to respond to sudden changes such as cold-related fish deaths at South Sea coastal farms and hypoxic water masses during high summer temperatures. Interest in the service is increasing along with demand to expand installation and operation beyond the limited waters and fish farms currently covered.
The meeting will gather opinions from relevant institutions and local fishermen and facilitate expert discussion on ways to make the best use of the system. It is expected to contribute to coastal ecosystem protection and improved productivity in coastal fishing grounds.

ko-news-notices-255-8372c75064.title: Real-time provision of Busan North Port weather information
ko-news-notices-255-8372c75064.text:
Real-time provision of Busan North Port weather information
2022-03-02
A marine weather observation system that can determine wind direction in real time will be established in Busan's North Port. This is to prepare for marine disasters such as typhoons and high wave heights.
Busan Port Authority (BPA) announced on the 14th that it plans to install a system by the end of next year that will provide 24-hour monitoring of marine weather conditions at Busan Port to port users, including shipping companies and stevedores. This system will be installed in the form of a light buoy in front of Jodo, the outer port of Busan Port.
For this purpose, BPA has secured a total project cost of 600 million won and plans to begin design services soon after consulting with experts.
Once the system installation is completed, it will be possible to accurately measure the wind direction, wave height, wind speed, and current speed in the North Port, which is expected to greatly contribute to the safe operation of domestic and foreign ships entering and leaving Busan Port.
BPA plans to provide marine weather information obtained through this system to shipping companies and other port users in real time through its website. Currently, marine weather observation facilities are installed in front of the Gwangan Bridge in Busan's North Port to increase its safety, and similar facilities are in operation at the new port.
An official from the Busan Port Authority said, "We are actively promoting the installation of a maritime weather observation system to increase the safety of Busan Port and provide the best service according to port calls by domestic and foreign shipping companies."
International Newspaper/Reporter Jinman Cho

ko-news-notices-254-8372c75064.title: GeoSR featured in Future Competitiveness of Korea Inc
ko-news-notices-254-8372c75064.text:
GeoSR featured in Future Competitiveness of Korea Inc
2022-03-02

ko-news-notices-253-8372c75064.title: Incheon coastal water quality rapidly deteriorates
ko-news-notices-253-8372c75064.text:
Incheon coastal water quality rapidly deteriorates
2022-03-02
The city of Incheon has begun to prepare countermeasures as it has been shown that coastal water quality is deteriorating, with the amount of garbage collected from the coasts of the Incheon region showing an increase.
According to the city on the 21st, over the past four years, COD (chemical oxygen demand) along the coast of Incheon has rapidly worsened from 1.32 mg per liter in 2002 to 1.71 mg in 2004 and 1.69 mg last year.
Last year, the amount of waste collected from the coast was 19,916 tons, a 14.9% increase from 17,330 tons in 2004, and a nearly 2.5-fold increase compared to 7,980 tons in 2002.
By type, mid-layer waste increased more than tenfold, from 380 tons in 2002 to 4,481 tons last year, and coastal trash also increased nearly six-fold, from 2,663 tons to 13,370 tons.
However, during the same period, floating waste in the sea decreased by about half from 1,290 tons to 692 tons, and silted trash also decreased by about a third from 3,647 tons to 1,373 tons.
Accordingly, the city plans to establish comprehensive measures to improve coastal water quality and preserve marine ecosystems and invest a budget of 9.4 billion won this year.
To this end, we plan to spend 24 million won to install a real-time automatic marine water quality environment measurement network in the waters near Palmido Island and establish a pollution monitoring system, and by the end of this year, we plan to invest 1 billion won to install a dedicated incinerator and reducer capable of processing 100 kg of sea waste per hour on Socheong Island and Ganghwa within this year.
In addition, the wetland protection area for 153㎢ of Yeongjong and Yeongheungdo tidal flats will be expanded and designated, and 55.7㎢ of Daeijakdo in Jawol-myeon will be developed as a pilot area for native plant colonies. /Reporter Park In-kwon/Incheon Ilbo

ko-news-notices-252-8372c75064.title: An organization dedicated to marine environment assessment is established.
ko-news-notices-252-8372c75064.text:
An organization dedicated to marine environment assessment is established.
2022-03-02
An organization dedicated to environmental impact assessment of various development projects using the ocean, such as sea aggregate extraction, will be established.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced that in order to systematically manage the impact on the marine environment of continuously increasing marine development activities, the 'Marine Environmental Impact Assessment Center', which will be dedicated to marine environmental impact assessment, was established at the National Institute of Fisheries Science and began operation on the 17th.
In order to ensure professionalism and fairness in the evaluation work, the center has an evaluation deliberation committee and appoints 35 domestic marine environment-related experts from universities, research institutes, and environmental organizations as expert committee members, and divides the center into five subcommittees: water quality environment, sediment environment, forecast reduction, social economy, and marine life.
Accordingly, the marine environment consultation function for the environmental impact assessment and preliminary environmental review conducted by the Ministry of Environment, as well as the analysis and evaluation of the marine environment aspect of marine use and development activities such as marine aggregate extraction, is expected to be strengthened more professionally. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries also plans to systematically strengthen its marine environmental impact assessment capabilities through the development of marine environmental impact assessment report evaluation techniques, development of evaluation guidelines for each type of activity, training of public officials in charge, and database of evaluation data.
Until now, marine environment surveys have been operated dually between the National Institute of Fisheries Science and the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute.
Accordingly, the National Aquatic Research Center was handed over management rights to the automatic marine water quality measurement stations located in eight regions across the country, including Masan Bay on the Nakdong River, which had been operated by the Korea Ocean Research Institute.
However, regarding the unification of the marine environmental impact assessment to the Aquatic Research Center, some in the marine science and industry circles are protesting, saying, "It is unconvincing that the Aquatic Research Institute, which has been in charge of fisheries resources and aquaculture, was made to take full responsibility for marine environmental assessment." Reporter Lee Dong-hyeon / Busan Ilbo

ko-news-notices-251-8372c75064.title: Korean coastal disaster prevention policy introduced overseas
ko-news-notices-251-8372c75064.text:
Korean coastal disaster prevention policy introduced overseas
2022-03-02
Coastal surge warning system selected as an exemplary February policy and featured in an English-language magazine
The Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency's project to establish a warning system to reduce coastal surge damage was a priority task in 2005. It was featured internationally in the February issue of Korea Policy Review an English-language government policy magazine.
The article covers the agency's coastal disaster prevention policy including comprehensive and systematic monitoring of ocean-related natural hazards such as storm surges and tsunamis sharing observational information and promptly assessing and communicating developing situations.
Korea Policy Review (KPR) is published monthly by the Korean Overseas Information Service of the Government Information Agency. It introduces major Korean government policies and developments to specialists worldwide to strengthen international confidence in Korea. The article is available under Multimedia and Magazines at http://www.korea.net.
An agency representative said it would use the coverage as an opportunity to communicate its activities more actively abroad in line with the government's broader international policy outreach.

ko-news-notices-250-8372c75064.title: Starting this year, waterway surveys are mandatory after marine construction is implemented.
ko-news-notices-250-8372c75064.text:
Starting this year, waterway surveys are mandatory after marine construction is implemented.
2022-03-02
Partial amendment to the Waterway Business Act takes effect on January 30
After January 30, various construction works performed in the ocean related to navigational safety of ships must conduct a hydrographic survey at the expense of the construction contractor.
According to the newly revised Waterway Affairs Act, for construction that changes the existing coastline or seabed topography, such as most port construction, seaway dredging, coastal reclamation, sea sand collection, and artificial reef installation, the project owner must conduct a waterway survey directly, and the results of the survey must be submitted to the government for review.
An official from the Korea Ocean Research and Development Institute said, “With this revised law coming into effect, changes in the ocean can be quickly communicated to navigators, contributing to the navigational safety of ships, as well as securing basic information for the government to establish more reasonable coastal management measures based on scientific understanding of unexpected coastal erosion and sedimentation phenomena.”
Meanwhile, the revised Waterway Affairs Act was promulgated on July 29, 2005, and the revision of subordinate laws was passed at the Cabinet meeting on January 24 and came into effect on January 30.

ko-news-notices-249-8372c75064.title: “Introduction of the Total Pollution Control System to the Busan coast”
ko-news-notices-249-8372c75064.text:
“Introduction of the Total Pollution Control System to the Busan coast”
2022-03-02
In order to efficiently manage the water quality of Busan's coastal waters, it was argued that a coastal pollution total management system that can manage the total amount of pollution within the environmental capacity that each sea area can handle should be introduced rather than the currently implemented method of regulating the concentration of pollutants.
This claim was raised in a research report titled ‘Basic Research for Implementation of the Busan Coastal Pollution Control System’ published on the 1st by Baek Gyeong-hoon, associate research fellow at the Busan Development Institute.
According to the research report, it was found that a method of managing the total amount of pollution by dividing the Busan coast into an ecological coast with rich biodiversity and high ecological value, an environmental management coast in need of water quality improvement due to the serious inflow of land-based pollutants into the sea, and a water-friendly coast with excellent scenery and cultural value is more efficient in water quality management. In particular, the Total Pollution Control System is expected to prevent indiscriminate development of coastal areas because it manages the total amount of pollution in the area.
The report stated that as a prerequisite for applying the total pollution load management system, investigation and research on pollutant emissions from marine farms, pollution level and discharge amount from seabed sediments, and pollutant emissions from ships are necessary.
In addition, he added that basic data on the marine environment, such as the use status, geographical location, and flow of currents and ocean currents for sea areas subject to the Total Coastal Pollution Control System, must be accumulated over several years.
Reporter Kim Jong-gyun kjg11@busanilbo.com

ko-news-notices-248-8372c75064.title: Saemangeum seawall closure to be completed in April
ko-news-notices-248-8372c75064.text:
Saemangeum seawall closure to be completed in April
2022-03-02
Water dam construction on the world's longest Saemangeum seawall (33 km), which lasted for 15 years, resumed in March after 2 years and 9 months and will finally be completed in April.
The Saemangeum Project Division of the Korea Rural Community Corporation announced on the 30th, “After preparing earth and stones starting in February, water dam construction to connect all 2.7km of the two unconnected sections will begin on March 24th, and is scheduled to be completed around late April.”
When this section is connected, a 33km seawall connecting Buan, Gimje, and Gunsan in Jeollabuk-do will be created, and within it, 28,300 ha of reclaimed land and 11,800 ha of freshwater lakes, 140 times the area of ​​Yeouido, will be created.
Construction will be carried out in late March, when the amount of seawater flowing in and out of the year is at its lowest, by tearing down the dam and throwing a rock net weighing more than 3 tons into the sea using large barges and trucks. The amount of stone to be used in this construction is 1.17 million ㎥. This is equivalent to 180,000 large dump trucks.
The average forward distance per day is 105m. In the sea, barges dump 600 ㎥ of stones at a time, and on the sea wall, dump trucks ‘advance’ the embankment to a height of 5 m above sea level and a width of 9 m at the top. During the last week, a total of 210 dump trucks, 43 pieces of heavy equipment, and 14 barges will be mobilized. The current speed reaches 6 to 7 meters per second, and gabions that can withstand the rapid current and 3 to 5 tons of rock chunks are continuously injected to create a seawall.
This construction is the final water dam, and paving the road for the public and vehicles is expected to be completed by the end of 2008.
Accordingly, the Saemangeum Project Group decided to hold an on-site briefing session on the overall completion of the construction on the 2nd of next month, with government officials such as Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Park Hong-soo and Rural Development Corporation President Ahn Jong-un in attendance.
The project team said, “Blocking 2.7km requires a high level of technology that is incomparable to the seawall construction that has been built so far,” and added, “We are hoping that foreign experts, including from the Netherlands, will visit to observe this construction, which is said to be a difficult construction project in the architecture and civil engineering fields.”
Meanwhile, the Saemangeum seawall construction, which began in 1991, has been completed for 27.3km. However, due to joint public-private investigations and lawsuits, only reinforcement work has been carried out without progress for 2 years and 7 months. Of the total construction cost of 3.4756 trillion won, the seawall construction cost was 2.1604 trillion won, of which 88% was invested until last year.
Buan = Reporter Kim Yong-kwon ygkim@kmib.co.kr

ko-news-notices-247-8372c75064.title: ‘Tidal Flat Ecosystem’ homepage operation
ko-news-notices-247-8372c75064.text:
‘Tidal Flat Ecosystem’ homepage operation
2022-03-02
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries will begin operating the information website (tidalflat.go.kr) on the tidal flat ecosystem from the 23rd, where you can see the country's major tidal flats at a glance and even have a virtual experience in the tidal flats.
This site contains a variety of information on the definition and types of mudflats, information on famous mudflats and tides at home and abroad, and related international conventions.
In particular, it provides information on five wetland protection areas, including the Muan Tidal Flat, which is a mudflat ecosystem conservation area, and four ecosystem conservation areas, including the Sinduri Dune Sea Ecosystem Conservation Area, and operates a mudflat information center such as a mudflat virtual experience, a dictionary of marine terms, and an open plaza. Reporter Lee Dong-hyeon, Busan Ilbo / Entry time: 2006. 01.23. 11:03

ko-news-notices-246-8372c75064.title: Promotion of ‘underwater park’ off Dadaepo
ko-news-notices-246-8372c75064.text:
Promotion of ‘underwater park’ off Dadaepo
2022-03-02
A project to create the country's first 'underwater park' where you can enjoy the 'undersea world' is being promoted off the coast of Busan.
On the 25th, Busan City announced that it has decided to build a 7,000-hectare 'underwater fish park' in the waters around Namu Island and Hyeongje Island, southeast of Dadaepo Port, Saha-gu, Busan, and plans to secure 100 million won in municipal funds to begin services to establish a basic plan in February.
Through this service, the city plans to draw up a rough outline of the underwater park's location, direction, construction costs, and installation facilities, and then decide whether to pursue the project in earnest. If the results of the service are released at the end of this year and the project gets back on track as scheduled, construction of the park is expected to be completed around 2010.
In the underwater park, we plan to build a fish farm with artificial reefs and allow people to enjoy a variety of fish and the underwater environment through skin scuba diving, snorkeling, an underwater observatory, and glass boats. In addition, plans to build an ocean observatory and fishing spot on Namu Island are also being considered.
An official from Busan City said, "As Busan City aims to become a marine tourism city, we are promoting an eco-friendly underwater park with the aim of providing things to see and enjoy using the underwater world." Reporter Youngshin Son zero@

ko-news-notices-245-8372c75064.title: ‘Seogwipo Tourism Port’ is promoted
ko-news-notices-245-8372c75064.text:
‘Seogwipo Tourism Port’ is promoted
2022-03-02
The ‘Seogwipo Tourist Port’ development project, one of the seven leading projects of Jeju Free International City, will be promoted by developing the sea 400m east of the original planned site. ‘Wellbeing Theme Town’, which is known to replace ‘Seogwipo Tourist Port’, is being promoted separately as a follow-up project to the 7 leading projects. The Yerae-dong recreational residential complex in Seogwipo will begin infrastructure construction in the second half of this year, and the Jeju High-Tech Science and Technology Complex will begin sales around May. Let’s find out how the seven leading projects are being materialized.
◆Tourism beauty port and wellness theme town
According to Seogwipo City and the Jeju Free International City Development Center on the 25th, the Seogwipo Tourist Port development project was in danger of being ‘failed’ as changes to the status quo were not permitted by the Cultural Heritage Administration due to concerns that it would affect the soft coral colonies living in the waters outside Seogwipo Port and the habitat of green eel downstream of Cheonjiyeon Falls. It was known that the development center's plan was to create a 'well-being theme town' in Seogwipo City in case the 'tourism beauty port' was canceled.
However, it is known that Seogwipo City and the Development Center are discussing a decision to move forward with the tourism port project by changing its location. Initially, it was considered difficult to create a landfill by reclaiming the Jaguri Coast, so plans are being reviewed to create a marine leisure tourism town with 30,000 to 80,000 ton cruise ship berthing facilities, mooring facilities with marina facilities, water leisure facilities, and a visitor center on an area of ​​64,000 pyeong, 400 meters east of the Jaguri Coast. In this case, the position of Seogwipo City and the Development Center is that environmental damage can be minimized and development is possible.
Therefore, the ‘Wellbeing Theme Town’, which has been promoted since 2004, is promoted completely separately from tourism. Initially, the development center was promoted as a ‘health and beauty town’, but expanded into a ‘well-being theme town’ equipped with professional education institutions, specialized nursing facilities for the elderly, and alternative medicine treatment facilities. It is unclear whether the Well-being Theme Town will be built in downtown Seogwipo as it is not a replacement project for the ‘tourism beauty port’. Areas such as mid-mountainous areas, hot springs, and coastal areas are being considered.
◆High-tech science complex scheduled to be sold around May
The recreational residential complex, which received development project implementation approval and implementation plan approval in October last year, is expected to begin construction after the detailed design service results are released at the end of August. Currently, consent for sale has been secured for 71% of all landowners, and land compensation work is progressing relatively smoothly.
In the case of Jeju High-Tech Science Complex, land compensation, which was the most difficult task, was completed in December last year, and sales are scheduled to begin around May. The Jeju High-Tech Science Complex is attracting the attention of companies in Seoul and other metropolitan areas with groundbreaking incentives such as a 100% reduction in corporate tax for three years and a 50% reduction in property tax and comprehensive land tax for five years for companies moving into the complex. A land purchase contract for 70% of the total area of ​​Shinhwa Historical Park has also been signed, and the development project is expected to be approved this year.
◆Shopping outlets are expected to perform poorly
Three projects, including Jeju High-Tech Science Complex, Yerae-dong Recreational Residential Complex, and Shinhwa History Park, are ‘on track’, but it is unclear whether ‘Shopping Outlet’, ‘Seogwipo Tourist Port’, ‘Expansion of Jungmun Complex’, and ‘Designation of Jeju Airport Free Trade Zone’ can be promoted as originally planned. The designation of Jeju Airport as a free trade zone was canceled at the end of last year.
Jin Cheol-hoon, chairman of the Jeju Free International City Development Center, said, “This year, we will focus our capabilities on three key projects, including the high-tech science and technology complex, the recreational residential complex, and the Shinhwa Historical Park.” He added, “In particular, in celebration of the 2006 Visit Jeju Year, we will also strengthen promotion and marketing of Jeju development projects and do our best to attract domestic and foreign investors.”
Reporter Lim Hyeong-gyun hyim@chosun.com

ko-news-notices-244-8372c75064.title: Sihwa Lake flows again through the 4th main stream.
ko-news-notices-244-8372c75064.text:
Sihwa Lake flows again through the 4th main stream.
2022-03-02
The water quality of the 4th main stream, one of the worst sources of pollution in Sihwa Lake, has been improved, allowing water from this place to flow back into Sihwa Lake after two years.
The Sihwa Regional Sustainable Development Council announced on the 18th that the water quality of the 4th Gansu River has fallen below COD (biochemical oxygen demand) of 20 ppm since the second half of last year and has been maintained steadily for more than six months.
This is about 1/100th lower than the 1,970ppm in March 2004, and meets the legal standard of 40ppm.
Accordingly, the Sihwa Sustainable Development Association decided to dismantle the 40m-long weir installed on the 4th main channel and hold a water supply ceremony to connect it to Sihwa Lake at the northern tidal flat at around 1pm on the 19th.
After the water quality of the 4th main channel was confirmed to be the worst in early 2004, a weir was installed along with the 1st main channel to prevent it from flowing into Sihwa Lake, and the water has been purified at the Sihwa Sewage Treatment Plant through a collection pipe facility.
Starting this year, the Sihwa Sustainable Development Association has decided to gradually expand water quality improvement activities for the 1st trunk channel, where a weir is installed, as well as the 2nd and 3rd trunk channel.
An official from the City Council for Sustainable Development said, “Over the past two years, we have monitored the water quality of 13 stormwater pipes connected to the 4th main waterway every day, fixed 64 incorrectly connected sewer pipes, and achieved improvement results through continuous crackdown on companies and education promotion.”
The Sihwa Sustainable Development Association was formed in February 2004 as a public-private consultative body with the participation of the Ministry of Construction and Transportation, local governments, local civic groups, residents, experts, and Korea Water Resources Corporation, and has been carrying out activities such as improving water quality in the 4th Main Waterway, the most polluted of the 4 main waterways, and establishing a comprehensive development plan for the Sihwa District./Siheung = Reporter Kim Shin-seop (blog) skim

ko-news-notices-243-8372c75064.title: Yangyang Jeongam Beach is a gravel beach.
ko-news-notices-243-8372c75064.text:
Yangyang Jeongam Beach is a gravel beach.
2022-03-02
Jeongam Beach in Ganghyeon-myeon, Yangyang-gun continued to have its white sand washed away for a long period of time, turning it into a gravel field.
In particular, the clavicle (sand sweep) phenomenon at Jeongam Beach has been going on for a long time over the past 10 years. During this period, all of the 1m high white sand beach has disappeared and the pebbles buried underneath have been revealed, making it unclear whether the beach will operate this year.
In addition, the phenomenon of sand washing, which was limited to some sections, has recently expanded to the entire section of the beach, revealing a gravel field spanning 1 km, and it is pointed out that countermeasures are urgently needed.
Residents said, "All the sand on Jeongam Beach's white sand has disappeared and turned into a gravel field, raising doubts as to whether the beach can be operated this summer." They added, "Measures are needed for the clavicle phenomenon as well as coastal erosion in the east coast area."
Accordingly, Yangyang-gun plans to temporarily store sand generated during the dredging of the nearby Jeonjeon Port and temporarily restore the beach during the summer, but it has been revealed that not only is the pouring sand continuing to be swept away by waves, but no measures have been taken to fundamentally prevent sand washing.
An official from Yangyang-gun said, "It is presumed that the sand washing phenomenon at Jeongam Beach was caused by the influence of artificial structures such as breakwaters or the impediment of the flow of sea breeze due to large buildings built on the coast," and added, "We plan to prepare and implement long-term measures against the clavicle phenomenon, including coastal erosion."
Yangyang/Namjincheon

ko-news-notices-242-8372c75064.title: [Ocean Observation] Announcement of the Byeongsul Year East Sea Marine Survey Project
ko-news-notices-242-8372c75064.text:
[Ocean Observation] Announcement of the Byeongsul Year East Sea Marine Survey Project
2022-03-02
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency East Sea Oceanographic Survey Office (Director Kim Jeong-gi) announced the 2006 oceanographic survey project for Korea's East Sea.
The main projects in 2006 were ▲tide observation to observe the height and low of sea level at 6 locations along the East Sea coast, ▲tidal-current observation near Sokcho Port, ▲Korean coastal current survey in the East Sea, Jukbyeon, and Hupo, ▲Tidal Bench Mark survey on the East Sea coast, ▲short-term tidal observation to verify vertical standards in Jumunjin and Ganggu. We plan to conduct marine surveys and observations, including ▲hydrographic survey of the southern part of Jukbyeon Port, coastal route survey of 44 ports including Ulsan Port, and ▲marine characteristics survey of anchorage sites at Donghae Port.
In particular, as the 1st National Marine Sports Festival hosted by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries this August has been decided to be held in Uljin-gun, Gyeongsangbuk-do, we plan to conduct seawater flow observations during the competition period and provide real-time data on the direction and speed of seawater flow to competition officials and athletes. We plan to promote marine research projects centered on local communities and consumers.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, “Various observed data are analyzed and processed and provided quickly through the website (www.nori.go.kr), and are quickly reflected in the publication of hydrographic books such as charts, so it is expected to be greatly used for safe ship operation, port construction, understanding of the marine environment, as well as disaster prevention work support and fishing activities.”

ko-news-notices-241-8372c75064.title: Ministry develops an integrated port construction information system
ko-news-notices-241-8372c75064.text:
Ministry develops an integrated port construction information system
2022-03-02
Port construction information system to improve transparency
Online planning design construction and supervision
The integrated Port Construction Information System (PortCIS) is expected to improve transparency and fairness throughout port construction by digitizing project information.
The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries announced on the 17th that development would begin that year. Clients designers contractors and other project participants would exchange and share all documents and drawings generated throughout the project life cycle from planning and design through construction supervision and maintenance.
Its main functions include project management for port master plans budgets contracts and completion of construction and consulting services; construction management for schedules and progress payments; and preparation and management of documents and drawings transmitted online.
It also provides status reports and statistics on project implementation using search criteria and a document search for design documents associated with port construction and consulting services.
Digitizing information previously exchanged by hand or post will allow it to be shared online. This will help prevent damage to or loss of valuable drawings and make storage and retrieval easier.
Sharing and reusing information and reducing transmission and storage costs are expected to improve productivity. Disclosure of information will also support fairness and transparency in construction.
The ministry plans to establish or revise relevant rules including operating regulations and provide training and publicity to encourage efficient operation and early adoption.

ko-news-notices-240-8372c75064.title: [Goseong] “Goseong-gun’s own initiative to promote deep ocean water”
ko-news-notices-240-8372c75064.text:
[Goseong] “Goseong-gun’s own initiative to promote deep ocean water”
2022-03-02
The Goseong County Council urged Goseong County to pursue the creation of a deep ocean water industrialization complex as its own project.
At the 152nd administrative audit evaluation on the 23rd, the Goseong County Council pointed out that the provincial government intervened in the deep ocean water project jointly promoted by Goseong County and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries under the pretext of attracting foreign investment, and that the industrialization complex development project was wasted for over two years without any results.
In particular, he criticized the province for wasting time and budget by using foreign companies with unproven business capabilities as well as capital power, such as IBM and Arcadia, as business partners in order to attract foreign investment, but was unable to offer any apology or alternative.
The county council urged Goseong-gun to become the sole developer of the deep ocean water industrialization project and actively attract domestic private investors, invalidate the agreement between the province and the province itself, and strongly demand compensation for damages caused by the delay in the project.
In addition, in order to revitalize the marine bio industry using deep ocean water, the government actively promoted the creation of industrial complexes, job creation, and increased military taxation, and established a detailed and feasible comprehensive tourism development plan linked to Mt. Geumgang tourism. <Reporter Lee Jeong-yeon, kwlee@kwnews.co.kr>

ko-news-notices-239-8372c75064.title: Production of 3D video footage of the East Sea
ko-news-notices-239-8372c75064.text:
Production of 3D video footage of the East Sea
2022-03-02
It is expected that the underwater appearance of the East Sea and the surrounding waters of Dokdo will be produced as a 3D video, helping to understand the seabed of the East Coast.
According to the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency on the 23rd, it recently completed a project to produce 3D images of the underwater scenery of the East Sea and the waters around Dokdo, with a project cost of 100 million won, starting last April.
This project, which was carried out over 99,000㎢ of the East Sea area, is evaluated as having identified the shape of the seabed in the East Sea and Dokdo by producing videos of the shape of the seafloor for major trade ports, including waters under Korea's jurisdiction.
The production of this 3D video involved precise surveying using cutting-edge marine survey equipment, such as the navigation satellite system (DGPS), in the East Sea area for two years since 1996 to produce the National Marine Basic Map.
In addition, this video production will be used as basic data in assigning names of East Sea submarine names announced by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries Marine Geographical Names Committee, and discussions are underway with the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development so that it can be included in elementary, middle, and high school textbooks.
An official from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency said, "This video production will help us understand the East Sea and Dokdo and can be used as information to clarify our position to the outside world. It will also contribute to raising public awareness of the ocean as it will allow us to see the shape of the seafloor easily and in detail."
Donghae/Hong Seong-bae sbhong@kado.net

ko-news-notices-238-8372c75064.title: Yeongheung-Seonjaedo tidal flat wetland protection area
ko-news-notices-238-8372c75064.text:
Yeongheung-Seonjaedo tidal flat wetland protection area
2022-03-02
[Seoul Newspaper] 49.4㎢ of mudflats around Yeongheung and Seonjae Island in Ongjin-gun, Incheon, whose designation as a wetland protection area was canceled due to opposition from residents, will be designated as a wetland protection area within this month.
Incheon City announced on the 9th that the mudflats along the coasts of Yeongheung and Seonjae Island, excluding Janggyeong-ni and Simnipo beaches, festival fish farms, and youth marine training centers, will be designated as wetland protection areas by the end of the month.
It appears that it will be possible to install infrastructure for fishing activities in the mudflats here, such as a fishing farm access road and a storage yard.
The exclusion of four areas from wetland protection areas and the ability to install infrastructure is the result of the city and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries accepting the demands of Yeongheung and Seonjae Island residents.
In November 2003, the city requested the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries to designate the Yeongheung and Seonjaedo tidal flats as wetland protection zones, but the request was canceled due to opposition from residents.
Based on this designation plan, the city held the final public hearing for residents at the Ongjin County Office conference room on this day.
Incheon Reporter Kim Hak-jun

ko-news-notices-237-8372c75064.title: Prevent Pohang’s ‘sea desertification’ with seaweed
ko-news-notices-237-8372c75064.text:
Prevent Pohang’s ‘sea desertification’ with seaweed
2022-03-02
Pohang City, Gyeongsangbuk-do, is attracting attention by carrying out an afforestation project to create a forest with seaweed to eliminate the phenomenon of coastal greening that is devastating coastal fishing grounds.
The phenomenon of sea greening is similar to land desertification, where the surface of rocks in the sea turns white due to changes in the marine environment, and is fatal to the habitat of fish, including sea urchins, abalone, and sea cucumbers.
Since the 1980s, when steel complexes and coastal tourism and entertainment complexes were indiscriminately built around the east coast of Gyeongbuk, a huge amount of wastewater has flowed into the sea, becoming the main culprit in ruining fishing grounds.
Planted plants are rectangular concrete or steel structures measuring 3m in length and width that are dropped into the center of a rocky area in the sea whose color has faded to white and left to sink. The purpose of the plantation plant drop project is that when seaweed seeds such as seaweed and kelp take root on the surface of the sunken plantation plant, it will grow lush like a forest on land, making it easier for marine life to inhabit.
The seaweed forest created with plantation grass is mainly used as a spawning ground for fish during the spawning season or as an excellent breeding ground for young fish and shellfish, which is very effective in protecting and nurturing marine life.
Although the area of ​​the coastal village's coastal fishing grounds is 3,070 ha, Pohang City, which has been experiencing difficulties due to a decrease in catch and harvest, judged the greening of the seashore to be the main cause of the decline in fishermen's income.
For the first time this year, Pohang City, which spent 140 million won on a pilot basis to distribute afforestation to five fishing grounds, including the coastal fishing grounds in Jigyeong-ri, Songra-myeon, Buk-gu, saw a great effect on the spawning and proliferation of fish and shellfish, according to an effectiveness survey conducted by the East Sea Fisheries Research Institute.
Pohang City plans to spend 600 million won next year to designate three areas where coastal greening occurs on the east coast, plant about 200 plants, and then begin full-scale restoration of the marine ecosystem as an annual project.
“The marine ecosystem devastated by coastal greening will be completely restored after 2008, when a seaweed forest will be created around the plantation plants that have been submerged in water starting early next year,” said Oh Yeong-seok, a fishery resource manager at the Fisheries Department of Pohang City.
Pohang = Reporter Kim Sangjo sangjo@kmib.co.kr

ko-news-notices-236-8372c75064.title: [Goseong] Laying the foundation for deep water business
ko-news-notices-236-8372c75064.text:
[Goseong] Laying the foundation for deep water business
2022-03-02
The nation's first institute to conduct full-scale research on developed deep ocean water will be established in Goseong-gun.　Goseong-gun announced that it will open the Deep Ocean Water Research Center, which has been jointly promoted with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, on the 21st and begin full-scale test research.
According to the military, the Deep Ocean Water Research Center spent a total of 13.9 billion won to build a research complex including a research and development building and a fisheries experiment building in Ohori, Jukwang-myeon, and has a deep water intake capacity of 1,000 tons per day on average.
At the opening and water intake ceremony on this day, Goseong-gun and the Korea Ocean Research Institute signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on the establishment and operation of a research center to commercialize deep water and revitalize research.
In particular, eight companies for joint research on commercialization of deep ocean water will move into the research center and begin full-scale prototype development.
The companies participating in this study include 8 products from 8 companies, including Kooksoondang's soju, Aekyung Industrial cosmetics, Sempio Foods sauce, Dongwon FB green tea beverage, Hyeonnae Pharmaceutical Industry's ionic beverage, Gangneung Chodang tofu, Doosan Cheongju, and Daehakchon fermented beverage.
An official from Goseong-gun said, “Although construction of the water intake pipe was started a little late, it proceeded smoothly due to good weather, and the deep water development project was promoted as planned.” He added, “It is expected to be a new breakthrough not only in revitalizing the deep ocean water industry but also in reviving the stagnant local economy.” <Reporter Lee Jeong-jeong, kwlee@kwnews.co.kr>

ko-news-notices-235-8372c75064.title: Saving the white sand of Gusan Beach
ko-news-notices-235-8372c75064.text:
Saving the white sand of Gusan Beach
2022-03-02
An artificial reef to prevent coastal erosion will be installed at Gusan Beach in Uljin.
The Pohang Regional Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Office (Director Kim Jong-sook) announced on the 6th that it will install an artificial reef, an underwater breakwater, at Gusan-ri Beach in Giseong-myeon, Uljin-gun, next year for the first time in Korea to prevent coastal erosion and protect the coastal environment at a project cost of 7 billion won.
At Gusan-ri Beach, the width of the white sand beach has decreased as the white sand beach has been continuously lost due to abnormal fluctuations in ocean currents, and when typhoons arrive, high waves are causing great damage to facilities around the beach, so active prevention measures were needed.
Accordingly, the Pohang Maritime Administration decided to introduce and install an artificial reef, an underwater structure used in developed countries, for the first time in Korea.
An artificial reef is an eco-friendly structure that secures views by installing a structure under the water, does not have to damage the existing coastal scenery, and can also function as a reef for sea creatures. It can prevent coastal erosion and reduce damage to the coastal area during typhoons.
An official from the Pohang Maritime Administration said, “This project is the first of its kind in Korea, and it is expected to contribute to revitalizing the local economy by maintaining its function as a marine tourist destination and preserving the national territory, as well as increasing the number of tourists by expanding the white sand beach of Gusan-ri Beach on the east coast.”

ko-news-notices-234-8372c75064.title: From “embankment construction” to “nature-friendly” Netherlands
ko-news-notices-234-8372c75064.text:
From “embankment construction” to “nature-friendly” Netherlands
2022-03-02
(Seoul = Yonhap News) Reporter Kim Se-jin = For the past hundreds of years, there has been a war to secure territory against water.
The Netherlands, which has suffered a lot, is showing signs of giving up its hard-line policy, represented by the construction of embankments, and changing its flood control strategy to a moderate policy of being friendly to nature.
Increasingly predictable to what extent natural disasters will increase due to global warming.
The urgency to prepare for the ‘worst case situation’ amidst difficult times has led to the Netherlands’ water crisis.
This is a result of aggravating the need to change the idea of life.
As part of this effort, the International Herald Tribune (IHT) reported on the 6th that the Dutch government
is purchasing millions of square meters of farmland and factory land near major canals.
